decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn
decls.sig: def AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (f : ℝ → ℝ) (s : Set ℝ) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is **absolutely monotone on a set `s`** if, heuristically, all iterated derivatives of `f` on `s` are nonnegative. For technical reasons related to unique differentiability, the precise definition is phrased as the existence of a Taylor series for `f` on `s` whose `n`th term,

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.contDiffOn
decls.sig: theorem contDiffOn (hf : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s) : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f s
decls.doc: An absolutely monotone function on `s` is `C^∞` on `s`.

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.of_contDiff
decls.sig: theorem of_contDiff (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv n f x) : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s
decls.doc: A globally `C^∞` function whose iterated derivatives are nonnegative on `s` is absolutely monotone on `s`. The set `s` need *not* satisfy `UniqueDiffOn`.

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg (hf : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s) (hs : UniqueDiffOn ℝ s) (n : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ s) : 0 ≤ iteratedDerivWithin n f s x
decls.doc: Under `UniqueDiffOn`, a Taylor witness for an absolutely monotone function agrees with `iteratedDerivWithin`, so the latter is nonnegative on `s`.

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.iff_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem iff_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg (hs : UniqueDiffOn ℝ s) : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s ↔ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f s ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ iteratedDerivWithin n f s x
decls.doc: Under `UniqueDiffOn`, a function is absolutely monotone on `s` iff it is `C^∞` on `s` with every iterated derivative within `s` nonnegative.

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.add
decls.sig: theorem add (hf : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s) (hg : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn g s) : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (f + g) s
decls.doc: The sum of two absolutely monotone functions is absolutely monotone.

decls.name: AbsolutelyMonotoneOn.smul
decls.sig: theorem smul {c : ℝ} (hf : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn f s) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (c • f) s
decls.doc: A nonnegative scalar multiple of an absolutely monotone function is absolutely monotone.

decls.name: exists_hasDerivWithinAt_eq_of_gt_of_lt
decls.sig: theorem exists_hasDerivWithinAt_eq_of_gt_of_lt (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Icc a b) x) {m : ℝ} (hma : f' a < m) (hmb : m < f' b) : m ∈ f' '' Ioo a b
decls.doc: **Darboux's theorem**: if `a ≤ b` and `f' a < m < f' b`, then `f' c = m` for some `c ∈ (a, b)`.

decls.name: exists_hasDerivWithinAt_eq_of_lt_of_gt

decls.doc: **Darboux's theorem**: if `a ≤ b` and `f' b < m < f' a`, then `f' c = m` for some `c ∈ (a, b)`.

decls.name: logDeriv
decls.sig: def logDeriv (f : 𝕜 → 𝕜')
decls.doc: The logarithmic derivative of a function defined as `deriv f /f`. Note that it will be zero at `x` if `f` is not DifferentiableAt `x`.

decls.name: logDeriv_apply
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_apply (f : 𝕜 → 𝕜') (x : 𝕜) : logDeriv f x = deriv f x / f x

decls.name: logDeriv_eq_zero_of_not_differentiableAt
decls.sig: lemma logDeriv_eq_zero_of_not_differentiableAt (f : 𝕜 → 𝕜') (x : 𝕜) (h : ¬DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) : logDeriv f x = 0

decls.name: logDeriv_congr_nhds
decls.sig: lemma logDeriv_congr_nhds {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g) : logDeriv f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] logDeriv g
decls.doc: If two functions agree in a neighborhood of `x`, then so do their logarithmic derivatives.

decls.name: logDeriv_congr_nhdsNE
decls.sig: lemma logDeriv_congr_nhdsNE {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] g) : logDeriv f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] x] logDeriv g
decls.doc: If two functions agree in a punctured neighborhood of `x`, then so do their logarithmic derivatives.

decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_congr_codiscreteWithin {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {U : Set 𝕜} (hU : IsOpen U) (h : f =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U] g) : logDeriv f =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U] logDeriv g
decls.doc: If two functions agree on a codiscrete subset of an open set `U`, then so do their logarithmic derivatives.

decls.name: logDeriv_congr_codiscrete
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_congr_codiscrete {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} (h : f =ᶠ[codiscrete 𝕜] g) : logDeriv f =ᶠ[codiscrete 𝕜] logDeriv g
decls.doc: If two functions agree on a codiscrete subset of `𝕜`, then so do their logarithmic derivatives.

decls.name: logDeriv_id
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_id (x : 𝕜) : logDeriv id x = 1 / x

decls.name: logDeriv_id'
decls.sig: @[simp] theorem logDeriv_id' (x : 𝕜) : logDeriv (·) x = 1 / x

decls.name: logDeriv_const
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_const (a : 𝕜') : logDeriv (fun _ : 𝕜 ↦ a) = 0

decls.name: logDeriv_mul
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} (x : 𝕜) (hf : f x ≠ 0) (hg : g x ≠ 0) (hdf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) (hdg : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 g x) : logDeriv (f * g) x = logDeriv f x + logDeriv g x

decls.name: logDeriv_div
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_div {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} (x : 𝕜) (hf : f x ≠ 0) (hg : g x ≠ 0) (hdf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) (hdg : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 g x) : logDeriv (f / g) x = logDeriv f x - logDeriv g x

decls.name: logDeriv_mul_const
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_mul_const {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} (x : 𝕜) (a : 𝕜') (ha : a ≠ 0) : logDeriv (fun z => f z * a) x = logDeriv f x

decls.name: logDeriv_const_mul

decls.name: logDeriv_prod
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_prod {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, f i x ≠ 0) (hd : ∀ i ∈ s, DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (f i) x) : logDeriv (∏ i ∈ s, f i) x = ∑ i ∈ s, logDeriv (f i) x

decls.name: logDeriv_fun_zpow
decls.sig: lemma logDeriv_fun_zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (hdf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) (n : ℤ) : logDeriv (f · ^ n) x = n * logDeriv f x

decls.name: logDeriv_zpow

decls.name: logDeriv_pow
decls.sig: lemma logDeriv_pow (x : 𝕜) (n : ℕ) : logDeriv (· ^ n) x = n / x

decls.name: logDeriv_inv
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma logDeriv_inv (x : 𝕜) : logDeriv (·⁻¹) x = -1 / x

decls.name: logDeriv_comp
decls.sig: theorem logDeriv_comp {f : 𝕜' → 𝕜'} {g : 𝕜 → 𝕜'} {x : 𝕜} (hf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜' f (g x)) (hg : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 g x) : logDeriv (f ∘ g) x = logDeriv f (g x) * deriv g x

decls.name: logDeriv_neg

decls.name: logDeriv_comp_neg

decls.name: HasDerivAtFilter
decls.sig: def HasDerivAtFilter (f : 𝕜 → F) (f' : F) (L : Filter (𝕜 × 𝕜))
decls.doc: `f` has the derivative `f'` along the filter `L`. That is, `f x' = f x + (x' - x) • f' + o(x' - x)` where `(x', x)` converges along the filter `L`.

decls.name: HasDerivWithinAt
decls.sig: def HasDerivWithinAt (f : 𝕜 → F) (f' : F) (s : Set 𝕜) (x : 𝕜)
decls.doc: `f` has the derivative `f'` at the point `x` within the subset `s`. That is, `f x' = f x + (x' - x) • f' + o(x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x` inside `s`.

decls.name: HasDerivAt
decls.sig: def HasDerivAt (f : 𝕜 → F) (f' : F) (x : 𝕜)
decls.doc: `f` has the derivative `f'` at the point `x`. That is, `f x' = f x + (x' - x) • f' + o(x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x`.

decls.name: HasStrictDerivAt
decls.sig: def HasStrictDerivAt (f : 𝕜 → F) (f' : F) (x : 𝕜)
decls.doc: `f` has the derivative `f'` at the point `x` in the sense of strict differentiability. That is, `f y - f z = (y - z) • f' + o(y - z)` as `y, z → x`.

decls.name: derivWithin
decls.sig: def derivWithin (f : 𝕜 → F) (s : Set 𝕜) (x : 𝕜)
decls.doc: Derivative of `f` at the point `x` within the set `s`, if it exists. Zero otherwise. If the derivative exists (i.e., `∃ f', HasDerivWithinAt f f' s x`), then `f x' = f x + (x' - x) • derivWithin f s x + o(x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x` inside `s`.

decls.name: deriv
decls.sig: def deriv (f : 𝕜 → F) (x : 𝕜)
decls.doc: Derivative of `f` at the point `x`, if it exists. Zero otherwise. If the derivative exists (i.e., `∃ f', HasDerivAt f f' x`), then `f x' = f x + (x' - x) • deriv f x + o(x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x`.

decls.name: HasFDerivAt.le_of_lip'
decls.sig: theorem HasFDerivAt.le_of_lip' {f : E → F} {f' : E →L[𝕜] F} {x₀ : E} (hf : HasFDerivAt f f' x₀) {C : ℝ} (hC₀ : 0 ≤ C) (hlip : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, ‖f x - f x₀‖ ≤ C * ‖x - x₀‖) : ‖f'‖ ≤ C

This definition is designed to be specialized - for `L = 𝓝 (x, x)` (in `HasStrictFDerivAt`), giving rise to the deriv

decls.name: HasFDerivWithinAt
decls.sig: def HasFDerivWithinAt (f : E → F) (f' : E →L[𝕜] F) (s : Set E) (x : E)
decls.doc: A function `f` has the continuous linear map `f'` as derivative at `x` within a set `s` if `f x' = f x + f' (x' - x) + o (x' - x)` when `x'` tends to `x` inside `s`.

decls.name: HasFDerivAt
decls.sig: def HasFDerivAt (f : E → F) (f' : E →L[𝕜] F) (x : E)
decls.doc: A function `f` has the continuous linear map `f'` as derivative at `x` if `f x' = f x + f' (x' - x) + o (x' - x)` when `x'` tends to `x`.

decls.name: HasStrictFDerivAt
decls.sig: def HasStrictFDerivAt (f : E → F) (f' : E →L[𝕜] F) (x : E)
decls.doc: A function `f` has derivative `f'` at `a` in the sense of *strict differentiability* if `f x - f y - f' (x - y) = o(x - y)` as `x, y → a`. This form of differentiability is required, e.g., by the inverse function theorem. Any `C^1` function on a vector space over `ℝ` is strictly differentiable but t

decls.name: DifferentiableWithinAt
decls.sig: def DifferentiableWithinAt (f : E → F) (s : Set E) (x : E)
decls.doc: A function `f` is differentiable at a point `x` within a set `s` if it admits a derivative there (possibly non-unique).

decls.name: DifferentiableAt
decls.sig: def DifferentiableAt (f : E → F) (x : E)
decls.doc: A function `f` is differentiable at a point `x` if it admits a derivative there (possibly non-unique).

decls.name: fderivWithin
decls.sig: irreducible_def fderivWithin (f : E → F) (s : Set E) (x : E) : E →L[𝕜] F
decls.doc: If `f` has a derivative at `x` within `s`, then `fderivWithin 𝕜 f s x` is such a derivative. Otherwise, it is set to `0`. We also set it to be zero, if zero is one of possible derivatives.

decls.name: fderiv
decls.sig: irreducible_def fderiv (f : E → F) (x : E) : E →L[𝕜] F
decls.doc: If `f` has a derivative at `x`, then `fderiv 𝕜 f x` is such a derivative. Otherwise, it is set to `0`.

decls.name: DifferentiableOn
decls.sig: def DifferentiableOn (f : E → F) (s : Set E)
decls.doc: `DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s` means that `f` is differentiable within `s` at any point of `s`.

decls.name: Differentiable
decls.sig: def Differentiable (f : E → F)
decls.doc: `Differentiable 𝕜 f` means that `f` is differentiable at any point.

decls.name: fderivWithin_comp_smul

decls.name: fderiv_comp_smul

decls.name: hasFDerivWithinAt_closure_of_tendsto_fderiv
decls.sig: theorem hasFDerivWithinAt_closure_of_tendsto_fderiv {f : E → F} {s : Set E} {x : E} {f' : E →L[ℝ] F} (f_diff : DifferentiableOn ℝ f s) (s_conv : Convex ℝ s) (s_open : IsOpen s) (f_cont : ∀ y ∈ closure s, ContinuousWithinAt f s y) (h : Tendsto (fun y => fderiv ℝ f y) (𝓝[s] x) (𝓝 f')) : HasFDerivWithinAt f f' (closure s) x
decls.doc: If a function `f` is differentiable in a convex open set and continuous on its closure, and its derivative converges to a limit `f'` at a point on the boundary, then `f` is differentiable there with derivative `f'`.

decls.name: hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv
decls.sig: theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv {s : Set ℝ} {e : E} {a : ℝ} {f : ℝ → E} (f_diff : DifferentiableOn ℝ f s) (f_lim : ContinuousWithinAt f s a) (hs : s ∈ 𝓝[>] a) (f_lim' : Tendsto (fun x => deriv f x) (𝓝[>] a) (𝓝 e)) : HasDerivWithinAt f e (Ici a) a
decls.doc: If a function is differentiable on the right of a point `a : ℝ`, continuous at `a`, and its derivative also converges at `a`, then `f` is differentiable on the right at `a`.

decls.name: hasDerivWithinAt_Iic_of_tendsto_deriv
decls.sig: theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Iic_of_tendsto_deriv {s : Set ℝ} {e : E} {a : ℝ} {f : ℝ → E} (f_diff : DifferentiableOn ℝ f s) (f_lim : ContinuousWithinAt f s a) (hs : s ∈ 𝓝[<] a) (f_lim' : Tendsto (fun x => deriv f x) (𝓝[<] a) (𝓝 e)) : HasDerivWithinAt f e (Iic a) a
decls.doc: If a function is differentiable on the left of a point `a : ℝ`, continuous at `a`, and its derivative also converges at `a`, then `f` is differentiable on the left at `a`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_of_hasDerivAt_of_ne
decls.sig: theorem hasDerivAt_of_hasDerivAt_of_ne {f g : ℝ → E} {x : ℝ} (f_diff : ∀ y ≠ x, HasDerivAt f (g y) y) (hf : ContinuousAt f x) (hg : ContinuousAt g x) : HasDerivAt f (g x) x
decls.doc: If a real function `f` has a derivative `g` everywhere but at a point, and `f` and `g` are continuous at this point, then `g` is also the derivative of `f` at this point.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_of_hasDerivAt_of_ne'

decls.name: FDerivMeasurableAux.A
decls.sig: def A (f : E → F) (L : E →L[𝕜] F) (r ε : ℝ) : Set E
decls.doc: The set `A f L r ε` is the set of points `x` around which the function `f` is well approximated at scale `r` by the linear map `L`, up to an error `ε`. We tweak the definition to make sure that this is an open set.

decls.name: FDerivMeasurableAux.B
decls.sig: def B (f : E → F) (K : Set (E →L[𝕜] F)) (r s ε : ℝ) : Set E
decls.doc: The set `B f K r s ε` is the set of points `x` around which there exists a continuous linear map `L` belonging to `K` (a given set of continuous linear maps) that approximates well the function `f` (up to an error `ε`), simultaneously at scales `r` and `s`.

decls.name: FDerivMeasurableAux.D
decls.sig: def D (f : E → F) (K : Set (E →L[𝕜] F)) : Set E
decls.doc: The set `D f K` is a complicated set constructed using countable intersections and unions. Its main use is that, when `K` is complete, it is exactly the set of points where `f` is differentiable, with a derivative in `K`.

decls.sig: theorem A_mono (L : E →L[𝕜] F) (r : ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (h : ε ≤ δ) : A f L r ε ⊆ A f L r δ

decls.name: FDerivMeasurableAux.le_of_mem_A
decls.sig: theorem le_of_mem_A {r ε : ℝ} {L : E →L[𝕜] F} {x : E} (hx : x ∈ A f L r ε) {y z : E} (hy : y ∈ closedBall x (r / 2)) (hz : z ∈ closedBall x (r / 2)) : ‖f z - f y - L (z - y)‖ ≤ ε * r

decls.name: FDerivMeasurableAux.mem_A_of_differentiable
decls.sig: theorem mem_A_of_differentiable {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) {x : E} (hx : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x) : ∃ R > 0, ∀ r ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) R, x ∈ A f (fderiv 𝕜 f x) r ε

decls.name: exist_minSmoothness_le_ne_infty

decls.doc: If `minSmoothness 𝕜 m ≤ n` for some (finite) integer `m`, then one can find `n' ∈ [minSmoothness 𝕜 m, n]` which is not `∞`: over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, just take `m`, and otherwise just take `ω`. The interest of this technical lemma is that, if a function is `C^{n'}` at a point for `n' ≠ ∞`, then it is `C^{n'}

decls.name: HasGradientWithinAt

decls.name: HasGradientAt
decls.sig: def HasGradientAt (f : F → 𝕜) (f' x : F)

decls.name: gradientWithin

decls.doc: Gradient of `f` at the point `x` within the set `s`, if it exists. Zero otherwise. If the derivative exists (i.e., `∃ f', HasGradientWithinAt f f' s x`), then `f x' = f x + ⟨f', x' - x⟩ + o (x' - x)` where `x'` converges to `x` inside `s`.

decls.name: gradient

decls.name: HasLineDerivAt
decls.sig: def HasLineDerivAt (f : E → F) (f' : F) (x : E) (v : E)
decls.doc: `f` has the derivative `f'` at the point `x` along the direction `v`. That is, `f (x + t v) = f x + t • f' + o (t)` when `t` tends to `0`. Note that this definition is less well behaved than the total Fréchet derivative, which should generally be favored over this one.

decls.name: LineDifferentiableWithinAt
decls.sig: def LineDifferentiableWithinAt (f : E → F) (s : Set E) (x : E) (v : E) : Prop
decls.doc: `f` is line-differentiable at the point `x` in the direction `v` in the set `s` if there exists `f'` such that `f (x + t v) = f x + t • f' + o (t)` when `t` tends to `0` and `x + t v ∈ s`.

decls.name: LineDifferentiableAt

decls.doc: `f` is line-differentiable at the point `x` in the direction `v` if there exists `f'` such that `f (x + t v) = f x + t • f' + o (t)` when `t` tends to `0`.

decls.name: lineDerivWithin

decls.doc: Line derivative of `f` at the point `x` in the direction `v` within the set `s`, if it exists. Zero otherwise. If the line derivative exists (i.e., `∃ f', HasLineDerivWithinAt 𝕜 f f' s x v`), then `f (x + t v) = f x + t lineDerivWithin 𝕜 f s x v + o (t)` when `t` tends to `0` and `x + t v ∈ s`.

decls.name: HasFDerivAt.apply_self_eq_smul_of_eventuallyEq
decls.sig: theorem HasFDerivAt.apply_self_eq_smul_of_eventuallyEq {w : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {w' : 𝕜} (hf : HasFDerivAt f L x) (hw : HasDerivAt w w' 1) (hhom : (fun t ↦ f (t • x)) =ᶠ[𝓝 1] fun t ↦ w t • f x) : L x = w' • f x
decls.doc: A local, vector-valued version of Euler's theorem on homogeneous functions. If `f (t • x) = w t • f x` for `t` in a neighborhood of `1`, then the derivative of `f` at `x`, applied to `x`, is `w' • f x`, where `w'` is the derivative of `w` at `1`.

decls.doc: A vector-valued version of Euler's theorem for a homogeneous function. If `f (t • y) = w t • f y` for all scalars `t` and points `y`, then the derivative of `f` at `x`, applied to `x`, is `w' • f x`, where `w'` is the derivative of `w` at `1`.

decls.sig: theorem HasFDerivAt.apply_self_eq_nsmul_of_homogeneous {k : ℕ} (hf : HasFDerivAt f L x) (hhom : ∀ (t : 𝕜) y, f (t • y) = t ^ k • f y) : L x = k • f x
decls.doc: A vector-valued version of Euler's theorem for a homogeneous function of natural degree. If `f (t • y) = t ^ k • f y` for all scalars `t` and points `y`, then the derivative of `f` at `x`, applied to `x`, is `k • f x`.

decls.doc: Converse to the mean value inequality: if `f` is line differentiable at `x₀` and `C`-lipschitz on a neighborhood of `x₀` then its line derivative at `x₀` in the direction `v` has norm bounded by `C * ‖v‖`. This version only assumes that `‖f x - f x₀‖ ≤ C * ‖x - x₀‖` in a neighborhood of `x`.

decls.name: tangentConeAt
decls.sig: irreducible_def tangentConeAt (s : Set E) (x : E) : Set E
decls.doc: The set of all tangent directions to the set `s` at the point `x`. A point `y` belongs to the tangent cone of `s` at `x` iff there exist a family of scalars `c n`, a family of vectors `d n`, and a nontrivial filter in the index type such that - `d n → 0` along the filter; - `x + d n ∈ s` eventually

decls.name: mem_tangentConeAt_of_frequently
decls.sig: theorem mem_tangentConeAt_of_frequently {α : Type*} (l : Filter α) (c : α → R) (d : α → E) (hd₀ : Tendsto d l (𝓝 0)) (hds : ∃ᶠ n in l, x + d n ∈ s) (hcd : Tendsto (fun n ↦ c n • d n) l (𝓝 y)) : y ∈ tangentConeAt R s x
decls.doc: Let `c n` be a family of scalars, `d n` be a family of vectors, and `l` be a filter such that - `d n → 0` along `l`; - `x + d n ∈ s` frequently along `l`; - `c n • d n → y` along `l`. Then `y` belongs to the tangent cone of `s` at `x`. See also - `mem_tangentConeAt_of_seq` for a version assuming tha

decls.name: mem_tangentConeAt_of_seq
decls.sig: theorem mem_tangentConeAt_of_seq {α : Type*} (l : Filter α) [l.NeBot] (c : α → R) (d : α → E) (hd₀ : Tendsto d l (𝓝 0)) (hds : ∀ᶠ n in l, x + d n ∈ s) (hcd : Tendsto (fun n ↦ c n • d n) l (𝓝 y)) : y ∈ tangentConeAt R s x
decls.doc: A special case of `mem_tangentConeAt_of_frequently`, which avoids `Filter.Frequently`.

decls.name: exists_fun_of_mem_tangentConeAt
decls.sig: theorem exists_fun_of_mem_tangentConeAt (h : y ∈ tangentConeAt R s x) : ∃ (α : Type (max u v)) (l : Filter α) (_hl : l.NeBot) (c : α → R) (d : α → E), Tendsto d l (𝓝 0) ∧ (∀ᶠ n in l, x + d n ∈ s) ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ c n • d n) l (𝓝 y)
decls.doc: If `y` belongs to the tangent cone of `s` at `x`, then there exist - an index type `α` and a nontrivial filter `l` on `α`; - a family of scalars `c n`, `n : α`, and a family of vectors `d n`, `n : α` such that - `d n → 0` along `l`; - `x + d n ∈ s` eventually along `l`; - `c n • d n → y` along `l`.

decls.sig: theorem bernstein_apply (n ν : ℕ) (x : I) : bernstein n ν x = (n.choose ν : ℝ) * (x : ℝ) ^ ν * (1 - (x : ℝ)) ^ (n - ν)

decls.name: bernsteinApproximation.apply_zero

decls.name: bernsteinApproximation.apply_one

decls.name: abs_integral_sub_setIntegral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_lt

decls.name: dist_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_le
decls.sig: theorem dist_integral_mulExpNegMulSq_comp_le (f : E →ᵇ ℝ) {A : Subalgebra ℝ (E →ᵇ ℝ)} (hA : (A.map (toContinuousMapₐ ℝ)).SeparatesPoints) (heq : ∀ g ∈ A, ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P = ∫ x, (g : E → ℝ) x ∂P') (hε : 0 < ε) : |∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P - ∫ x, mulExpNegMulSq ε (f x) ∂P'| ≤ 6 * √ε
decls.doc: If for any `g ∈ A` the integrals with respect to two finite measures `P, P'` coincide, then the difference of the integrals of `mulExpNegMulSq ε ∘ g` with respect to `P, P'` is bounded by `6 * √ε`.

decls.name: not_integrableOn_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter_aux
decls.sig: theorem not_integrableOn_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter_aux [CompleteSpace E] {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → F} {k : Set ℝ} (l : Filter ℝ) [NeBot l] [TendstoIxxClass Icc l l] (hl : k ∈ l) (hd : ∀ᶠ x in l, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hf : Tendsto (fun x => ‖f x‖) l atTop) (hfg : deriv f =O[l] g) : ¬IntegrableOn g k
decls.doc: If `f` is eventually differentiable along a nontrivial filter `l : Filter ℝ` that is generated by convex sets, the norm of `f` tends to infinity along `l`, and `f' = O(g)` along `l`, where `f'` is the derivative of `f`, then `g` is not integrable on any set `k` belonging to `l`. Auxiliary version as

decls.name: not_integrableOn_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter
decls.sig: theorem not_integrableOn_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → F} {k : Set ℝ} (l : Filter ℝ) [NeBot l] [TendstoIxxClass Icc l l] (hl : k ∈ l) (hd : ∀ᶠ x in l, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hf : Tendsto (fun x => ‖f x‖) l atTop) (hfg : deriv f =O[l] g) : ¬IntegrableOn g k

decls.name: not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter
decls.sig: theorem not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → F} {a b : ℝ} (l : Filter ℝ) [NeBot l] [TendstoIxxClass Icc l l] (hl : [[a, b]] ∈ l) (hd : ∀ᶠ x in l, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hf : Tendsto (fun x => ‖f x‖) l atTop) (hfg : deriv f =O[l] g) : ¬IntervalIntegrable g volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is eventually differentiable along a nontrivial filter `l : Filter ℝ` that is generated by convex sets, the norm of `f` tends to infinity along `l`, and `f' = O(g)` along `l`, where `f'` is the derivative of `f`, then `g` is not integrable on any interval `a..b` such that `[a, b] ∈ l`.

decls.name: not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_within_sdiff_singleton
decls.sig: theorem not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_within_sdiff_singleton {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → F} {a b c : ℝ} (hne : a ≠ b) (hc : c ∈ [[a, b]]) (h_deriv : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[[[a, b]] \ {c}] c, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (h_infty : Tendsto (fun x => ‖f x‖) (𝓝[[[a, b]] \ {c}] c) atTop) (hg : deriv f =O[𝓝[[[a, b]] \ {c}] c] g) : ¬IntervalIntegrable g volume a b
decls.doc: If `a ≠ b`, `c ∈ [a, b]`, `f` is differentiable in the neighborhood of `c` within `[a, b] \ {c}`, `‖f x‖ → ∞` as `x → c` within `[a, b] \ {c}`, and `f' = O(g)` along `𝓝[[a, b] \ {c}] c`, where `f'` is the derivative of `f`, then `g` is not interval integrable on `a..b`.

decls.name: not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_punctured
decls.sig: theorem not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_punctured {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → F} {a b c : ℝ} (h_deriv : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[≠] c, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (h_infty : Tendsto (fun x => ‖f x‖) (𝓝[≠] c) atTop) (hg : deriv f =O[𝓝[≠] c] g) (hne : a ≠ b) (hc : c ∈ [[a, b]]) : ¬IntervalIntegrable g volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is differentiable in a punctured neighborhood of `c`, `‖f x‖ → ∞` as `x → c` (more formally, along the filter `𝓝[≠] c`), and `f' = O(g)` along `𝓝[≠] c`, where `f'` is the derivative of `f`, then `g` is not interval integrable on any nontrivial interval `a..b` such that `c ∈ [a, b]`.

decls.name: not_intervalIntegrable_of_sub_inv_isBigO_punctured
decls.sig: theorem not_intervalIntegrable_of_sub_inv_isBigO_punctured {f : ℝ → F} {a b c : ℝ} (hf : (fun x => (x - c)⁻¹) =O[𝓝[≠] c] f) (hne : a ≠ b) (hc : c ∈ [[a, b]]) : ¬IntervalIntegrable f volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` grows in the punctured neighborhood of `c : ℝ` at least as fast as `1 / (x - c)`, then it is not interval integrable on any nontrivial interval `a..b`, `c ∈ [a, b]`.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_sub_inv_iff
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_sub_inv_iff {a b c : ℝ} : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => (x - c)⁻¹) volume a b ↔ a = b ∨ c ∉ [[a, b]]
decls.doc: The function `fun x => (x - c)⁻¹` is integrable on `a..b` if and only if `a = b` or `c ∉ [a, b]`.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_inv_iff
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_inv_iff {a b : ℝ} : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => x⁻¹) volume a b ↔ a = b ∨ (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]
decls.doc: The function `fun x => x⁻¹` is integrable on `a..b` if and only if `a = b` or `0 ∉ [a, b]`.

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq
decls.sig: noncomputable def stirlingSeq (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: Define `stirlingSeq n` as $\frac{n!}{\sqrt{2n}(\frac{n}{e})^n}$. Stirling's formula states that this sequence has limit $\sqrt(π)$.

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq_zero
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq_zero : stirlingSeq 0 = 0

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq_one
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq_one : stirlingSeq 1 = exp 1 / √2

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_formula
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq_formula (n : ℕ) : log (stirlingSeq n) = Real.log n ! - 1 / 2 * Real.log (2 * n) - n * log (n / exp 1)

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_sdiff_hasSum
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq_sdiff_hasSum (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / (2 * ↑(k + 1) + 1) * ((1 / (2 * ↑(m + 1) + 1)) ^ 2) ^ ↑(k + 1)) (log (stirlingSeq (m + 1)) - log (stirlingSeq (m + 2)))
decls.doc: The sequence `log (stirlingSeq (m + 1)) - log (stirlingSeq (m + 2))` has the series expansion `∑ 1 / (2 * (k + 1) + 1) * (1 / 2 * (m + 1) + 1)^(2 * (k + 1))`.

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq'_antitone
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq'_antitone : Antitone (Real.log ∘ stirlingSeq ∘ succ)
decls.doc: The sequence `log ∘ stirlingSeq ∘ succ` is monotone decreasing

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_sdiff_le
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq_sdiff_le (n : ℕ) : log (stirlingSeq n) - log (stirlingSeq (n + 1)) ≤ 1 / (12 * n * (n + 1))
decls.doc: **Robbins' sharp stepwise bound** for the Stirling sequence: `log (stirlingSeq n) - log (stirlingSeq (n+1)) ≤ 1 / (12 n (n + 1))`.

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_bounded_aux
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq_bounded_aux (n : ℕ) : log (stirlingSeq 1) - log (stirlingSeq (n + 1)) ≤ 12⁻¹
decls.doc: For any `n`, we have `log_stirlingSeq 1 - log_stirlingSeq n ≤ 12⁻¹`.

decls.name: Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_bounded_by_constant
decls.sig: theorem log_stirlingSeq_bounded_by_constant (n : ℕ) : 1 - 12⁻¹ - log 2 / 2 ≤ log (stirlingSeq (n + 1))
decls.doc: The sequence `log_stirlingSeq` is bounded below for `n ≥ 1`.

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq'_pos
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq'_pos (n : ℕ) : 0 < stirlingSeq (n + 1)
decls.doc: The sequence `stirlingSeq` is positive for `n > 0`.

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq'_bounded_by_pos_constant
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq'_bounded_by_pos_constant : ∃ a, 0 < a ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, a ≤ stirlingSeq (n + 1)
decls.doc: The sequence `stirlingSeq` has a positive lower bound.

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq'_antitone
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq'_antitone : Antitone (stirlingSeq ∘ succ)
decls.doc: The sequence `stirlingSeq ∘ succ` is monotone decreasing

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq_has_pos_limit_a
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq_has_pos_limit_a : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Tendsto stirlingSeq atTop (𝓝 a)
decls.doc: The limit `a` of the sequence `stirlingSeq` satisfies `0 < a`

decls.name: Stirling.tendsto_self_div_two_mul_self_add_one
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_self_div_two_mul_self_add_one : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) / (2 * n + 1)) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 2))
decls.doc: The sequence `n / (2 * n + 1)` tends to `1/2`

decls.name: Stirling.stirlingSeq_pow_four_div_stirlingSeq_pow_two_eq
decls.sig: theorem stirlingSeq_pow_four_div_stirlingSeq_pow_two_eq (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : stirlingSeq n ^ 4 / stirlingSeq (2 * n) ^ 2 * (n / (2 * n + 1)) = Wallis.W n
decls.doc: For any `n ≠ 0`, we have the identity `(stirlingSeq n)^4 / (stirlingSeq (2*n))^2 * (n / (2 * n + 1)) = W n`, where `W n` is the `n`-th partial product of Wallis' formula for `π / 2`.

decls.name: Stirling.second_wallis_limit
decls.sig: theorem second_wallis_limit (a : ℝ) (hane : a ≠ 0) (ha : Tendsto stirlingSeq atTop (𝓝 a)) : Tendsto Wallis.W atTop (𝓝 (a ^ 2 / 2))
decls.doc: Suppose the sequence `stirlingSeq` (defined above) has the limit `a ≠ 0`. Then the Wallis sequence `W n` has limit `a^2 / 2`.

decls.name: Stirling.tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi : Tendsto stirlingSeq atTop (𝓝 (√π))
decls.doc: **Stirling's Formula**

decls.name: Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling
decls.sig: lemma factorial_isEquivalent_stirling : (fun n ↦ n ! : ℕ → ℝ) ~[atTop] fun n ↦ Real.sqrt (2 * n * π) * (n / exp 1) ^ n
decls.doc: **Stirling's Formula**, formulated in terms of `Asymptotics.IsEquivalent`.

decls.name: Stirling.sqrt_pi_le_stirlingSeq
decls.sig: theorem sqrt_pi_le_stirlingSeq {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : √π ≤ stirlingSeq n
decls.doc: The Stirling sequence is bounded below by `√π`, for all positive naturals. Note that this bound holds for all `n > 0`, rather than for sufficiently large `n`: it is effective.

decls.name: Stirling.le_factorial_stirling
decls.sig: theorem le_factorial_stirling (n : ℕ) : √(2 * π * n) * (n / exp 1) ^ n ≤ n !
decls.doc: Stirling's approximation gives a lower bound for `n!` for all `n`. The left-hand side is formulated to mimic the usual informal description of the approximation. See also `factorial_isEquivalent_stirling` which says these are asymptotically equivalent. That statement gives an upper bound also, but r

decls.name: Stirling.le_log_factorial_stirling
decls.sig: theorem le_log_factorial_stirling {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : n * log n - n + log n / 2 + log (2 * π) / 2 ≤ log n !
decls.doc: Stirling's approximation gives a lower bound for `log n!` for all positive `n`. The left-hand side is formulated in decreasing order in `n`: the higher order terms are first. This is a consequence of `le_factorial_stirling`, but is stated separately since the logarithmic version is sometimes more pr

decls.name: Complex.cos_ne_zero_of_arctan_bounds

decls.name: Complex.arctan_tan
decls.sig: theorem arctan_tan {z : ℂ} (h₀ : z ≠ π / 2) (h₁ : -(π / 2) < z.re) (h₂ : z.re ≤ π / 2) : arctan (tan z) = z

decls.name: Complex.log_neg_one

decls.name: Complex.log_I

decls.name: Complex.log_neg_I

decls.name: Complex.log_conj_eq_ite

decls.name: Complex.log_conj

decls.name: Complex.log_inv_eq_ite
decls.sig: theorem log_inv_eq_ite (x : ℂ) : log x⁻¹ = if x.arg = π then -conj (log x) else -log x

decls.name: Complex.log_inv
decls.sig: theorem log_inv (x : ℂ) (hx : x.arg ≠ π) : log x⁻¹ = -log x

decls.name: Complex.two_pi_I_ne_zero

decls.doc: `Complex.exp` as an `OpenPartialHomeomorph` with `source = {z | -π < im z < π}` and `target = {z | 0 < re z} ∪ {z | im z ≠ 0}` (a.k.a. `slitPlane`). This definition is used to prove that `Complex.log` is complex differentiable at all points but the negative real semi-axis.

decls.name: Complex.norm_log_sub_logTaylor_le

decls.name: Real.Gamma_eq_zero_iff

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral
decls.sig: noncomputable def betaIntegral (u v : ℂ) : ℂ
decls.doc: The Beta function `Β (u, v)`, defined as `∫ x:ℝ in 0..1, x ^ (u - 1) * (1 - x) ^ (v - 1)`.

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_convergent_left
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_convergent_left {u : ℂ} (hu : 0 < re u) (v : ℂ) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => (x : ℂ) ^ (u - 1) * (1 - (x : ℂ)) ^ (v - 1) : ℝ → ℂ) volume 0 (1 / 2)

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_convergent
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_convergent {u v : ℂ} (hu : 0 < re u) (hv : 0 < re v) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => (x : ℂ) ^ (u - 1) * (1 - (x : ℂ)) ^ (v - 1) : ℝ → ℂ) volume 0 1
decls.doc: The Beta integral is convergent for all `u, v` of positive real part.

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_symm
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_symm (u v : ℂ) : betaIntegral v u = betaIntegral u v

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_eval_one_right
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_eval_one_right {u : ℂ} (hu : 0 < re u) : betaIntegral u 1 = 1 / u

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_scaled
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_scaled (s t : ℂ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : ∫ x in 0..a, (x : ℂ) ^ (s - 1) * ((a : ℂ) - x) ^ (t - 1) = (a : ℂ) ^ (s + t - 1) * betaIntegral s t

decls.name: Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral
decls.sig: theorem Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral {s t : ℂ} (hs : 0 < re s) (ht : 0 < re t) : Gamma s * Gamma t = Gamma (s + t) * betaIntegral s t
decls.doc: Relation between Beta integral and Gamma function.

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_recurrence
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_recurrence {u v : ℂ} (hu : 0 < re u) (hv : 0 < re v) : u * betaIntegral u (v + 1) = v * betaIntegral (u + 1) v
decls.doc: Recurrence formula for the Beta function.

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_eval_nat_add_one_right
decls.sig: theorem betaIntegral_eval_nat_add_one_right {u : ℂ} (hu : 0 < re u) (n : ℕ) : betaIntegral u (n + 1) = n ! / ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (u + j)

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq
decls.sig: noncomputable def GammaSeq (s : ℂ) (n : ℕ)
decls.doc: The sequence with `n`-th term `n ^ s * n! / (s * (s + 1) * ... * (s + n))`, for complex `s`. We will show that this tends to `Γ(s)` as `n → ∞`.

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq_eq_betaIntegral_of_re_pos
decls.sig: theorem GammaSeq_eq_betaIntegral_of_re_pos {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < re s) (n : ℕ) : GammaSeq s n = (n : ℂ) ^ s * betaIntegral s (n + 1)

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq_add_one_left
decls.sig: theorem GammaSeq_add_one_left (s : ℂ) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : GammaSeq (s + 1) n / s = n / (n + 1 + s) * GammaSeq s n

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral
decls.sig: theorem GammaSeq_eq_approx_Gamma_integral {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < re s) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : GammaSeq s n = ∫ x : ℝ in 0..n, ↑((1 - x / n) ^ n) * (x : ℂ) ^ (s - 1)

decls.name: Complex.approx_Gamma_integral_tendsto_Gamma_integral

decls.doc: The main technical lemma for `GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma`, expressing the integral defining the Gamma function for `0 < re s` as the limit of a sequence of integrals over finite intervals.

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma
decls.sig: theorem GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma (s : ℂ) : Tendsto (GammaSeq s) atTop (𝓝 <| Gamma s)
decls.doc: Euler's limit formula for the complex Gamma function.

decls.name: Complex.GammaSeq_mul
decls.sig: theorem GammaSeq_mul (z : ℂ) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : GammaSeq z n * GammaSeq (1 - z) n = n / (n + ↑1 - z) * (↑1 / (z * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range n, (↑1 - z ^ 2 / ((j : ℂ) + 1) ^ 2)))

decls.name: Complex.Gamma_ne_zero

decls.name: Complex.Gamma_add_nat_div_Gamma_eq
decls.sig: theorem Gamma_add_nat_div_Gamma_eq {n : ℕ} (z : ℂ) (hz : ∀ k : ℕ, z ≠ -k) : Gamma (z + n) / Gamma z = (ascPochhammer ℂ n).eval z

decls.name: Real.GammaSeq
decls.sig: noncomputable def GammaSeq (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ)

decls.name: Real.GammaSeq_tendsto_Gamma

decls.name: Real.Gamma_mul_Gamma_one_sub

decls.doc: Euler's reflection formula for the real Gamma function.

decls.name: Complex.one_div_Gamma_eq_self_mul_one_div_Gamma_add_one

decls.name: Complex.differentiable_one_div_Gamma

decls.name: Complex.betaIntegral_eq_Gamma_mul_div

decls.name: Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half

decls.name: Real.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half
decls.sig: theorem Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half (s : ℝ) : Gamma s * Gamma (s + 1 / 2) = Gamma (2 * s) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (1 - 2 * s) * √π

decls.name: Real.Gamma_mul_add_mul_le_rpow_Gamma_mul_rpow_Gamma
decls.sig: theorem Gamma_mul_add_mul_le_rpow_Gamma_mul_rpow_Gamma {s t a b : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (ht : 0 < t) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : a + b = 1) : Gamma (a * s + b * t) ≤ Gamma s ^ a * Gamma t ^ b

decls.name: Real.convexOn_log_Gamma

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.logGammaSeq
decls.sig: def logGammaSeq (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The function `n ↦ x log n + log n! - (log x + ... + log (x + n))`, which we will show tends to `log (Gamma x)` as `n → ∞`.

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.f_nat_eq
decls.sig: theorem f_nat_eq (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hn : n ≠ 0) : f n = f 1 + log (n - 1)!

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.f_add_nat_eq
decls.sig: theorem f_add_nat_eq (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hx : 0 < x) (n : ℕ) : f (x + n) = f x + ∑ m ∈ Finset.range n, log (x + m)

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.f_add_nat_le
decls.sig: theorem f_add_nat_le (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hx : 0 < x) (hx' : x ≤ 1) : f (n + x) ≤ f n + x * log n
decls.doc: Linear upper bound for `f (x + n)` on unit interval

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.f_add_nat_ge
decls.sig: theorem f_add_nat_ge (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hx : 0 < x) : f n + x * log (n - 1) ≤ f (n + x)
decls.doc: Linear lower bound for `f (x + n)` on unit interval

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.logGammaSeq_add_one
decls.sig: theorem logGammaSeq_add_one (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : logGammaSeq (x + 1) n = logGammaSeq x (n + 1) + log x - (x + 1) * (log (n + 1) - log n)

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.le_logGammaSeq
decls.sig: theorem le_logGammaSeq (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hx : 0 < x) (hx' : x ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) : f x ≤ f 1 + x * log (n + 1) - x * log n + logGammaSeq x n

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.ge_logGammaSeq
decls.sig: theorem ge_logGammaSeq (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hx : 0 < x) (hn : n ≠ 0) : f 1 + logGammaSeq x n ≤ f x

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.tendsto_logGammaSeq_of_le_one
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_logGammaSeq_of_le_one (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hx : 0 < x) (hx' : x ≤ 1) : Tendsto (logGammaSeq x) atTop (𝓝 <| f x - f 1)

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.tendsto_logGammaSeq
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_logGammaSeq (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) f) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = f y + log y) (hx : 0 < x) : Tendsto (logGammaSeq x) atTop (𝓝 <| f x - f 1)

decls.name: Real.BohrMollerup.tendsto_log_gamma
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_log_gamma {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : Tendsto (logGammaSeq x) atTop (𝓝 <| log (Gamma x))

decls.name: Real.eq_Gamma_of_log_convex
decls.sig: theorem eq_Gamma_of_log_convex {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf_conv : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) (log ∘ f)) (hf_feq : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → f (y + 1) = y * f y) (hf_pos : ∀ {y : ℝ}, 0 < y → 0 < f y) (hf_one : f 1 = 1) : EqOn f Gamma (Ioi (0 : ℝ))
decls.doc: The **Bohr-Mollerup theorem**: the Gamma function is the *unique* log-convex, positive-valued function on the positive reals which satisfies `f 1 = 1` and `f (x + 1) = x * f x` for all `x`.

decls.name: Complex.digamma_apply_add_nat
decls.sig: theorem digamma_apply_add_nat {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ m : ℕ, s ≠ -(m : ℂ)) (n : ℕ) : digamma (s + n) = digamma s + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (s + k)⁻¹
decls.doc: **The iterated digamma recurrence** `ψ(s + n) = ψ(s) + ∑_{k < n} 1 / (s + k)`, for `s ∉ {0, -1, -2, …}`. Proved by induction from `digamma_apply_add_one`.

decls.sig: theorem digamma_one_sub {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ n : ℤ, s ≠ n) : digamma (1 - s) = digamma s + π * cot (π * s)
decls.doc: **Euler's reflection formula for the digamma function**: `ψ (1 - s) = ψ s + π * cot (π * s)` for `s` not an integer.

decls.name: HasDerivAt.logDeriv_Gamma
decls.sig: theorem _root_.HasDerivAt.logDeriv_Gamma {g : ℂ → ℂ} {a s : ℂ} (hg : HasDerivAt g a s) (h : ∀ m : ℕ, g s ≠ -(m : ℂ)) : logDeriv (fun z ↦ Gamma (g z)) s = a * digamma (g s)
decls.doc: If `g` has derivative `a` at `s`, then the logarithmic derivative of `Gamma ∘ g` at `s` is `a * digamma (g s)`.

decls.name: Complex.digamma_two_mul
decls.sig: theorem digamma_two_mul {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ m : ℕ, 2 * s ≠ -(m : ℂ)) : digamma (2 * s) = (1 / 2) * (digamma s + digamma (s + 1 / 2)) + log 2
decls.doc: **The digamma duplication formula** `ψ(2s) = ½(ψ(s) + ψ(s + ½)) + log 2`, for `2s ∉ {0, -1, -2, …}`, which is equivalent to `s` and `s + ½` both avoiding the poles of `ψ`. Proved from Legendre's doubling `Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half` by taking logarithmic derivatives.

decls.doc: The power function `x ↦ x^s` is integrable on `(0, t)` iff `-1 < s`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_cpow
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_cpow {r : ℂ} (h : 0 ≤ r.re ∨ (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => (x : ℂ) ^ r) μ a b
decls.doc: See `intervalIntegrable_cpow'` for a version with a weaker hypothesis on `r`, but assuming the measure is volume.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_cpow'
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_cpow' {r : ℂ} (h : -1 < r.re) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => (x : ℂ) ^ r) volume a b
decls.doc: See `intervalIntegrable_cpow` for a version applying to any locally finite measure, but with a stronger hypothesis on `r`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integrableOn_Ioo_cpow_iff
decls.sig: theorem integrableOn_Ioo_cpow_iff {s : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : IntegrableOn (fun x : ℝ ↦ (x : ℂ) ^ s) (Ioo (0 : ℝ) t) ↔ -1 < s.re
decls.doc: The complex power function `x ↦ x^s` is integrable on `(0, t)` iff `-1 < s.re`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_id
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_id : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => x) μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_one_div
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_one_div (h : ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ [[a, b]] → f x ≠ 0) (hf : ContinuousOn f [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => 1 / f x) μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_inv
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_inv (h : ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ [[a, b]] → f x ≠ 0) (hf : ContinuousOn f [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => (f x)⁻¹) μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_sin
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_sin : IntervalIntegrable sin μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_cos
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_cos : IntervalIntegrable cos μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_exp
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_exp : IntervalIntegrable exp μ a b

decls.name: IntervalIntegrable.log
decls.sig: theorem _root_.IntervalIntegrable.log (hf : ContinuousOn f [[a, b]]) (h : ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ [[a, b]] → f x ≠ 0) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => log (f x)) μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_log
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_log (h : (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable log μ a b
decls.doc: The real logarithm is interval integrable (with respect to every locally finite measure) over every interval that does not contain zero. See `intervalIntegrable_log'` for a version without any hypothesis on the interval, but assuming the measure is the volume.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_log'
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_log' : IntervalIntegrable log volume a b
decls.doc: The real logarithm is interval integrable (with respect to the volume measure) on every interval. See `intervalIntegrable_log` for a version applying to any locally finite measure, but with an additional hypothesis on the interval.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_one_div_one_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_one_div_one_add_sq : IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => 1 / (↑1 + x ^ 2)) μ a b

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_inv_one_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_inv_one_add_sq : IntervalIntegrable (fun x : ℝ => (↑1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹) μ a b

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log_norm
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log_norm (hf : MeromorphicOn f [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (log ‖f ·‖) volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is real-meromorphic on a compact interval, then `log ‖f ·‖` is interval integrable on this interval.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log
decls.sig: theorem _root_.MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : MeromorphicOn f [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (log ∘ f) volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is real-meromorphic on a compact interval, then `log ∘ f` is interval integrable on this interval.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_log_sin
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_log_sin : IntervalIntegrable (log ∘ sin) volume a b
decls.doc: Special case of `MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log`: The function `log ∘ sin` is interval integrable over every interval.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_log_cos
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_log_cos : IntervalIntegrable (log ∘ cos) volume a b
decls.doc: Special case of `MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_log`: The function `log ∘ cos` is interval integrable over every interval.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm (hf : MeromorphicOn f (sphere c |R|)) : CircleIntegrable (log ‖f ·‖) c R
decls.doc: If `f` is complex meromorphic on a circle in the complex plane, then `log ‖f ·‖` is circle integrable over that circle.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm_of_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm_of_nonneg (hf : MeromorphicOn f (sphere c R)) (hR : 0 ≤ R) : CircleIntegrable (log ‖f ·‖) c R
decls.doc: Variant of `MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm` for non-negative radii.

decls.name: circleIntegrable_log_norm_factorizedRational
decls.sig: theorem circleIntegrable_log_norm_factorizedRational {R : ℝ} {c : ℂ} (D : ℂ → ℤ) : CircleIntegrable (∑ᶠ u, ((D u) * log ‖· - u‖)) c R
decls.doc: Variant of `MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_log_norm` for factorized rational functions.

decls.name: circleIntegrable_log_norm_sub_const
decls.sig: lemma circleIntegrable_log_norm_sub_const {a : ℂ} (r : ℝ) : CircleIntegrable (log ‖· - a‖) c r
decls.doc: If `a` is any complex number, the function `(log ‖· - a‖)` is circle integrable over every circle.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_posLog_norm
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.intervalIntegrable_posLog_norm (hf : MeromorphicOn f [[a, b]]) : IntervalIntegrable (log⁺ ‖f ·‖) volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is real-meromorphic on a compact interval, then `log⁺ ‖f ·‖` is interval integrable on this interval.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_posLog_norm
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_posLog_norm (hf : MeromorphicOn f (sphere c |R|)) : CircleIntegrable (log⁺ ‖f ·‖) c R
decls.doc: If `f` is complex meromorphic on a circle in the complex plane, then `log⁺ ‖f ·‖` is circle integrable over that circle.

decls.name: MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_posLog_norm_of_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_posLog_norm_of_nonneg (hf : MeromorphicOn f (sphere c R)) (hR : 0 ≤ R) : CircleIntegrable (log⁺ ‖f ·‖) c R
decls.doc: Variant of `MeromorphicOn.circleIntegrable_posLog_norm` for non-negative radii.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_mul_right
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_mul_right : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (x * c)) = ∫ x in a * c..b * c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_mul_left
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_mul_left : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x)) = ∫ x in c * a..c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_mul_integral_comp_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_mul_integral_comp_div : (c⁻¹ * ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c)) = ∫ x in a / c..b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_mul_add
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_mul_add : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x + d)) = ∫ x in c * a + d..c * b + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_add_mul
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_add_mul : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (d + c * x)) = ∫ x in d + c * a..d + c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_mul_integral_comp_div_add
decls.sig: theorem inv_mul_integral_comp_div_add : (c⁻¹ * ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c + d)) = ∫ x in a / c + d..b / c + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_mul_integral_comp_add_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_mul_integral_comp_add_div : (c⁻¹ * ∫ x in a..b, f (d + x / c)) = ∫ x in d + a / c..d + b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_mul_sub
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_mul_sub : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x - d)) = ∫ x in c * a - d..c * b - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.mul_integral_comp_sub_mul
decls.sig: theorem mul_integral_comp_sub_mul : (c * ∫ x in a..b, f (d - c * x)) = ∫ x in d - c * b..d - c * a, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_mul_integral_comp_div_sub
decls.sig: theorem inv_mul_integral_comp_div_sub : (c⁻¹ * ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c - d)) = ∫ x in a / c - d..b / c - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_mul_integral_comp_sub_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_mul_integral_comp_sub_div : (c⁻¹ * ∫ x in a..b, f (d - x / c)) = ∫ x in d - b / c..d - a / c, f x

decls.name: integral_cpow
decls.sig: theorem integral_cpow {r : ℂ} (h : -1 < r.re ∨ r ≠ -1 ∧ (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : (∫ x : ℝ in a..b, (x : ℂ) ^ r) = ((b : ℂ) ^ (r + 1) - (a : ℂ) ^ (r + 1)) / (r + 1)

decls.name: integral_rpow
decls.sig: theorem integral_rpow {r : ℝ} (h : -1 < r ∨ r ≠ -1 ∧ (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : ∫ x in a..b, x ^ r = (b ^ (r + 1) - a ^ (r + 1)) / (r + 1)

decls.name: integral_zpow
decls.sig: theorem integral_zpow {n : ℤ} (h : 0 ≤ n ∨ n ≠ -1 ∧ (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : ∫ x in a..b, x ^ n = (b ^ (n + 1) - a ^ (n + 1)) / (n + 1)

decls.name: integral_pow
decls.sig: theorem integral_pow : ∫ x in a..b, x ^ n = (b ^ (n + 1) - a ^ (n + 1)) / (n + 1)

decls.name: integral_pow_abs_sub_uIoc
decls.sig: theorem integral_pow_abs_sub_uIoc : ∫ x in Ι a b, |x - a| ^ n = |b - a| ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1)
decls.doc: Integral of `|x - a| ^ n` over `Ι a b`. This integral appears in the proof of the Picard-Lindelöf/Cauchy-Lipschitz theorem.

decls.name: integral_id
decls.sig: theorem integral_id : ∫ x in a..b, x = (b ^ 2 - a ^ 2) / 2

decls.name: integral_one
decls.sig: theorem integral_one : (∫ _ in a..b, (1 : ℝ)) = b - a

decls.name: integral_const_on_unit_interval
decls.sig: theorem integral_const_on_unit_interval : ∫ _ in a..a + 1, b = b

decls.name: integral_inv
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv (h : (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : ∫ x in a..b, x⁻¹ = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_inv_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_of_pos (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : ∫ x in a..b, x⁻¹ = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_inv_of_neg
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_of_neg (ha : a < 0) (hb : b < 0) : ∫ x in a..b, x⁻¹ = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_one_div
decls.sig: theorem integral_one_div (h : (0 : ℝ) ∉ [[a, b]]) : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, 1 / x = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_one_div_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem integral_one_div_of_pos (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, 1 / x = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_one_div_of_neg
decls.sig: theorem integral_one_div_of_neg (ha : a < 0) (hb : b < 0) : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, 1 / x = log (b / a)

decls.name: integral_exp
decls.sig: theorem integral_exp : ∫ x in a..b, exp x = exp b - exp a

decls.name: integral_exp_mul_complex
decls.sig: theorem integral_exp_mul_complex {c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0) : (∫ x in a..b, Complex.exp (c * x)) = (Complex.exp (c * b) - Complex.exp (c * a)) / c

decls.name: integral_exp_mul_I_eq_sin
decls.sig: lemma integral_exp_mul_I_eq_sin (r : ℝ) : ∫ t in -r..r, Complex.exp (t * Complex.I) = 2 * Real.sin r

decls.name: integral_exp_mul_I_eq_sinc
decls.sig: lemma integral_exp_mul_I_eq_sinc (r : ℝ) : ∫ t in -r..r, Complex.exp (t * Complex.I) = 2 * r * sinc r

decls.name: integral_log_from_zero_of_pos
decls.sig: lemma integral_log_from_zero_of_pos (ht : 0 < b) : ∫ s in 0..b, log s = b * log b - b
decls.doc: Helper lemma for `integral_log`: case where `a = 0` and `b` is positive.

decls.name: integral_log_from_zero
decls.sig: lemma integral_log_from_zero {b : ℝ} : ∫ s in 0..b, log s = b * log b - b
decls.doc: Helper lemma for `integral_log`: case where `a = 0`.

decls.name: integral_log
decls.sig: theorem integral_log : ∫ s in a..b, log s = b * log b - a * log a - b + a

decls.name: integral_sin
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin : ∫ x in a..b, sin x = cos a - cos b

decls.name: integral_cos
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos : ∫ x in a..b, cos x = sin b - sin a

decls.name: integral_cos_mul_complex
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_mul_complex {z : ℂ} (hz : z ≠ 0) (a b : ℝ) : (∫ x in a..b, Complex.cos (z * x)) = Complex.sin (z * b) / z - Complex.sin (z * a) / z

decls.name: integral_cos_sq_sub_sin_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_sq_sub_sin_sq : ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ 2 - sin x ^ 2 = sin b * cos b - sin a * cos a

decls.name: integral_one_div_one_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_one_div_one_add_sq : (∫ x : ℝ in a..b, ↑1 / (↑1 + x ^ 2)) = arctan b - arctan a

decls.name: integral_inv_one_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_one_add_sq : (∫ x : ℝ in a..b, (↑1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹) = arctan b - arctan a

decls.name: integral_inv_sq_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_sq_add_sq {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, (c ^ 2 + x ^ 2)⁻¹ = c⁻¹ * (arctan (b / c) - arctan (a / c))

decls.name: integral_div_sq_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_div_sq_add_sq {c : ℝ} : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, c / (c ^ 2 + x ^ 2) = arctan (b / c) - arctan (a / c)

decls.name: integral_id_div_sq_add_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_id_div_sq_add_sq {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) : ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, x / (c ^ 2 + x ^ 2) = (log (c ^ 2 + b ^ 2) - log (c ^ 2 + a ^ 2)) / 2

decls.name: integral_inv_div_log
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_div_log (ha : 1 < a) (hb : 1 < b) : ∫ t in a..b, t⁻¹ / log t = log (log b) - log (log a)
decls.doc: The integrand is chosen to match the conclusion of `Real.deriv_log_log`.

decls.name: integral_inv_div_log_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_inv_div_log_sq (ha : 1 < a) (hb : 1 < b) : ∫ t in a..b, t⁻¹ / log t ^ 2 = (log a)⁻¹ - (log b)⁻¹
decls.doc: The integrand is chosen to match the conclusion of `Real.deriv_inv_log`.

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_aux
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_aux : (∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ (n + 2)) = (sin a ^ (n + 1) * cos a - sin b ^ (n + 1) * cos b + (↑n + 1) * ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ n) - (↑n + 1) * ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ (n + 2)

decls.name: integral_sin_pow
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow : (∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ (n + 2)) = (sin a ^ (n + 1) * cos a - sin b ^ (n + 1) * cos b) / (n + 2) + (n + 1) / (n + 2) * ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ n
decls.doc: The reduction formula for the integral of `sin x ^ n` for any natural `n ≥ 2`.

decls.name: integral_sin_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_sq : ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ 2 = (sin a * cos a - sin b * cos b + b - a) / 2

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_odd
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_odd : (∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ (2 * n + 1)) = 2 * ∏ i ∈ range n, (2 * (i : ℝ) + 2) / (2 * i + 3)

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_even
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_even : (∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ (2 * n)) = π * ∏ i ∈ range n, (2 * (i : ℝ) + 1) / (2 * i + 2)

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_pos
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_pos : 0 < ∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ n

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_succ_le
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_succ_le : (∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ (n + 1)) ≤ ∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ n

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_antitone
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_antitone : Antitone fun n : ℕ => ∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ n

decls.name: integral_cos_pow_aux
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_pow_aux : (∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ (n + 2)) = (cos b ^ (n + 1) * sin b - cos a ^ (n + 1) * sin a + (n + 1) * ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ n) - (n + 1) * ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ (n + 2)

decls.name: integral_cos_pow
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_pow : (∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ (n + 2)) = (cos b ^ (n + 1) * sin b - cos a ^ (n + 1) * sin a) / (n + 2) + (n + 1) / (n + 2) * ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ n
decls.doc: The reduction formula for the integral of `cos x ^ n` for any natural `n ≥ 2`.

decls.name: integral_cos_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_sq : ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ 2 = (cos b * sin b - cos a * sin a + b - a) / 2

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_mul_cos_pow_odd
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_mul_cos_pow_odd (m n : ℕ) : (∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ m * cos x ^ (2 * n + 1)) = ∫ u in sin a..sin b, u ^ m * (1 - u ^ 2) ^ n
decls.doc: Simplification of the integral of `sin x ^ m * cos x ^ n`, case `n` is odd.

decls.name: integral_sin_mul_cos₁
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_mul_cos₁ : ∫ x in a..b, sin x * cos x = (sin b ^ 2 - sin a ^ 2) / 2
decls.doc: The integral of `sin x * cos x`, given in terms of sin². See `integral_sin_mul_cos₂` below for the integral given in terms of cos².

decls.name: integral_sin_sq_mul_cos
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_sq_mul_cos : ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ 2 * cos x = (sin b ^ 3 - sin a ^ 3) / 3

decls.name: integral_cos_pow_three
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_pow_three : ∫ x in a..b, cos x ^ 3 = sin b - sin a - (sin b ^ 3 - sin a ^ 3) / 3

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_odd_mul_cos_pow
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_odd_mul_cos_pow (m n : ℕ) : (∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ (2 * m + 1) * cos x ^ n) = ∫ u in cos b..cos a, u ^ n * (1 - u ^ 2) ^ m
decls.doc: Simplification of the integral of `sin x ^ m * cos x ^ n`, case `m` is odd.

decls.name: integral_sin_mul_cos₂
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_mul_cos₂ : ∫ x in a..b, sin x * cos x = (cos a ^ 2 - cos b ^ 2) / 2
decls.doc: The integral of `sin x * cos x`, given in terms of cos². See `integral_sin_mul_cos₁` above for the integral given in terms of sin².

decls.name: integral_sin_mul_cos_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_mul_cos_sq : ∫ x in a..b, sin x * cos x ^ 2 = (cos a ^ 3 - cos b ^ 3) / 3

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_three
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_three : ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ 3 = cos a - cos b - (cos a ^ 3 - cos b ^ 3) / 3

decls.name: integral_sin_pow_even_mul_cos_pow_even
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_pow_even_mul_cos_pow_even (m n : ℕ) : (∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ (2 * m) * cos x ^ (2 * n)) = ∫ x in a..b, ((1 - cos (2 * x)) / 2) ^ m * ((1 + cos (2 * x)) / 2) ^ n
decls.doc: Simplification of the integral of `sin x ^ m * cos x ^ n`, case `m` and `n` are both even.

decls.name: integral_sin_sq_mul_cos_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_sq_mul_cos_sq : ∫ x in a..b, sin x ^ 2 * cos x ^ 2 = (b - a) / 8 - (sin (4 * b) - sin (4 * a)) / 32

decls.name: integral_sqrt_one_sub_sq
decls.sig: theorem integral_sqrt_one_sub_sq : ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, √(1 - x ^ 2 : ℝ) = π / 2

decls.name: integral_log_sin_zero_pi_div_two
decls.sig: theorem integral_log_sin_zero_pi_div_two : ∫ x in 0..(π / 2), log (sin x) = -log 2 * π / 2
decls.doc: The integral of `log ∘ sin` on `0 … π/2` equals `-log 2 * π / 2`.

decls.name: integral_log_sin_zero_pi
decls.sig: theorem integral_log_sin_zero_pi : ∫ x in 0..π, log (sin x) = -log 2 * π
decls.doc: The integral of `log ∘ sin` on `0 … π` equals `-log 2 * π`.

decls.name: circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₀
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₀ (h : ‖a‖ < 1) : circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1 = 0
decls.doc: If `a : ℂ` has norm smaller than one, then `circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1` vanishes.

decls.name: circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₁
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₁ (h : ‖a‖ = 1) : circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1 = 0
decls.doc: If `a : ℂ` has norm one, then the circle average `circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1` vanishes.

decls.name: circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₂
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const₂ (h : 1 < ‖a‖) : circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1 = log ‖a‖
decls.doc: If `a : ℂ` has norm greater than one, then `circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1` equals `log ‖a‖`.

decls.name: circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_posLog
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_posLog : circleAverage (log ‖· - a‖) 0 1 = log⁺ ‖a‖

decls.doc: Induction principle for intervals of real numbers: if a proposition `P` is true on `[x₀, r * x₀)` and if `P` for `[x₀, r^n * x₀)` implies `P` for `[r^n * x₀, r^(n+1) * x₀)`, then `P` is true for all `x ≥ x₀`.

decls.name: Real.log
decls.sig: noncomputable def log (x : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The real logarithm function, equal to the inverse of the exponential for `x > 0`, to `log |x|` for `x < 0`, and to `0` for `0`. We use this unconventional extension to `(-∞, 0]` as it gives the formula `log (x * y) = log x + log y` for all nonzero `x` and `y`, and the derivative of `log` is `1/x` aw

decls.name: Complex.cpow
decls.sig: noncomputable def cpow (x y : ℂ) : ℂ
decls.doc: The complex power function `x ^ y`, given by `x ^ y = exp(y log x)` (where `log` is the principal determination of the logarithm), unless `x = 0` where one sets `0 ^ 0 = 1` and `0 ^ y = 0` for `y ≠ 0`.

decls.name: Complex.cpow_eq_pow
decls.sig: theorem cpow_eq_pow (x y : ℂ) : cpow x y = x ^ y

decls.name: Complex.cpow_def
decls.sig: theorem cpow_def (x y : ℂ) : x ^ y = if x = 0 then if y = 0 then 1 else 0 else exp (log x * y)

decls.name: Complex.cpow_def_of_ne_zero
decls.sig: theorem cpow_def_of_ne_zero {x : ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) (y : ℂ) : x ^ y = exp (log x * y)

decls.sig: theorem cpow_zero (x : ℂ) : x ^ (0 : ℂ) = 1

decls.name: Complex.cpow_ne_zero_iff
decls.sig: theorem cpow_ne_zero_iff {x y : ℂ} : x ^ y ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ 0 ∨ y = 0

decls.doc: A supporting lemma for the **Phragmen-Lindelöf principle** in a horizontal strip. If `z : ℂ` belongs to a horizontal strip `|Complex.im z| ≤ b`, `b ≤ π / 2`, and `a ≤ 0`, then $$\left|exp^{a\left(e^{z}+e^{-z}\right)}\right| \le e^{a\cos b \exp^{|re z|}}.$$

decls.name: Real.sin_ge_sub_cube

decls.doc: For `0 < x` we have `arctan x < x`. This is `lt_tan` reflected in the diagonal: `tan` lies above the identity on `(0, π / 2)`, hence its inverse lies below it.

decls.name: Complex.tan_add
decls.sig: theorem tan_add {x y : ℂ} (h : ((∀ k : ℤ, x ≠ (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∀ l : ℤ, y ≠ (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, x = (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∃ l : ℤ, y = (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) : tan (x + y) = (tan x + tan y) / (1 - tan x * tan y)

decls.name: Complex.tan_add'
decls.sig: theorem tan_add' {x y : ℂ} (h : (∀ k : ℤ, x ≠ (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∀ l : ℤ, y ≠ (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) : tan (x + y) = (tan x + tan y) / (1 - tan x * tan y)

decls.name: Complex.tan_sub
decls.sig: theorem tan_sub {x y : ℂ} (h : ((∀ k : ℤ, x ≠ (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∀ l : ℤ, y ≠ (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, x = (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∃ l : ℤ, y = (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) : tan (x - y) = (tan x - tan y) / (1 + tan x * tan y)

decls.name: Complex.tan_sub'

decls.name: Complex.tan_two_mul

decls.name: Complex.tan_add_mul_I
decls.sig: theorem tan_add_mul_I {x y : ℂ} (h : ((∀ k : ℤ, x ≠ (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∀ l : ℤ, y * I ≠ (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, x = (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∃ l : ℤ, y * I = (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) : tan (x + y * I) = (tan x + tanh y * I) / (1 - tan x * tanh y * I)

decls.name: Complex.tan_eq
decls.sig: theorem tan_eq {z : ℂ} (h : ((∀ k : ℤ, (z.re : ℂ) ≠ (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∀ l : ℤ, (z.im : ℂ) * I ≠ (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) ∨ (∃ k : ℤ, (z.re : ℂ) = (2 * k + 1) * π / 2) ∧ ∃ l : ℤ, (z.im : ℂ) * I = (2 * l + 1) * π / 2) : tan z = (tan z.re + tanh z.im * I) / (1 - tan z.re * tanh z.im * I)

decls.name: EulerSine.integral_sin_mul_sin_mul_cos_pow_eq
decls.sig: theorem integral_sin_mul_sin_mul_cos_pow_eq (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hz : z ≠ 0) : (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.sin (2 * z * x) * sin x * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (n - 1)) = (n / (2 * z) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ n) - (n - 1) / (2 * z) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (n - 2)

decls.name: EulerSine.integral_cos_mul_cos_pow
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_mul_cos_pow (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hz : z ≠ 0) : (((1 : ℂ) - (4 : ℂ) * z ^ 2 / (n : ℂ) ^ 2) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ n) = (n - 1 : ℂ) / n * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (n - 2)
decls.doc: Note this also holds for `z = 0`, but we do not need this case for `sin_pi_mul_eq`.

decls.name: EulerSine.integral_cos_mul_cos_pow_even
decls.sig: theorem integral_cos_mul_cos_pow_even (n : ℕ) (hz : z ≠ 0) : (((1 : ℂ) - z ^ 2 / ((n : ℂ) + 1) ^ 2) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (2 * n + 2)) = (2 * n + 1 : ℂ) / (2 * n + 2) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (2 * n)
decls.doc: Note this also holds for `z = 0`, but we do not need this case for `sin_pi_mul_eq`.

decls.doc: Relate the integral `cos x ^ n` over `[0, π/2]` to the integral of `sin x ^ n` over `[0, π]`, which is studied in `Mathlib/Analysis/Real/Pi/Wallis.lean` and other places.

decls.sig: theorem sin_pi_mul_eq (z : ℂ) (n : ℕ) : Complex.sin (π * z) = ((π * z * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range n, ((1 : ℂ) - z ^ 2 / ((j : ℂ) + 1) ^ 2)) * ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * x) * (cos x : ℂ) ^ (2 * n)) / (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..π / 2, cos x ^ (2 * n) : ℝ)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumZeroes
decls.sig: noncomputable def sumZeroes (n : ℕ) (P : ℝ[X]) : ℝ
decls.doc: Weighted sum of `P (x)` where `x` goes over `cos ((2 * i + 1) / (2 * n) * π)` for `0 ≤ i < n`.

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumZeroes_sum
decls.sig: theorem sumZeroes_sum (n : ℕ) {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (P : ι → ℝ[X]) : sumZeroes n (∑ i ∈ s, P i) = ∑ i ∈ s, sumZeroes n (P i)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumZeroes_smul
decls.sig: theorem sumZeroes_smul (n : ℕ) (c : ℝ) (P : ℝ[X]) : sumZeroes n (c • P) = c * sumZeroes n P

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumZeroes_T_zero
decls.sig: theorem sumZeroes_T_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : sumZeroes n (T ℝ 0) = π

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumZeroes_T_of_not_dvd
decls.sig: theorem sumZeroes_T_of_not_dvd {n : ℕ} {k : ℤ} (hk : ¬ (2 * n : ℤ) ∣ k) : sumZeroes n (T ℝ k) = 0

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integral_eq_sumZeroes
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_sumZeroes {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} (hn : n ≠ 0) (hP : P.degree < 2 * n) : ∫ x, P.eval x ∂measureT = sumZeroes n P
decls.doc: The integral of a polynomial of degree `< 2 * n` with respect to the weight function `√(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹` supported on `[-1, 1]` is equal to `π` times the average of its values on the points `cos ((2 * i + 1) / (2 * n) * π)` for `0 ≤ i < n`.

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.node
decls.sig: noncomputable def node (n i : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: For `n ≠ 0` and `i ≤ n`, `node n i` is one of the extremal points of the Chebyshev `T` polynomial over the interval `[-1, 1]`.

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.node_eq_one
decls.sig: lemma node_eq_one {n : ℕ} : node n 0 = 1

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.node_eq_neg_one
decls.sig: lemma node_eq_neg_one {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : node n n = -1

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.node_mem_Icc
decls.sig: lemma node_mem_Icc {n i : ℕ} : node n i ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.eval_T_real_node
decls.sig: lemma eval_T_real_node {n i : ℕ} (hi : i ∈ Finset.Iic n) : (T ℝ n).eval (node n i) = (-1) ^ i

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.strictAntiOn_node
decls.sig: lemma strictAntiOn_node (n : ℕ) : StrictAntiOn (node n ·) (Finset.range (n + 1))

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.node_lt
decls.sig: lemma node_lt {n i j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ n) (hij : i < j) : node n j < node n i

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.zero_lt_prod_node_sub_node
decls.sig: lemma zero_lt_prod_node_sub_node {n i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ n) : 0 < (-1) ^ i * ∏ j ∈ (Finset.range (n + 1)).erase i, (node n i - node n j)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumNodes
decls.sig: noncomputable def sumNodes (n : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℝ[X])
decls.doc: For a polynomial `P` and coefficient function `c`, `sumNodes n c P` is a linear combination of `P` evaluated at the `n`'th order Chebyshev nodes, with coefficients taken from `c`.

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumNodes_le_sumNodes_T
decls.sig: theorem sumNodes_le_sumNodes_T {n : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℝ} (hcnonneg : ∀ i ≤ n, 0 ≤ (-1) ^ i * (c i)) {P : ℝ[X]} (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : sumNodes n c P ≤ sumNodes n c (T ℝ n)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.sumNodes_eq_sumNodes_T_iff
decls.sig: theorem sumNodes_eq_sumNodes_T_iff {n : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℝ} (hcpos : ∀ i ≤ n, 0 < (-1) ^ i * (c i)) {P : ℝ[X]} (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : (sumNodes n c P = sumNodes n c (T ℝ n)) ↔ P = T ℝ n

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.coeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one
decls.sig: theorem coeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : P.coeff n ≤ 2 ^ (n - 1)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.leadingCoeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one
decls.sig: theorem leadingCoeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : P.leadingCoeff ≤ 2 ^ (n - 1)

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.coeff_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one
decls.sig: theorem coeff_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : P.coeff n = 2 ^ (n - 1) ↔ P = T ℝ n

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.leadingCoeff_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one
decls.sig: theorem leadingCoeff_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : P.leadingCoeff = 2 ^ (n - 1) ↔ P = T ℝ n

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.eval_iterate_derivative_le_of_forall_abs_le_one
decls.sig: theorem eval_iterate_derivative_le_of_forall_abs_le_one {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} {k : ℕ} {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : (derivative^[k] P).eval x ≤ (derivative^[k] (T ℝ n)).eval x

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.eval_iterate_derivative_eq_iff_of_bounded
decls.sig: theorem eval_iterate_derivative_eq_iff_of_bounded {n : ℕ} {P : ℝ[X]} {k : ℕ} (hk₁ : 0 < k) (hk₂ : k ≤ n) {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 ≤ x) (hPdeg : P.degree ≤ n) (hPbnd : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |P.eval x| ≤ 1) : (derivative^[k] P).eval x = (derivative^[k] (T ℝ n)).eval x ↔ P = T ℝ n

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integral_measureT
decls.sig: theorem integral_measureT (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ∫ x, f x ∂measureT = ∫ x in -1..1, f x * √(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.intervalIntegrable_sqrt_one_sub_sq_inv

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integrable_measureT
decls.sig: theorem integrable_measureT {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) : Integrable f measureT

decls.sig: theorem integral_eval_T_real_measureT_of_ne_zero {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : ∫ x, (T ℝ n).eval x ∂measureT = 0

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integral_eval_T_real_mul_eval_T_real_measureT
decls.sig: theorem integral_eval_T_real_mul_eval_T_real_measureT (n m : ℤ) : ∫ x, (T ℝ n).eval x * (T ℝ m).eval x ∂measureT = ((∫ x, (T ℝ (n + m)).eval x ∂measureT) + (∫ x, (T ℝ (n - m)).eval x ∂measureT)) / 2

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integral_eval_T_real_mul_eval_T_real_measureT_of_ne
decls.sig: theorem integral_eval_T_real_mul_eval_T_real_measureT_of_ne {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≠ m) : ∫ x, (T ℝ n).eval x * (T ℝ m).eval x ∂measureT = 0

decls.sig: theorem integral_eval_T_real_mul_self_measureT_zero : ∫ x, (T ℝ 0).eval x * (T ℝ 0).eval x ∂measureT = π

decls.name: Polynomial.Chebyshev.integral_T_real_mul_self_measureT_of_ne_zero

decls.name: arithGeom
decls.sig: def arithGeom [Mul R] [Add R] (a b u₀ : R) : ℕ → R | 0 => u₀ | n + 1 => a * arithGeom a b u₀ n + b
decls.doc: Arithmetic-geometric sequence with starting value `u₀` and recurrence relation `u (n + 1) = a * u n + b`.

decls.name: arithGeom_zero
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma arithGeom_zero [Mul R] [Add R] : arithGeom a b u₀ 0 = u₀

decls.name: arithGeom_succ

decls.name: arithGeom_eq_add_sum
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_eq_add_sum [CommSemiring R] (n : ℕ) : arithGeom a b u₀ n = a ^ n * u₀ + b * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a ^ k

decls.name: arithGeom_same_eq_sum
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_same_eq_sum [CommSemiring R] (n : ℕ) : arithGeom a b b n = b * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), a ^ k

decls.name: arithGeom_zero_eq_sum
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_zero_eq_sum [CommSemiring R] (n : ℕ) : arithGeom a b 0 n = b * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a ^ k

decls.name: arithGeom_eq
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_eq (ha : a ≠ 1) (n : ℕ) : arithGeom a b u₀ n = a ^ n * (u₀ - (b / (1 - a))) + b / (1 - a)

decls.name: arithGeom_eq'
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_eq' (ha : a ≠ 1) : arithGeom a b u₀ = fun n ↦ a ^ n * (u₀ - (b / (1 - a))) + b / (1 - a)

decls.name: arithGeom_same_eq_mul_div'
decls.sig: lemma arithGeom_same_eq_mul_div' (ha : a ≠ 1) (n : ℕ) : arithGeom a b b n = b * (1 - a ^ (n + 1)) / (1 - a)

decls.name: arithGeom_same_eq_mul_div

decls.name: AmpleSet

decls.doc: A subset of a topological real vector space is ample if the convex hull of each of its connected components is the full space.

decls.doc: The empty set in a vector space is ample.

decls.doc: The union of two ample sets is ample.

decls.doc: A set is ample iff its image under a continuous affine equivalence is.

decls.name: AmpleSet.preimage_iff
decls.sig: theorem preimage_iff {s : Set F} (L : E ≃ᴬ[ℝ] F) : AmpleSet (L ⁻¹' s) ↔ AmpleSet s
decls.doc: A set is ample iff its pre-image under a continuous affine equivalence is.

decls.name: AmpleSet.vadd
decls.sig: theorem vadd [ContinuousAdd E] {s : Set E} (h : AmpleSet s) {y : E} : AmpleSet (y +ᵥ s)
decls.doc: Affine translations of ample sets are ample.

decls.name: AmpleSet.vadd_iff
decls.sig: theorem vadd_iff [ContinuousAdd E] {s : Set E} {y : E} : AmpleSet (y +ᵥ s) ↔ AmpleSet s
decls.doc: A set is ample iff its affine translation is.

decls.doc: Let `E` be a linear subspace in a real vector space. If `E` has codimension at least two, its complement is ample.

decls.name: ConvexOn.exists_affine_le_of_lt
decls.sig: lemma exists_affine_le_of_lt {x : E} {a : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ s) (hax : a < φ x) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : ∃ (l : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℝ), s.domRestrict (re ∘ l) + const s c ≤ s.domRestrict φ ∧ re (l x) + c = a
decls.doc: Let `φ : E → ℝ` be a convex and lower-semicontinuous function on a closed convex subset `s`. For any point `x ∈ s` and `a < φ x`, there exists a continuous affine linear function `f` in `E` such that `f ≤ φ` on `s` and `f x = a`. This is an auxiliary lemma used in the proof of `ConvexOn.sSup_affine_

decls.name: ConvexOn.exists_affine_le_of_lt_real
decls.sig: lemma exists_affine_le_of_lt_real {s : Set ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} {x : ℝ} {a : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ s) (hax : a < f x) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfc : LowerSemicontinuousOn f s) (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) : ∃ (c c' : ℝ), (∀ y ∈ s, c * y + c' ≤ f y) ∧ c * x + c' = a

decls.name: ConvexOn.sSup_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem sSup_affine_eq (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : sSup {f | f ≤ s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℝ), f = s.domRestrict (re ∘ l) + const s c} = s.domRestrict φ
decls.doc: A function `φ : E → ℝ` that is convex and lower-semicontinuous on a closed convex subset `s` is the supremum of a family of functions that are the restrictions to `s` of continuous affine linear functions in `E`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.sSup_of_countable_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem sSup_of_countable_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : ∃ 𝓕' : Set (s → ℝ), 𝓕'.Countable ∧ sSup 𝓕' = s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∀ f ∈ 𝓕', f ≤ s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℝ), f = s.domRestrict (re ∘ l) + const s c
decls.doc: The countable version of `sSup_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.sSup_of_nat_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem sSup_of_nat_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : ∃ (l : ℕ → E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, s.domRestrict (re ∘ (l i)) + const s (c i) ≤ s.domRestrict φ) ∧ ⨆ i, s.domRestrict (re ∘ (l i)) + const s (c i) = s.domRestrict φ
decls.doc: The sequential version of `sSup_of_countable_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.univ_sSup_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem univ_sSup_affine_eq (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : sSup {f | f ≤ φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℝ), f = (re ∘ l) + const E c} = φ
decls.doc: A function `φ : E → ℝ` that is convex and lower-semicontinuous is the supremum of a family of of continuous affine linear functions.

decls.name: ConvexOn.univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : ∃ 𝓕' : Set (E → ℝ), 𝓕'.Countable ∧ sSup 𝓕' = φ ∧ ∀ f ∈ 𝓕', f ≤ φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℝ), f = (re ∘ l) + const E c
decls.doc: The countable version of `univ_sSup_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.univ_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem univ_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : ∃ (l : ℕ → E →L[𝕜] 𝕜) (c : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, re ∘ (l i) + const E (c i) ≤ φ) ∧ ⨆ i, re ∘ (l i) + const E (c i) = φ
decls.doc: The sequential version of `univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_sSup_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_sSup_affine_eq (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : sSup {f | f ≤ s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℝ), f = s.domRestrict l + const s c} = s.domRestrict φ
decls.doc: The real version of `sSup_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : ∃ 𝓕' : Set (s → ℝ), 𝓕'.Countable ∧ sSup 𝓕' = s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∀ f ∈ 𝓕', f ≤ s.domRestrict φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℝ), f = s.domRestrict l + const s c
decls.doc: The real version of `sSup_of_countable_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hsc : IsClosed s) (hφc : LowerSemicontinuousOn φ s) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ s φ) : ∃ (l : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, s.domRestrict (l i) + const s (c i) ≤ s.domRestrict φ) ∧ ⨆ i, s.domRestrict (l i) + const s (c i) = s.domRestrict φ
decls.doc: The real version of `sSup_of_nat_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_univ_sSup_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_univ_sSup_affine_eq (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : sSup {f | f ≤ φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℝ), f = l + const E c} = φ
decls.doc: The real version of `univ_sSup_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : ∃ 𝓕' : Set (E → ℝ), 𝓕'.Countable ∧ sSup 𝓕' = φ ∧ ∀ f ∈ 𝓕', f ≤ φ ∧ ∃ (l : E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℝ), f = l + const E c
decls.doc: The real version of `univ_sSup_of_countable_affine_eq`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.real_univ_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq
decls.sig: theorem real_univ_sSup_of_nat_affine_eq [HereditarilyLindelofSpace E] (hφc : LowerSemicontinuous φ) (hφcv : ConvexOn ℝ univ φ) : ∃ (l : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, (l i) + const E (c i) ≤ φ) ∧ ⨆ i, (l i) + const E (c i) = φ

decls.sig: lemma exists_eq_sum_perm_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : ∃ w : Equiv.Perm n → R, (∀ σ, 0 ≤ w σ) ∧ ∑ σ, w σ = 1 ∧ ∑ σ, w σ • σ.permMatrix R = M
decls.doc: If M is a doubly stochastic matrix, then it is a convex combination of permutation matrices. Note `doublyStochastic_eq_convexHull_permMatrix` shows `doublyStochastic n` is exactly the convex hull of the permutation matrices, and this lemma is instead most useful for accessing the coefficients of eac

decls.doc: **Birkhoff's theorem** The set of doubly stochastic matrices is the convex hull of the permutation matrices. Note `exists_eq_sum_perm_of_mem_doublyStochastic` gives a convex weighting of each permutation matrix directly. To show `doublyStochastic n` is convex, use `convex_doublyStochastic`.

decls.name: offers
decls.sig: theorem offers some compensation. Given a set `s` together with a point `x` in its convex hull, Carathéodory says that one may find an affine-independent family of elements `s` whose convex hull contains `x`. Thus the difference from the case of affine span is that the affine-independent family depends on `x`.

decls.name: Caratheodory.mem_convexHull_erase
