decls.doc: **Carathéodory's convexity theorem**

decls.name: eq_pos_convex_span_of_mem_convexHull
decls.sig: theorem eq_pos_convex_span_of_mem_convexHull {x : E} (hx : x ∈ convexHull 𝕜 s) : ∃ (ι : Sort (u + 1)) (_ : Fintype ι), ∃ (z : ι → E) (w : ι → 𝕜), Set.range z ⊆ s ∧ AffineIndependent 𝕜 z ∧ (∀ i, 0 < w i) ∧ ∑ i, w i = 1 ∧ ∑ i, w i • z i = x

decls.name: Finset.centerMass
decls.sig: def Finset.centerMass (t : Finset ι) (w : ι → R) (z : ι → E) : E
decls.doc: Center of mass of a finite collection of points with prescribed weights. Note that we require neither `0 ≤ w i` nor `∑ w = 1`.

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_empty
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_empty : (∅ : Finset ι).centerMass w z = 0

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_pair
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_pair [DecidableEq ι] (hne : i ≠ j) : ({i, j} : Finset ι).centerMass w z = (w i / (w i + w j)) • z i + (w j / (w i + w j)) • z j

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_insert
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_insert [DecidableEq ι] (ha : i ∉ t) (hw : ∑ j ∈ t, w j ≠ 0) : (insert i t).centerMass w z = (w i / (w i + ∑ j ∈ t, w j)) • z i + ((∑ j ∈ t, w j) / (w i + ∑ j ∈ t, w j)) • t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_singleton
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_singleton (hw : w i ≠ 0) : ({i} : Finset ι).centerMass w z = z i

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_neg_left
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma Finset.centerMass_neg_left : t.centerMass (-w) z = t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_smul_left
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_smul_left {c : R'} [Module R' R] [Module R' E] [SMulCommClass R' R R] [IsScalarTower R' R R] [SMulCommClass R R' E] [IsScalarTower R' R E] (hc : c ≠ 0) : t.centerMass (c • w) z = t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_eq_of_sum_1
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_eq_of_sum_1 (hw : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) : t.centerMass w z = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • z i

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_smul
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_smul : (t.centerMass w fun i => c • z i) = c • t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_segment'
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_segment' (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset ι') (ws : ι → R) (zs : ι → E) (wt : ι' → R) (zt : ι' → E) (hws : ∑ i ∈ s, ws i = 1) (hwt : ∑ i ∈ t, wt i = 1) (a b : R) (hab : a + b = 1) : a • s.centerMass ws zs + b • t.centerMass wt zt = (s.disjSum t).centerMass (Sum.elim (fun i => a * ws i) fun j => b * wt j) (Sum.elim zs zt)
decls.doc: A convex combination of two centers of mass is a center of mass as well. This version deals with two different index types.

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_segment
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_segment (s : Finset ι) (w₁ w₂ : ι → R) (z : ι → E) (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i = 1) (hw₂ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i = 1) (a b : R) (hab : a + b = 1) : a • s.centerMass w₁ z + b • s.centerMass w₂ z = s.centerMass (fun i => a * w₁ i + b * w₂ i) z
decls.doc: A convex combination of two centers of mass is a center of mass as well. This version works if two centers of mass share the set of original points.

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_ite_eq
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_ite_eq [DecidableEq ι] (hi : i ∈ t) : t.centerMass (fun j => if i = j then (1 : R) else 0) z = z i

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_subset
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_subset {t' : Finset ι} (ht : t ⊆ t') (h : ∀ i ∈ t', i ∉ t → w i = 0) : t.centerMass w z = t'.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_filter_ne_zero
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centerMass_filter_ne_zero [∀ i, Decidable (w i ≠ 0)] : {i ∈ t | w i ≠ 0}.centerMass w z = t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_le_sup
decls.sig: theorem centerMass_le_sup {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → α} {w : ι → R} (hw₀ : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w i) (hw₁ : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, w i) : s.centerMass w f ≤ s.sup' (nonempty_of_ne_empty <| by rintro rfl; simp at hw₁) f

decls.name: Finset.inf_le_centerMass
decls.sig: theorem inf_le_centerMass {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → α} {w : ι → R} (hw₀ : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w i) (hw₁ : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, w i) : s.inf' (nonempty_of_ne_empty <| by rintro rfl; simp at hw₁) f ≤ s.centerMass w f

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_const
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_const (hw : ∑ j ∈ t, w j ≠ 0) (c : E) : t.centerMass w (Function.const _ c) = c

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_congr
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_congr [DecidableEq ι] {t' : Finset ι} {w' : ι → R} {z' : ι → E} (h : ∀ i, (i ∈ t ∧ w i ≠ 0 ∨ i ∈ t' ∧ w' i ≠ 0) → i ∈ t ∩ t' ∧ w i = w' i ∧ z i = z' i) : t.centerMass w z = t'.centerMass w' z'

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_congr_finset
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_congr_finset [DecidableEq ι] {t' : Finset ι} (h : ∀ i ∈ t ∪ t', w i ≠ 0 → i ∈ t ∩ t') : t.centerMass w z = t'.centerMass w z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_congr_weights
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_congr_weights {w' : ι → R} (h : ∀ i ∈ t, w i = w' i) : t.centerMass w z = t.centerMass w' z

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_congr_fun
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_congr_fun {z' : ι → E} (h : ∀ i ∈ t, w i ≠ 0 → z i = z' i) : t.centerMass w z = t.centerMass w z'

decls.name: Finset.centerMass_of_sum_add_sum_eq_zero
decls.sig: lemma Finset.centerMass_of_sum_add_sum_eq_zero {s t : Finset ι} (hw : ∑ i ∈ s, w i + ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 0) (hz : ∑ i ∈ s, w i • z i + ∑ i ∈ t, w i • z i = 0) : s.centerMass w z = t.centerMass w z

decls.name: Convex.centerMass_mem
decls.sig: theorem Convex.centerMass_mem (hs : Convex R s) : (∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) → (0 < ∑ i ∈ t, w i) → (∀ i ∈ t, z i ∈ s) → t.centerMass w z ∈ s
decls.doc: The center of mass of a finite subset of a convex set belongs to the set provided that all weights are non-negative, and the total weight is positive.

decls.name: Convex.sum_mem

decls.name: convex_iff_sum_mem

decls.name: Finset.centroid_mem_convexHull
decls.sig: theorem Finset.centroid_mem_convexHull (s : Finset E) (hs : s.Nonempty) : s.centroid R id ∈ convexHull R (s : Set E)

decls.name: convexHull_range_eq_exists_affineCombination
decls.sig: theorem convexHull_range_eq_exists_affineCombination (v : ι → E) : convexHull R (range v) = { x | ∃ (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → R), (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ w i) ∧ s.sum w = 1 ∧ s.affineCombination R v w = x }

decls.name: convexHull_eq
decls.sig: theorem convexHull_eq (s : Set E) : convexHull R s = { x : E | ∃ (ι : Type) (t : Finset ι) (w : ι → R) (z : ι → E), (∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) ∧ ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1 ∧ (∀ i ∈ t, z i ∈ s) ∧ t.centerMass w z = x }
decls.doc: Convex hull of `s` is equal to the set of all centers of masses of `Finset`s `t`, `z '' t ⊆ s`. For universe reasons, you shouldn't use this lemma to prove that a given center of mass belongs to the convex hull. Use convexity of the convex hull instead.

decls.name: mem_convexHull_of_exists_fintype
decls.sig: lemma mem_convexHull_of_exists_fintype {s : Set E} {x : E} [Fintype ι] (w : ι → R) (z : ι → E) (hw₀ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hw₁ : ∑ i, w i = 1) (hz : ∀ i, z i ∈ s) (hx : ∑ i, w i • z i = x) : x ∈ convexHull R s
decls.doc: Universe polymorphic version of the reverse implication of `mem_convexHull_iff_exists_fintype`.

decls.name: mem_convexHull_iff_exists_fintype
decls.sig: lemma mem_convexHull_iff_exists_fintype {s : Set E} {x : E} : x ∈ convexHull R s ↔ ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (w : ι → R) (z : ι → E), (∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) ∧ ∑ i, w i = 1 ∧ (∀ i, z i ∈ s) ∧ ∑ i, w i • z i = x
decls.doc: The convex hull of `s` is equal to the set of centers of masses of finite families of points in `s`. For universe reasons, you shouldn't use this lemma to prove that a given center of mass belongs to the convex hull. Use `mem_convexHull_of_exists_fintype` of the convex hull instead.

decls.name: Finset.convexHull_eq
decls.sig: theorem Finset.convexHull_eq (s : Finset E) : convexHull R ↑s = { x : E | ∃ w : E → R, (∀ y ∈ s, 0 ≤ w y) ∧ ∑ y ∈ s, w y = 1 ∧ s.centerMass w id = x }

decls.name: Finset.mem_convexHull
decls.sig: theorem Finset.mem_convexHull {s : Finset E} {x : E} : x ∈ convexHull R (s : Set E) ↔ ∃ w : E → R, (∀ y ∈ s, 0 ≤ w y) ∧ ∑ y ∈ s, w y = 1 ∧ s.centerMass w id = x

decls.name: Finset.mem_convexHull'
decls.sig: lemma Finset.mem_convexHull' {s : Finset E} {x : E} : x ∈ convexHull R (s : Set E) ↔ ∃ w : E → R, (∀ y ∈ s, 0 ≤ w y) ∧ ∑ y ∈ s, w y = 1 ∧ ∑ y ∈ s, w y • y = x
decls.doc: This is a version of `Finset.mem_convexHull` stated without `Finset.centerMass`.

decls.name: Set.Finite.convexHull_eq
decls.sig: theorem Set.Finite.convexHull_eq {s : Set E} (hs : s.Finite) : convexHull R s = { x : E | ∃ w : E → R, (∀ y ∈ s, 0 ≤ w y) ∧ ∑ y ∈ hs.toFinset, w y = 1 ∧ hs.toFinset.centerMass w id = x }

decls.name: convexHull_eq_union_convexHull_finite_subsets

decls.name: convexHull_prod

decls.name: convexHull_add

decls.name: doublyStochastic
decls.sig: def doublyStochastic (R n : Type*) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Semiring R] [PartialOrder R] [IsOrderedRing R] : Submonoid (Matrix n n R) where
decls.doc: A square matrix is doubly stochastic iff all entries are nonnegative, and left or right multiplication by the vector of all 1s gives the vector of all 1s.

decls.name: mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma mem_doublyStochastic : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n ↔ (∀ i j, 0 ≤ M i j) ∧ M *ᵥ 1 = 1 ∧ 1 ᵥ* M = 1

decls.name: mem_doublyStochastic_iff_sum
decls.sig: lemma mem_doublyStochastic_iff_sum : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n ↔ (∀ i j, 0 ≤ M i j) ∧ (∀ i, ∑ j, M i j = 1) ∧ ∀ j, ∑ i, M i j = 1

decls.name: doublyStochastic_eq_rowStochastic_inf_colStochastic
decls.sig: lemma doublyStochastic_eq_rowStochastic_inf_colStochastic : doublyStochastic R n = rowStochastic R n ⊓ colStochastic R n
decls.doc: A matrix is doubly stochastic if and only if it is both row and column stochastic.

decls.name: mem_doublyStochastic_iff_mem_rowStochastic_and_mem_colStochastic
decls.sig: lemma mem_doublyStochastic_iff_mem_rowStochastic_and_mem_colStochastic {M : Matrix n n R} : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n ↔ M ∈ rowStochastic R n ∧ M ∈ colStochastic R n

decls.name: nonneg_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma nonneg_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) {i j : n} : 0 ≤ M i j
decls.doc: Every entry of a doubly stochastic matrix is nonnegative.

decls.name: sum_row_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma sum_row_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) (i : n) : ∑ j, M i j = 1
decls.doc: Each row sum of a doubly stochastic matrix is 1.

decls.name: sum_col_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma sum_col_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) (j : n) : ∑ i, M i j = 1
decls.doc: Each column sum of a doubly stochastic matrix is 1.

decls.name: mulVec_one_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma mulVec_one_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : M *ᵥ 1 = 1
decls.doc: A doubly stochastic matrix multiplied with the all-ones column vector is 1.

decls.name: one_vecMul_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma one_vecMul_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : 1 ᵥ* M = 1
decls.doc: The all-ones row vector multiplied with a doubly stochastic matrix is 1.

decls.name: le_one_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma le_one_of_mem_doublyStochastic (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) {i j : n} : M i j ≤ 1
decls.doc: Every entry of a doubly stochastic matrix is less than or equal to 1.

decls.name: convex_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma convex_doublyStochastic : Convex R (doublyStochastic R n : Set (Matrix n n R))
decls.doc: The set of doubly stochastic matrices is convex.

decls.name: permMatrix_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma permMatrix_mem_doublyStochastic {σ : Equiv.Perm n} : σ.permMatrix R ∈ doublyStochastic R n
decls.doc: Any permutation matrix is doubly stochastic.

decls.name: transpose_mem_doublyStochastic_iff
decls.sig: lemma transpose_mem_doublyStochastic_iff : Mᵀ ∈ doublyStochastic R n ↔ M ∈ doublyStochastic R n
decls.doc: A matrix is doubly stochastic iff its transpose is doubly stochastic

decls.name: reindex_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma reindex_mem_doublyStochastic {m : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] {M : Matrix n n R} {e₁ e₂ : n ≃ m} (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : M.reindex e₁ e₂ ∈ doublyStochastic R m
decls.doc: Reindexing a matrix preserves double stochasticity.

decls.name: reindex_mem_doublyStochastic_iff
decls.sig: lemma reindex_mem_doublyStochastic_iff {m : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] {M : Matrix n n R} {e₁ e₂ : n ≃ m} : M.reindex e₁ e₂ ∈ doublyStochastic R m ↔ M ∈ doublyStochastic R n
decls.doc: Reindexing a matrix preserves double stochasticity.

decls.name: sum_mulVec_of_mem_doublyStochastic
decls.sig: lemma sum_mulVec_of_mem_doublyStochastic {M : Matrix n n R} {x : n → R} (hA : M ∈ doublyStochastic R n) : ∑ i, (M *ᵥ x) i = ∑ i, x i
decls.doc: Applying a doubly stochastic matrix to a vector preserves its sum.

decls.name: exists_mem_doublyStochastic_eq_smul_iff
decls.sig: lemma exists_mem_doublyStochastic_eq_smul_iff {M : Matrix n n R} {s : R} (hs : 0 ≤ s) : (∃ M' ∈ doublyStochastic R n, M = s • M') ↔ (∀ i j, 0 ≤ M i j) ∧ (∀ i, ∑ j, M i j = s) ∧ (∀ j, ∑ i, M i j = s)
decls.doc: A matrix is `s` times a doubly stochastic matrix iff all entries are nonnegative, and all row and column sums are equal to `s`. This lemma is useful for the proof of Birkhoff's theorem - in particular because it allows scaling by nonnegative factors rather than positive ones only.

decls.name: egauge
decls.sig: noncomputable def egauge (𝕜 : Type*) [ENorm 𝕜] {E : Type*} [SMul 𝕜 E] (s : Set E) (x : E) : ℝ≥0∞
decls.doc: The Minkowski functional for vector spaces over normed fields. Given a set `s` in a vector space over a normed field `𝕜`, `egauge s` is the functional which sends `x : E` to the infimum of `‖c‖ₑ` over `c` such that `x` belongs to `s` scaled by `c`. The definition only requires `𝕜` to have a `ENorm`

decls.name: Set.MapsTo.egauge_le
decls.sig: lemma Set.MapsTo.egauge_le {E' F : Type*} [SMul 𝕜 E'] [FunLike F E E'] [MulActionHomClass F 𝕜 E E'] (f : F) {t : Set E'} (h : MapsTo f s t) (x : E) : egauge 𝕜 t (f x) ≤ egauge 𝕜 s x

decls.name: egauge_anti
decls.sig: lemma egauge_anti (h : s ⊆ t) (x : E) : egauge 𝕜 t x ≤ egauge 𝕜 s x

decls.name: egauge_empty
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma egauge_empty (x : E) : egauge 𝕜 ∅ x = ∞

decls.name: egauge_le_of_mem_smul
decls.sig: lemma egauge_le_of_mem_smul (h : x ∈ c • s) : egauge 𝕜 s x ≤ ‖c‖ₑ

decls.name: le_egauge_iff
decls.sig: lemma le_egauge_iff : r ≤ egauge 𝕜 s x ↔ ∀ c : 𝕜, x ∈ c • s → r ≤ ‖c‖ₑ

decls.name: egauge_eq_top
decls.sig: lemma egauge_eq_top : egauge 𝕜 s x = ∞ ↔ ∀ c : 𝕜, x ∉ c • s

decls.name: egauge_lt_iff
decls.sig: lemma egauge_lt_iff : egauge 𝕜 s x < r ↔ ∃ c : 𝕜, x ∈ c • s ∧ ‖c‖ₑ < r

decls.name: egauge_union
decls.sig: lemma egauge_union (s t : Set E) (x : E) : egauge 𝕜 (s ∪ t) x = egauge 𝕜 s x ⊓ egauge 𝕜 t x

decls.name: le_egauge_inter
decls.sig: lemma le_egauge_inter (s t : Set E) (x : E) : egauge 𝕜 s x ⊔ egauge 𝕜 t x ≤ egauge 𝕜 (s ∩ t) x

decls.name: le_egauge_pi
decls.sig: lemma le_egauge_pi {ι : Type*} {E : ι → Type*} [∀ i, SMul 𝕜 (E i)] {I : Set ι} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ I) (s : ∀ i, Set (E i)) (x : ∀ i, E i) : egauge 𝕜 (s i) (x i) ≤ egauge 𝕜 (I.pi s) x

decls.name: le_egauge_prod
decls.sig: lemma le_egauge_prod (s : Set E) (t : Set F) (a : E) (b : F) : max (egauge 𝕜 s a) (egauge 𝕜 t b) ≤ egauge 𝕜 (s ×ˢ t) (a, b)

decls.name: egauge_zero_left_eq_top
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma egauge_zero_left_eq_top : egauge 𝕜 0 x = ∞ ↔ x ≠ 0

decls.name: gauge
decls.sig: def gauge (s : Set E) (x : E) : ℝ
decls.doc: The Minkowski functional. Given a set `s` in a real vector space, `gauge s` is the functional which sends `x : E` to the smallest `r : ℝ` such that `x` is in `s` scaled by `r`.

decls.name: gauge_def
decls.sig: theorem gauge_def : gauge s x = sInf ({ r ∈ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) | x ∈ r • s })

decls.name: gauge_def'
decls.sig: theorem gauge_def' : gauge s x = sInf {r ∈ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) | r⁻¹ • x ∈ s}
decls.doc: An alternative definition of the gauge using scalar multiplication on the element rather than on the set.

decls.name: Absorbent.gauge_set_nonempty
decls.sig: theorem Absorbent.gauge_set_nonempty (absorbs : Absorbent ℝ s) : { r : ℝ | 0 < r ∧ x ∈ r • s }.Nonempty
decls.doc: If the given subset is `Absorbent` then the set we take an infimum over in `gauge` is nonempty, which is useful for proving many properties about the gauge.

decls.name: gauge_mono
decls.sig: theorem gauge_mono (hs : Absorbent ℝ s) (h : s ⊆ t) : gauge t ≤ gauge s

decls.name: exists_lt_of_gauge_lt
decls.sig: theorem exists_lt_of_gauge_lt (absorbs : Absorbent ℝ s) (h : gauge s x < a) : ∃ b, 0 < b ∧ b < a ∧ x ∈ b • s

decls.name: gauge_zero
decls.sig: theorem gauge_zero : gauge s 0 = 0
decls.doc: The gauge evaluated at `0` is always zero (mathematically this requires `0` to be in the set `s` but, the real infimum of the empty set in Lean being defined as `0`, it holds unconditionally).

decls.name: gauge_zero'
decls.sig: theorem gauge_zero' : gauge (0 : Set E) = 0

decls.name: gauge_empty
decls.sig: theorem gauge_empty : gauge (∅ : Set E) = 0

decls.name: gauge_of_subset_zero
decls.sig: theorem gauge_of_subset_zero (h : s ⊆ 0) : gauge s = 0

decls.name: gauge_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem gauge_nonneg (x : E) : 0 ≤ gauge s x
decls.doc: The gauge is always nonnegative.

decls.name: gauge_neg
decls.sig: theorem gauge_neg (symmetric : ∀ x ∈ s, -x ∈ s) (x : E) : gauge s (-x) = gauge s x

decls.name: gauge_neg_set_neg
decls.sig: theorem gauge_neg_set_neg (x : E) : gauge (-s) (-x) = gauge s x

decls.name: gauge_neg_set_eq_gauge_neg
decls.sig: theorem gauge_neg_set_eq_gauge_neg (x : E) : gauge (-s) x = gauge s (-x)

decls.name: gauge_le_of_mem

decls.name: setOfPred_gauge_le_eq

decls.doc: If a family is convex independent, so is any subfamily given by composition of an embedding into index type with the original family.

decls.name: ConvexIndependent.subtype
decls.sig: protected theorem ConvexIndependent.subtype {p : ι → E} (hc : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p) (s : Set ι) : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 fun i : s => p i
decls.doc: If a family is convex independent, so is any subfamily indexed by a subtype of the index type.

decls.name: ConvexIndependent.range
decls.sig: protected theorem ConvexIndependent.range {p : ι → E} (hc : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p) : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : Set.range p → E)
decls.doc: If an indexed family of points is convex independent, so is the corresponding set of points.

decls.name: ConvexIndependent.mono
decls.sig: protected theorem ConvexIndependent.mono {s t : Set E} (hc : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : t → E)) (hs : s ⊆ t) : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : s → E)
decls.doc: A subset of a convex independent set of points is convex independent as well.

decls.name: Function.Injective.convexIndependent_iff_set
decls.sig: theorem Function.Injective.convexIndependent_iff_set {p : ι → E} (hi : Function.Injective p) : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : Set.range p → E) ↔ ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p
decls.doc: The range of an injective indexed family of points is convex independent iff that family is.

decls.name: ConvexIndependent.mem_convexHull_iff
decls.sig: protected theorem ConvexIndependent.mem_convexHull_iff {p : ι → E} (hc : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p) (s : Set ι) (i : ι) : p i ∈ convexHull 𝕜 (p '' s) ↔ i ∈ s
decls.doc: If a family is convex independent, a point in the family is in the convex hull of some of the points given by a subset of the index type if and only if the point's index is in this subset.

decls.name: convexIndependent_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff
decls.sig: theorem convexIndependent_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff {p : ι → E} : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p ↔ ∀ i s, p i ∉ convexHull 𝕜 (p '' (s \ {i}))
decls.doc: If a family is convex independent, a point in the family is not in the convex hull of the other points. See `convexIndependent_set_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff` for the `Set` version.

decls.name: convexIndependent_set_iff_inter_convexHull_subset
decls.sig: theorem convexIndependent_set_iff_inter_convexHull_subset {s : Set E} : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : s → E) ↔ ∀ t, t ⊆ s → s ∩ convexHull 𝕜 t ⊆ t

decls.name: convexIndependent_set_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff
decls.sig: theorem convexIndependent_set_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff {s : Set E} : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 ((↑) : s → E) ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, x ∉ convexHull 𝕜 (s \ {x})
decls.doc: If a set is convex independent, a point in the set is not in the convex hull of the other points. See `convexIndependent_iff_notMem_convexHull_sdiff` for the indexed family version.

decls.name: convexIndependent_iff_finset
decls.sig: theorem convexIndependent_iff_finset {p : ι → E} : ConvexIndependent 𝕜 p ↔ ∀ (s : Finset ι) (x : ι), p x ∈ convexHull 𝕜 (s.image p : Set E) → x ∈ s
decls.doc: To check convex independence, one only has to check finsets thanks to Carathéodory's theorem.

decls.name: Convex.convexIndependent_extremePoints

decls.name: Convex.integral_mem

decls.name: ae_eq_const_or_exists_average_ne_compl
decls.sig: theorem ae_eq_const_or_exists_average_ne_compl [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hfi : Integrable f μ) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ ∃ t, MeasurableSet t ∧ μ t ≠ 0 ∧ μ tᶜ ≠ 0 ∧ (⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ) ≠ ⨍ x in tᶜ, f x ∂μ
decls.doc: If `f : α → E` is an integrable function, then either it is a.e. equal to the constant `⨍ x, f x ∂μ` or there exists a measurable set such that `μ t ≠ 0`, `μ tᶜ ≠ 0`, and the average values of `f` over `t` and `tᶜ` are different.

decls.name: Convex.average_mem_interior_of_set
decls.sig: theorem Convex.average_mem_interior_of_set [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hs : Convex ℝ s) (h0 : μ t ≠ 0) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) (ht : (⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ) ∈ interior s) : (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∈ interior s
decls.doc: If an integrable function `f : α → E` takes values in a convex set `s` and for some set `t` of positive measure, the average value of `f` over `t` belongs to the interior of `s`, then the average of `f` over the whole space belongs to the interior of `s`.

decls.name: StrictConvex.ae_eq_const_or_average_mem_interior
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvex.ae_eq_const_or_average_mem_interior [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hs : StrictConvex ℝ s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∈ interior s
decls.doc: If an integrable function `f : α → E` takes values in a strictly convex closed set `s`, then either it is a.e. equal to its average value, or its average value belongs to the interior of `s`.

decls.name: StrictConvexOn.ae_eq_const_or_map_average_lt
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvexOn.ae_eq_const_or_map_average_lt [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hg : StrictConvexOn ℝ s g) (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ g (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) < ⨍ x, g (f x) ∂μ
decls.doc: **Jensen's inequality**, strict version: if an integrable function `f : α → E` takes values in a convex closed set `s`, and `g : E → ℝ` is continuous and strictly convex on `s`, then either `f` is a.e. equal to its average value, or `g (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) < ⨍ x, g (f x) ∂μ`.

decls.name: StrictConcaveOn.ae_eq_const_or_lt_map_average
decls.sig: theorem StrictConcaveOn.ae_eq_const_or_lt_map_average [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hg : StrictConcaveOn ℝ s g) (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ (⨍ x, g (f x) ∂μ) < g (⨍ x, f x ∂μ)
decls.doc: **Jensen's inequality**, strict version: if an integrable function `f : α → E` takes values in a convex closed set `s`, and `g : E → ℝ` is continuous and strictly concave on `s`, then either `f` is a.e. equal to its average value, or `⨍ x, g (f x) ∂μ < g (⨍ x, f x ∂μ)`.

decls.name: ae_eq_const_or_norm_average_lt_of_norm_le_const
decls.sig: theorem ae_eq_const_or_norm_average_lt_of_norm_le_const [StrictConvexSpace ℝ E] (h_le : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ ‖⨍ x, f x ∂μ‖ < C
decls.doc: If `E` is a strictly convex normed space and `f : α → E` is a function such that `‖f x‖ ≤ C` a.e., then either this function is a.e. equal to its average value, or the norm of its average value is strictly less than `C`.

decls.name: ae_eq_const_or_norm_integral_lt_of_norm_le_const
decls.sig: theorem ae_eq_const_or_norm_integral_lt_of_norm_le_const [StrictConvexSpace ℝ E] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (h_le : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ ‖∫ x, f x ∂μ‖ < μ.real univ * C
decls.doc: If `E` is a strictly convex normed space and `f : α → E` is a function such that `‖f x‖ ≤ C` a.e., then either this function is a.e. equal to its average value, or the norm of its integral is strictly less than `μ.real univ * C`.

decls.name: ae_eq_const_or_norm_setIntegral_lt_of_norm_le_const
decls.sig: theorem ae_eq_const_or_norm_setIntegral_lt_of_norm_le_const [StrictConvexSpace ℝ E] (ht : μ t ≠ ∞) (h_le : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ.restrict t, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) : f =ᵐ[μ.restrict t] const α (⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ) ∨ ‖∫ x in t, f x ∂μ‖ < μ.real t * C
decls.doc: If `E` is a strictly convex normed space and `f : α → E` is a function such that `‖f x‖ ≤ C` a.e. on a set `t` of finite measure, then either this function is a.e. equal to its average value on `t`, or the norm of its integral over `t` is strictly less than `μ.real t * C`.

decls.name: intrinsicInterior

decls.doc: The intrinsic interior of a set is its interior considered as a set in its affine span.

decls.name: mem_intrinsicFrontier

decls.name: mem_intrinsicClosure

decls.name: QuasiconvexOn
decls.sig: def QuasiconvexOn : Prop
decls.doc: A function is quasiconvex if all its sublevels are convex. This means that, for all `r`, `{x ∈ s | f x ≤ r}` is `𝕜`-convex.

decls.name: QuasiconcaveOn
decls.sig: def QuasiconcaveOn : Prop
decls.doc: A function is quasiconcave if all its superlevels are convex. This means that, for all `r`, `{x ∈ s | r ≤ f x}` is `𝕜`-convex.

decls.name: QuasilinearOn
decls.sig: def QuasilinearOn : Prop
decls.doc: A function is quasilinear if it is both quasiconvex and quasiconcave. This means that, for all `r`, the sets `{x ∈ s | f x ≤ r}` and `{x ∈ s | r ≤ f x}` are `𝕜`-convex.

decls.name: segment
decls.sig: def segment (x y : E) : Set E
decls.doc: Segments in a vector space. Denoted as `[x -[𝕜] y]` within the `Convex` namespace.

decls.name: openSegment
decls.sig: def openSegment (x y : E) : Set E
decls.doc: Open segment in a vector space. Note that `openSegment 𝕜 x x = {x}` instead of being `∅` when the base semiring has some element between `0` and `1`.

decls.name: segment_eq_image₂
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_image₂ (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] = (fun p : 𝕜 × 𝕜 => p.1 • x + p.2 • y) '' { p | 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.1 + p.2 = 1 }

decls.name: openSegment_eq_image₂
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_image₂ (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = (fun p : 𝕜 × 𝕜 => p.1 • x + p.2 • y) '' { p | 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ p.1 + p.2 = 1 }

decls.name: segment_symm
decls.sig: theorem segment_symm (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] = [y -[𝕜] x]

decls.name: openSegment_symm
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_symm (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = openSegment 𝕜 y x

decls.name: openSegment_subset_segment
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_subset_segment (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y ⊆ [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.name: segment_subset_iff
decls.sig: theorem segment_subset_iff : [x -[𝕜] y] ⊆ s ↔ ∀ a b : 𝕜, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 → a • x + b • y ∈ s

decls.name: openSegment_subset_iff
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_subset_iff : openSegment 𝕜 x y ⊆ s ↔ ∀ a b : 𝕜, 0 < a → 0 < b → a + b = 1 → a • x + b • y ∈ s

decls.name: left_mem_segment
decls.sig: theorem left_mem_segment (x y : E) : x ∈ [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.name: right_mem_segment
decls.sig: theorem right_mem_segment (x y : E) : y ∈ [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.name: segment_same
decls.sig: theorem segment_same (x : E) : [x -[𝕜] x] = {x}

decls.name: insert_endpoints_openSegment
decls.sig: theorem insert_endpoints_openSegment (x y : E) : insert x (insert y (openSegment 𝕜 x y)) = [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.name: mem_openSegment_of_ne_left_right
decls.sig: theorem mem_openSegment_of_ne_left_right (hx : x ≠ z) (hy : y ≠ z) (hz : z ∈ [x -[𝕜] y]) : z ∈ openSegment 𝕜 x y

decls.name: openSegment_subset_iff_segment_subset
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_subset_iff_segment_subset (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : openSegment 𝕜 x y ⊆ s ↔ [x -[𝕜] y] ⊆ s

decls.name: segment.lift
decls.sig: theorem segment.lift [SMulPosMono R 𝕜] (x y : E) : segment R x y ⊆ segment 𝕜 x y

decls.name: openSegment.lift
decls.sig: theorem openSegment.lift [Nontrivial 𝕜] [SMulPosStrictMono R 𝕜] (x y : E) : openSegment R x y ⊆ openSegment 𝕜 x y

decls.name: openSegment_same
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_same (x : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x x = {x}

decls.name: segment_eq_image
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_image (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] = (fun θ : 𝕜 => (1 - θ) • x + θ • y) '' Icc (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: openSegment_eq_image
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_image (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = (fun θ : 𝕜 => (1 - θ) • x + θ • y) '' Ioo (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: segment_eq_image'
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_image' (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] = (fun θ : 𝕜 => x + θ • (y - x)) '' Icc (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: openSegment_eq_image'
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_image' (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = (fun θ : 𝕜 => x + θ • (y - x)) '' Ioo (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: segment_eq_image_lineMap
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_image_lineMap (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] = AffineMap.lineMap x y '' Icc (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: openSegment_eq_image_lineMap
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_image_lineMap (x y : E) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = AffineMap.lineMap x y '' Ioo (0 : 𝕜) 1

decls.name: lineMap_mem_openSegment
decls.sig: theorem lineMap_mem_openSegment (a b : E) {t : 𝕜} (ht : t ∈ Ioo 0 1) : AffineMap.lineMap a b t ∈ openSegment 𝕜 a b

decls.name: lineMap_mem_segment
decls.sig: theorem lineMap_mem_segment (a b : E) {t : 𝕜} (ht : t ∈ Icc 0 1) : AffineMap.lineMap a b t ∈ [a -[𝕜] b]

decls.name: image_segment
decls.sig: theorem image_segment (f : E →ᵃ[𝕜] F) (a b : E) : f '' [a -[𝕜] b] = [f a -[𝕜] f b]

decls.name: image_openSegment
decls.sig: theorem image_openSegment (f : E →ᵃ[𝕜] F) (a b : E) : f '' openSegment 𝕜 a b = openSegment 𝕜 (f a) (f b)

decls.name: vadd_segment
decls.sig: theorem vadd_segment [AddTorsor G E] [VAddCommClass G E E] (a : G) (b c : E) : a +ᵥ [b -[𝕜] c] = [a +ᵥ b -[𝕜] a +ᵥ c]

decls.name: vadd_openSegment
decls.sig: theorem vadd_openSegment [AddTorsor G E] [VAddCommClass G E E] (a : G) (b c : E) : a +ᵥ openSegment 𝕜 b c = openSegment 𝕜 (a +ᵥ b) (a +ᵥ c)

decls.name: mem_segment_translate
decls.sig: theorem mem_segment_translate (a : E) {x b c} : a + x ∈ [a + b -[𝕜] a + c] ↔ x ∈ [b -[𝕜] c]

decls.name: mem_openSegment_translate
decls.sig: theorem mem_openSegment_translate (a : E) {x b c : E} : a + x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 (a + b) (a + c) ↔ x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 b c

decls.name: segment_translate_preimage
decls.sig: theorem segment_translate_preimage (a b c : E) : (fun x => a + x) ⁻¹' [a + b -[𝕜] a + c] = [b -[𝕜] c]

decls.name: openSegment_translate_preimage
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_translate_preimage (a b c : E) : (fun x => a + x) ⁻¹' openSegment 𝕜 (a + b) (a + c) = openSegment 𝕜 b c

decls.name: segment_translate_image
decls.sig: theorem segment_translate_image (a b c : E) : (fun x => a + x) '' [b -[𝕜] c] = [a + b -[𝕜] a + c]

decls.name: openSegment_translate_image
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_translate_image (a b c : E) : (fun x => a + x) '' openSegment 𝕜 b c = openSegment 𝕜 (a + b) (a + c)

decls.name: segment_inter_subset_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_sub
decls.sig: lemma segment_inter_subset_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_sub {c x y : E} (h : LinearIndependent 𝕜 ![x - c, y - c]) : [c -[𝕜] x] ∩ [c -[𝕜] y] ⊆ {c}

decls.name: segment_inter_eq_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_sub
decls.sig: lemma segment_inter_eq_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_sub [ZeroLEOneClass 𝕜] {c x y : E} (h : LinearIndependent 𝕜 ![x - c, y - c]) : [c -[𝕜] x] ∩ [c -[𝕜] y] = {c}

decls.name: sameRay_of_mem_segment
decls.sig: theorem sameRay_of_mem_segment [CommRing 𝕜] [PartialOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] {x y z : E} (h : x ∈ [y -[𝕜] z]) : SameRay 𝕜 (x - y) (z - x)

decls.name: segment_inter_eq_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_of_ne
decls.sig: lemma segment_inter_eq_endpoint_of_linearIndependent_of_ne [CommRing 𝕜] [PartialOrder 𝕜] [IsOrderedRing 𝕜] [IsDomain 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] {x y : E} (h : LinearIndependent 𝕜 ![x, y]) {s t : 𝕜} (hs : s ≠ t) (c : E) : [c + x -[𝕜] c + t • y] ∩ [c + x -[𝕜] c + s • y] = {c + x}

decls.name: midpoint_mem_openSegment
decls.sig: theorem midpoint_mem_openSegment [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : midpoint 𝕜 x y ∈ openSegment 𝕜 x y

decls.name: midpoint_mem_segment
decls.sig: theorem midpoint_mem_segment [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : midpoint 𝕜 x y ∈ [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.name: mem_openSegment_sub_add
decls.sig: theorem mem_openSegment_sub_add [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 (x - y) (x + y)

decls.name: mem_segment_sub_add
decls.sig: theorem mem_segment_sub_add [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : x ∈ [x - y -[𝕜] x + y]

decls.name: mem_openSegment_add_sub
decls.sig: theorem mem_openSegment_add_sub [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 (x + y) (x - y)

decls.name: mem_segment_add_sub
decls.sig: theorem mem_segment_add_sub [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] (x y : E) : x ∈ [x + y -[𝕜] x - y]

decls.name: left_mem_openSegment_iff
decls.sig: theorem left_mem_openSegment_iff [DenselyOrdered 𝕜] [IsTorsionFree 𝕜 E] : x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 x y ↔ x = y

decls.name: right_mem_openSegment_iff
decls.sig: theorem right_mem_openSegment_iff [DenselyOrdered 𝕜] [IsTorsionFree 𝕜 E] : y ∈ openSegment 𝕜 x y ↔ x = y

decls.name: mem_segment_iff_div
decls.sig: theorem mem_segment_iff_div : x ∈ [y -[𝕜] z] ↔ ∃ a b : 𝕜, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ 0 < a + b ∧ (a / (a + b)) • y + (b / (a + b)) • z = x

decls.name: mem_openSegment_iff_div
decls.sig: theorem mem_openSegment_iff_div : x ∈ openSegment 𝕜 y z ↔ ∃ a b : 𝕜, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ (a / (a + b)) • y + (b / (a + b)) • z = x

decls.name: mem_segment_iff_sameRay
decls.sig: theorem mem_segment_iff_sameRay : x ∈ [y -[𝕜] z] ↔ SameRay 𝕜 (x - y) (z - x)

decls.name: openSegment_subset_union
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_subset_union (x y : E) {z : E} (hz : z ∈ range (lineMap x y : 𝕜 → E)) : openSegment 𝕜 x y ⊆ insert z (openSegment 𝕜 x z ∪ openSegment 𝕜 z y)
decls.doc: If `z = lineMap x y c` is a point on the line passing through `x` and `y`, then the open segment `openSegment 𝕜 x y` is included in the union of the open segments `openSegment 𝕜 x z`, `openSegment 𝕜 z y`, and the point `z`. Informally, `(x, y) ⊆ {z} ∪ (x, z) ∪ (z, y)`.

decls.name: segment_subset_uIcc
decls.sig: theorem segment_subset_uIcc (x y : E) : [x -[𝕜] y] ⊆ uIcc x y

decls.sig: theorem Convex.min_le_combo (x y : E) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) : min x y ≤ a • x + b • y

decls.sig: theorem Convex.combo_le_max (x y : E) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) : a • x + b • y ≤ max x y

decls.name: Icc_subset_segment
decls.sig: theorem Icc_subset_segment : Icc x y ⊆ [x -[𝕜] y]

decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_Icc (h : x ≤ y) : [x -[𝕜] y] = Icc x y

decls.name: openSegment_eq_Ioo
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_Ioo (h : x < y) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = Ioo x y

decls.name: segment_eq_Icc'
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_Icc' (x y : 𝕜) : [x -[𝕜] y] = Icc (min x y) (max x y)

decls.name: openSegment_eq_Ioo'
decls.sig: theorem openSegment_eq_Ioo' (hxy : x ≠ y) : openSegment 𝕜 x y = Ioo (min x y) (max x y)

decls.name: segment_eq_uIcc
decls.sig: theorem segment_eq_uIcc (x y : 𝕜) : [x -[𝕜] y] = uIcc x y

decls.name: Convex.mem_Icc
decls.sig: theorem Convex.mem_Icc (h : x ≤ y) : z ∈ Icc x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z
decls.doc: A point is in an `Icc` iff it can be expressed as a convex combination of the endpoints.

decls.name: Convex.mem_Ioo
decls.sig: theorem Convex.mem_Ioo (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ioo x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z
decls.doc: A point is in an `Ioo` iff it can be expressed as a strict convex combination of the endpoints.

decls.name: Convex.mem_Ioc
decls.sig: theorem Convex.mem_Ioc (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ioc x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z
decls.doc: A point is in an `Ioc` iff it can be expressed as a semistrict convex combination of the endpoints.

decls.name: Convex.mem_Ico
decls.sig: theorem Convex.mem_Ico (h : x < y) : z ∈ Ico x y ↔ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 ≤ b ∧ a + b = 1 ∧ a * x + b * y = z
decls.doc: A point is in an `Ico` iff it can be expressed as a semistrict convex combination of the endpoints.

decls.name: AffineSubspace.WSameSide

decls.name: ConvexOn.slope_mono_adjacent
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.slope_mono_adjacent (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f y - f x) / (y - x) ≤ (f z - f y) / (z - y)
decls.doc: If `f : 𝕜 → 𝕜` is convex, then for any three points `x < y < z` the slope of the secant line of `f` on `[x, y]` is less than the slope of the secant line of `f` on `[y, z]`.

decls.sig: theorem strictConcaveOn_iff_slope_strict_anti_adjacent : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f ↔ Convex 𝕜 s ∧ ∀ ⦃x y z : 𝕜⦄, x ∈ s → z ∈ s → x < y → y < z → (f z - f y) / (z - y) < (f y - f x) / (y - x)
decls.doc: A function `f : 𝕜 → 𝕜` is strictly concave iff for any three points `x < y < z` the slope of the secant line of `f` on `[x, y]` is strictly greater than the slope of the secant line of `f` on `[y, z]`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux1
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux1 (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (z - x) * f y ≤ (z - y) * f x + (y - x) * f z

decls.name: ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux2
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux2 (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f y - f x) / (y - x) ≤ (f z - f x) / (z - x)

decls.name: ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux3
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.secant_mono_aux3 (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f z - f x) / (z - x) ≤ (f z - f y) / (z - y)

decls.name: ConvexOn.secant_mono
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.secant_mono (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {a x y : 𝕜} (ha : a ∈ s) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hxa : x ≠ a) (hya : y ≠ a) (hxy : x ≤ y) : (f x - f a) / (x - a) ≤ (f y - f a) / (y - a)
decls.doc: If `f : 𝕜 → 𝕜` is convex, then for any point `a` the slope of the secant line of `f` through `a` and `b ≠ a` is monotone with respect to `b`.

decls.name: StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux1
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux1 (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (z - x) * f y < (z - y) * f x + (y - x) * f z

decls.name: StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux2
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux2 (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f y - f x) / (y - x) < (f z - f x) / (z - x)

decls.name: StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux3
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono_aux3 (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f z - f x) / (z - x) < (f z - f y) / (z - y)

decls.name: StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono
decls.sig: theorem StrictConvexOn.secant_strict_mono (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {a x y : 𝕜} (ha : a ∈ s) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hxa : x ≠ a) (hya : y ≠ a) (hxy : x < y) : (f x - f a) / (x - a) < (f y - f a) / (y - a)
decls.doc: If `f : 𝕜 → 𝕜` is strictly convex, then for any point `a` the slope of the secant line of `f` through `a` and `b` is strictly monotone with respect to `b`.

decls.name: StrictConcaveOn.secant_strict_mono
decls.sig: theorem StrictConcaveOn.secant_strict_mono (hf : StrictConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) {a x y : 𝕜} (ha : a ∈ s) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hxa : x ≠ a) (hya : y ≠ a) (hxy : x < y) : (f y - f a) / (y - a) < (f x - f a) / (x - a)
decls.doc: If `f : 𝕜 → 𝕜` is strictly concave, then for any point `a` the slope of the secant line of `f` through `a` and `b` is strictly antitone with respect to `b`.

decls.name: ConvexOn.strictMonoOn
decls.sig: theorem ConvexOn.strictMonoOn (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) {x y : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hxy' : f x < f y) : StrictMonoOn f (s ∩ Set.Ici y)
decls.doc: If `f` is convex on a set `s` in a linearly ordered field, and `f x < f y` for two points `x < y` in `s`, then `f` is strictly monotone on `s ∩ [y, ∞)`.

decls.name: ConcaveOn.strictMonoOn

decls.doc: If `f` is concave on a set `s` in a linearly ordered field, and `f x < f y` for two points `x < y` in `s`, then `f` is strictly monotone on `s ∩ (∞, x]`.

decls.name: ConcaveOn.strictAntiOn
decls.sig: theorem ConcaveOn.strictAntiOn (hf : ConcaveOn 𝕜 s f) {x y : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hxy' : f y < f x) : StrictAntiOn f (s ∩ .Ici y)
decls.doc: If `f` is concave on a set `s` in a linearly ordered field, and `f y < f x` for two points `x < y` in `s`, then `f` is strictly antitone on `s ∩ [y, ∞)`.

decls.name: StarConvex
decls.sig: def StarConvex (𝕜 : Type*) {E : Type*} [Semiring 𝕜] [PartialOrder 𝕜] [AddCommMonoid E] [SMul 𝕜 E] (x : E) (s : Set E) : Prop
decls.doc: Star-convexity of sets. `s` is star-convex at `x` if every segment from `x` to a point in `s` is contained in `s`.

decls.name: starConvex_iff_segment_subset

decls.name: starConvex_iff_pointwise_add_subset
decls.sig: theorem starConvex_iff_pointwise_add_subset : StarConvex 𝕜 x s ↔ ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 → a • {x} + b • s ⊆ s

decls.name: stdSimplex
decls.sig: def stdSimplex : Set (ι → 𝕜)
decls.doc: The standard simplex in the space of functions `ι → 𝕜` is the set of vectors with non-negative coordinates with total sum `1`. This is the free object in the category of convex spaces.

decls.name: stdSimplex_eq_inter
decls.sig: theorem stdSimplex_eq_inter : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι = (⋂ x, { f | 0 ≤ f x }) ∩ { f | ∑ x, f x = 1 }

decls.name: convex_stdSimplex
decls.sig: theorem convex_stdSimplex [IsOrderedRing 𝕜] : Convex 𝕜 (stdSimplex 𝕜 ι)

decls.name: stdSimplex_of_subsingleton
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplex_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton 𝕜] : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι = univ

decls.name: stdSimplex_of_isEmpty_index
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplex_of_isEmpty_index [IsEmpty ι] [Nontrivial 𝕜] : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι = ∅
decls.doc: The standard simplex in the zero-dimensional space is empty.

decls.name: stdSimplex_unique
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplex_unique [ZeroLEOneClass 𝕜] [Nonempty ι] [Subsingleton ι] : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι = {fun _ ↦ 1}

decls.name: mem_Icc_of_mem_stdSimplex
decls.sig: theorem mem_Icc_of_mem_stdSimplex [IsOrderedAddMonoid 𝕜] {f : ι → 𝕜} (hf : f ∈ stdSimplex 𝕜 ι) (x) : f x ∈ Icc (0 : 𝕜) 1
decls.doc: All values of a function `f ∈ stdSimplex 𝕜 ι` belong to `[0, 1]`.

decls.name: stdSimplex_subset_Icc
decls.sig: theorem stdSimplex_subset_Icc [IsOrderedAddMonoid 𝕜] : stdSimplex 𝕜 ι ⊆ Icc 0 1
decls.doc: `stdSimplex 𝕜 ι` is a subset of the unit cube

decls.name: single_mem_stdSimplex
decls.sig: theorem single_mem_stdSimplex (i : ι) : Pi.single i 1 ∈ stdSimplex 𝕜 ι

decls.name: ite_eq_mem_stdSimplex
decls.sig: theorem ite_eq_mem_stdSimplex (i : ι) : (if i = · then (1 : 𝕜) else 0) ∈ stdSimplex 𝕜 ι

decls.name: segment_single_subset_stdSimplex
decls.sig: lemma segment_single_subset_stdSimplex (i j : ι) : [Pi.single i 1 -[𝕜] Pi.single j 1] ⊆ stdSimplex 𝕜 ι
decls.doc: The edges are contained in the simplex.

decls.name: stdSimplex_fin_two
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplex_fin_two : stdSimplex 𝕜 (Fin 2) = [Pi.single 0 1 -[𝕜] Pi.single 1 1]

decls.name: stdSimplexEquivIcc
decls.sig: def stdSimplexEquivIcc : stdSimplex 𝕜 (Fin 2) ≃ Icc (0 : 𝕜) 1 where
decls.doc: The standard one-dimensional simplex in `Fin 2 → 𝕜` is equivalent to the unit interval. This bijection sends the zeroth vertex `Pi.single 0 1` to `0` and the first vertex `Pi.single 1 1` to `1`.

decls.name: stdSimplexEquivIcc_zero
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplexEquivIcc_zero : stdSimplexEquivIcc 𝕜 ⟨_, single_mem_stdSimplex 𝕜 0⟩ = 0

decls.name: stdSimplexEquivIcc_one
decls.sig: lemma stdSimplexEquivIcc_one : stdSimplexEquivIcc 𝕜 ⟨_, single_mem_stdSimplex 𝕜 1⟩ = 1

decls.name: convexHull_basis_eq_stdSimplex
decls.sig: theorem convexHull_basis_eq_stdSimplex [DecidableEq ι] : convexHull R (range fun i j : ι => if i = j then (1 : R) else 0) = stdSimplex R ι
decls.doc: `stdSimplex 𝕜 ι` is the convex hull of the canonical basis in `ι → 𝕜`.

decls.doc: Strict convexity is equivalent to `‖a • x + b • y‖ < 1` for all `x` and `y` of norm at most `1` and all strictly positive `a` and `b` such that `a + b = 1`. This lemma shows that it suffices to check this for points of norm one and some `a`, `b` such that `a + b = 1`.

decls.name: UniformConvexOn
decls.sig: def UniformConvexOn (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f` from a real normed space is uniformly convex with modulus `φ` if `f (t • x + (1 - t) • y) ≤ t • f x + (1 - t) • f y - t * (1 - t) * φ ‖x - y‖` for all `t ∈ [0, 1]`. `φ` is usually taken to be a monotone function such that `φ r = 0 ↔ r = 0`.

decls.name: UniformConcaveOn
decls.sig: def UniformConcaveOn (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f` from a real normed space is uniformly concave with modulus `φ` if `t • f x + (1 - t) • f y + t * (1 - t) * φ ‖x - y‖ ≤ f (t • x + (1 - t) • y)` for all `t ∈ [0, 1]`. `φ` is usually taken to be a monotone function such that `φ r = 0 ↔ r = 0`.

decls.name: StrongConvexOn
decls.sig: def StrongConvexOn (s : Set E) (m : ℝ) : (E → ℝ) → Prop
decls.doc: A function `f` from a real normed space is `m`-strongly convex if it is uniformly convex with modulus `φ(r) = m / 2 * r ^ 2`. In an inner product space, this is equivalent to `x ↦ f x - m / 2 * ‖x‖ ^ 2` being convex.

decls.name: UniformConvexSpace
decls.sig: class UniformConvexSpace (E : Type*) [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] : Prop where
decls.doc: A *uniformly convex space* is a real normed space where the triangle inequality is strict with a uniform bound. Namely, over the `x` and `y` of norm `1`, `‖x + y‖` is uniformly bounded above by a constant `< 2` when `‖x - y‖` is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant.

decls.name: exists_forall_sphere_dist_add_le_two_sub
decls.sig: theorem exists_forall_sphere_dist_add_le_two_sub (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ ⦃x : E⦄, ‖x‖ = 1 → ∀ ⦃y⦄, ‖y‖ = 1 → ε ≤ ‖x - y‖ → ‖x + y‖ ≤ 2 - δ

decls.name: exists_forall_closed_ball_dist_add_le_two_sub
decls.sig: theorem exists_forall_closed_ball_dist_add_le_two_sub (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ ⦃x : E⦄, ‖x‖ ≤ 1 → ∀ ⦃y⦄, ‖y‖ ≤ 1 → ε ≤ ‖x - y‖ → ‖x + y‖ ≤ 2 - δ

decls.name: exists_forall_closed_ball_dist_add_le_two_mul_sub
decls.sig: theorem exists_forall_closed_ball_dist_add_le_two_mul_sub (hε : 0 < ε) (r : ℝ) : ∃ δ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ ⦃x : E⦄, ‖x‖ ≤ r → ∀ ⦃y⦄, ‖y‖ ≤ r → ε ≤ ‖x - y‖ → ‖x + y‖ ≤ 2 * r - δ

decls.name: IsVisible
decls.sig: def IsVisible (s : Set P) (x y : P) : Prop
decls.doc: Two points are visible to each other through a set if no point of that set lies strictly between them. By convention, a point `x` sees itself through any set `s`, even when `x ∈ s`.

decls.name: IsVisible.rfl
decls.sig: lemma IsVisible.rfl : IsVisible 𝕜 s x x

decls.name: isVisible_comm
decls.sig: lemma isVisible_comm : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y ↔ IsVisible 𝕜 s y x

decls.name: IsVisible.mono
decls.sig: lemma IsVisible.mono (hst : s ⊆ t) (ht : IsVisible 𝕜 t x y) : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y

decls.name: isVisible_iff_lineMap
decls.sig: lemma isVisible_iff_lineMap (hxy : x ≠ y) : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y ↔ ∀ δ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : 𝕜) 1, lineMap x y δ ∉ s

decls.name: IsVisible.of_convexHull_of_pos
decls.sig: lemma IsVisible.of_convexHull_of_pos {ι : Type*} {t : Finset ι} {a : ι → V} {w : ι → 𝕜} (hw₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (ha : ∀ i ∈ t, a i ∈ s) (hx : x ∉ convexHull 𝕜 s) (hw : IsVisible 𝕜 (convexHull 𝕜 s) x (∑ i ∈ t, w i • a i)) {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ t) (hwi : 0 < w i) : IsVisible 𝕜 (convexHull 𝕜 s) x (a i)
decls.doc: If a point `x` sees a convex combination of points of a set `s` through `convexHull ℝ s ∌ x`, then it sees all terms of that combination. Note that the converse does not hold.

decls.name: IsVisible.eq_of_mem_interior
decls.sig: lemma IsVisible.eq_of_mem_interior (hsxy : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y) (hy : y ∈ interior s) : x = y
decls.doc: One cannot see any point in the interior of a set.

decls.name: IsOpen.eq_of_isVisible_of_left_mem
decls.sig: lemma IsOpen.eq_of_isVisible_of_left_mem (hs : IsOpen s) (hsxy : IsVisible 𝕜 s x y) (hy : y ∈ s) : x = y
decls.doc: One cannot see any point of an open set.

decls.name: IsVisible.mem_convexHull_isVisible
decls.sig: lemma IsVisible.mem_convexHull_isVisible (hx : x ∉ convexHull ℝ s) (hy : y ∈ convexHull ℝ s) (hxy : IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x y) : y ∈ convexHull ℝ {z ∈ s | IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x z}
decls.doc: All points of the convex hull of a set `s` visible from a point `x ∉ convexHull ℝ s` lie in the convex hull of such points that actually lie in `s`. Note that the converse does not hold.

decls.name: IsClosed.exists_wbtw_isVisible
decls.sig: lemma IsClosed.exists_wbtw_isVisible (hs : IsClosed s) (hy : y ∈ s) (x : V) : ∃ z ∈ s, Wbtw ℝ x z y ∧ IsVisible ℝ s x z
decls.doc: If `s` is a closed set, then any point `x` sees some point of `s` in any direction where there is something to see.

decls.name: IsClosed.convexHull_subset_affineSpan_isVisible
decls.sig: lemma IsClosed.convexHull_subset_affineSpan_isVisible (hs : IsClosed (convexHull ℝ s)) (hx : x ∉ convexHull ℝ s) : convexHull ℝ s ⊆ affineSpan ℝ ({x} ∪ {y ∈ s | IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x y})
decls.doc: A set whose convex hull is closed lies in the cone based at a point `x` generated by its points visible from `x` through its convex hull.

decls.name: rank_le_card_isVisible
decls.sig: lemma rank_le_card_isVisible (hs : IsClosed (convexHull ℝ s)) (hx : x ∉ convexHull ℝ s) : Module.rank ℝ (span ℝ (-x +ᵥ s)) ≤ #{y ∈ s | IsVisible ℝ (convexHull ℝ s) x y}
decls.doc: If `s` is a closed set of dimension `d` and `x` is a point outside of its convex hull, then `x` sees at least `d` points of the convex hull of `s` that actually lie in `s`.

decls.name: ProperCone

decls.doc: A proper cone is a pointed cone `C` that is closed. Proper cones have the nice property that they are equal to their double dual, see `ProperCone.dual_dual`. This makes them useful for defining cone programs and proving duality theorems.

decls.doc: (Order) topology on a partial order `α` generated by the subbase of open intervals `(a, ∞) = { x ∣ a < x }, (-∞, b) = {x ∣ x < b}` for all `a, b` in `α`. We do not register it as an instance as many ordered sets are already endowed with the same topology, most often in a non-defeq way though. Regist

decls.name: OrderTopology
decls.sig: class OrderTopology (α : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] : Prop where
decls.doc: The order topology on an ordered type is the topology generated by open intervals. We register it on a preorder, but it is mostly interesting in linear orders, where it is also order-closed. We define it as a mixin. If you want to introduce the order topology on a preorder, use `Preorder.topology`.

decls.doc: Consider a disjoint family of intervals `(x, y)` with `x < y` in a second-countable space. Then the family is countable. This is not a straightforward consequence of second-countability as some of these intervals might be empty (but in fact this can happen only for countably many of them).

decls.name: exists_mem_Icc_isFixedPt

decls.name: exists_mem_Icc_isFixedPt_of_surjOn

decls.name: ContinuousInf
decls.sig: class ContinuousInf (L : Type*) [TopologicalSpace L] [Min L] : Prop where
decls.doc: Let `L` be a topological space and let `L×L` be equipped with the product topology and let `⊓:L×L → L` be an infimum. Then `L` is said to have *(jointly) continuous infimum* if the map `⊓:L×L → L` is continuous.

decls.name: ContinuousSup

decls.doc: Let `L` be a topological space and let `L×L` be equipped with the product topology and let `⊓:L×L → L` be a supremum. Then `L` is said to have *(jointly) continuous supremum* if the map `⊓:L×L → L` is continuous.

decls.name: TopologicalLattice
decls.sig: class TopologicalLattice (L : Type*) [TopologicalSpace L] [Lattice L] : Prop extends ContinuousInf L, ContinuousSup L
decls.doc: Let `L` be a lattice equipped with a topology such that `L` has continuous infimum and supremum. Then `L` is said to be a *topological lattice*.

decls.name: IsLocalMin

decls.doc: `IsLocalMin f a` means that `f a ≤ f x` for all `x` in some neighborhood of `a`.

decls.name: IsLocalMax

decls.doc: `IsLocalMax f a` means that `f x ≤ f a` for all `x ∈ s` in some neighborhood of `a`.

decls.name: liminf_add_const
decls.sig: lemma liminf_add_const (F : Filter ι) [NeBot F] [Add R] [ContinuousAdd R] [AddRightMono R] (f : ι → R) (c : R) (cobdd : F.IsCoboundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) (bdd_below : F.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) : Filter.liminf (fun i ↦ f i + c) F = Filter.liminf f F + c
decls.doc: `liminf (xᵢ + c) = (liminf xᵢ) + c`.

decls.name: limsup_const_sub
decls.sig: lemma limsup_const_sub (F : Filter ι) [AddCommSemigroup R] [Sub R] [ContinuousSub R] [OrderedSub R] [AddLeftMono R] (f : ι → R) (c : R) (cobdd : F.IsCoboundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) (bdd_below : F.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) : Filter.limsup (fun i ↦ c - f i) F = c - Filter.liminf f F
decls.doc: `limsup (c - xᵢ) = c - liminf xᵢ`.

decls.name: limsup_sub_const
decls.sig: lemma limsup_sub_const (F : Filter ι) [AddCommSemigroup R] [Sub R] [ContinuousSub R] [OrderedSub R] (f : ι → R) (c : R) (bdd_above : F.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) f) (cobdd : F.IsCoboundedUnder (· ≤ ·) f) : Filter.limsup (fun i ↦ f i - c) F = Filter.limsup f F - c
decls.doc: `limsup (xᵢ - c) = (limsup xᵢ) - c`.

decls.name: liminf_const_sub
decls.sig: lemma liminf_const_sub (F : Filter ι) [NeBot F] [AddCommSemigroup R] [Sub R] [ContinuousSub R] [OrderedSub R] [AddLeftMono R] (f : ι → R) (c : R) (bdd_above : F.IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) f) (cobdd : F.IsCoboundedUnder (· ≤ ·) f) : Filter.liminf (fun i ↦ c - f i) F = c - Filter.limsup f F
decls.doc: `liminf (c - xᵢ) = c - limsup xᵢ`.

decls.name: liminf_sub_const
decls.sig: lemma liminf_sub_const (F : Filter ι) [NeBot F] [AddCommSemigroup R] [Sub R] [ContinuousSub R] [OrderedSub R] (f : ι → R) (c : R) (cobdd : F.IsCoboundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) (bdd_below : F.IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) f) : Filter.liminf (fun i ↦ f i - c) F = Filter.liminf f F - c
decls.doc: `liminf (xᵢ - c) = (liminf xᵢ) - c`.

decls.name: HasUpperLowerClosure

decls.doc: Ad hoc class stating that the closure of an upper set is an upper set. This is used to state lemmas that do not mention algebraic operations for both the additive and multiplicative versions simultaneously. If you find a satisfying replacement for this typeclass, please remove it!

decls.name: TopologicalSpace
decls.sig: class TopologicalSpace (X : Type u) where
decls.doc: A topology on `X`.

decls.name: IsOpen
decls.sig: def IsOpen : Set X → Prop
decls.doc: `IsOpen s` means that `s` is open in the ambient topological space on `X`

decls.name: isOpen_univ
decls.sig: @[simp] theorem isOpen_univ : IsOpen (univ : Set X)

decls.name: IsOpen.inter
decls.sig: theorem IsOpen.inter (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : IsOpen (s ∩ t)

decls.name: isOpen_sUnion
decls.sig: theorem isOpen_sUnion {s : Set (Set X)} (h : ∀ t ∈ s, IsOpen t) : IsOpen (⋃₀ s)

decls.name: IsClosed
decls.sig: class IsClosed (s : Set X) : Prop where
decls.doc: A set is closed if its complement is open

decls.name: IsClopen
decls.sig: def IsClopen (s : Set X) : Prop
decls.doc: A set is clopen if it is both closed and open.

decls.name: IsLocallyClosed
decls.sig: def IsLocallyClosed (s : Set X) : Prop
decls.doc: A set is locally closed if it is the intersection of some open set and some closed set. Also see `isLocallyClosed_tfae` and other lemmas in `Mathlib/Topology/LocallyClosed.lean`.

decls.name: interior
decls.sig: def interior (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The interior of a set `s` is the largest open subset of `s`.

decls.name: closure
decls.sig: def closure (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The closure of `s` is the smallest closed set containing `s`.

decls.name: frontier
decls.sig: def frontier (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The frontier of a set is the set of points between the closure and interior.

decls.name: coborder
decls.sig: def coborder (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The coborder is defined as the complement of `closure s \ s`, or the union of `s` and the complement of `∂(s)`. This is the largest set in which `s` is closed, and `s` is locally closed if and only if `coborder s` is open. This is unnamed in the literature, and this name is due to the fact that `cob

decls.name: Dense
decls.sig: def Dense (s : Set X) : Prop
decls.doc: A set is dense in a topological space if every point belongs to its closure.

decls.name: DenseRange
decls.sig: def DenseRange {α : Type*} (f : α → X)
decls.doc: `f : α → X` has dense range if its range (image) is a dense subset of `X`.

decls.name: Continuous
decls.sig: structure Continuous (f : X → Y) : Prop where
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is continuous if the preimage of every open set is open. Registered as a structure to make sure it is not unfolded by Lean.

decls.name: IsOpenMap
decls.sig: def IsOpenMap (f : X → Y) : Prop
decls.doc: A map `f : X → Y` is said to be an *open map*, if the image of any open `U : Set X` is open in `Y`.

decls.name: IsClosedMap
decls.sig: def IsClosedMap (f : X → Y) : Prop
decls.doc: A map `f : X → Y` is said to be a *closed map*, if the image of any closed `U : Set X` is closed in `Y`.

decls.name: IsOpenQuotientMap
decls.sig: structure IsOpenQuotientMap (f : X → Y) : Prop where
decls.doc: An open quotient map is an open map `f : X → Y` which is both an open map and a quotient map. Equivalently, it is a surjective continuous open map. We use the latter characterization as a definition. Many important quotient maps are open quotient maps, including - the quotient map from a topological

decls.name: BaireSpace
decls.sig: class BaireSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
decls.doc: The property `BaireSpace α` means that the topological space `α` has the Baire property: any countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense. Formulated here when the source space is ℕ. Use `dense_iInter_of_isOpen` which works for any countable index type instead.

decls.name: WithTopology
decls.sig: structure WithTopology (X : Type*) (t : TopologicalSpace X) where
decls.doc: A one-field structure wrapper for `X` with the topology coinduced from `t`.

decls.name: nhds
decls.sig: irreducible_def nhds (x : X) : Filter X
decls.doc: A set is called a neighborhood of `x` if it contains an open set around `x`. The set of all neighborhoods of `x` forms a filter, the neighborhood filter at `x`, is here defined as the infimum over the principal filters of all open sets containing `x`.

decls.name: nhdsWithin
decls.sig: def nhdsWithin (x : X) (s : Set X) : Filter X
decls.doc: The "neighborhood within" filter. Elements of `𝓝[s] x` are sets containing the intersection of `s` and a neighborhood of `x`.

decls.name: nhdsSet
decls.sig: def nhdsSet (s : Set X) : Filter X
decls.doc: The filter of neighborhoods of a set in a topological space.

decls.name: nhdsSetWithin
decls.sig: def nhdsSetWithin (s t : Set X) : Filter X
decls.doc: The "neighbourhood within" filter for sets. Elements of `𝓝[t] s` are sets containing the intersection of `t` and a neighbourhood of `s`.

decls.name: nhdsKer
decls.sig: def nhdsKer (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The *neighborhoods kernel* of a set is the intersection of all its neighborhoods. In an Alexandrov-discrete space, this is the smallest neighborhood of the set.

decls.name: ContinuousAt
decls.sig: def ContinuousAt (f : X → Y) (x : X)
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is continuous at a point `x₀` if `f x` tends to `f x₀` when `x` tends to `x₀`.

decls.name: ContinuousWithinAt
decls.sig: def ContinuousWithinAt (f : X → Y) (s : Set X) (x : X) : Prop
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is continuous at a point `x₀` within a subset `s` if `f x` tends to `f x₀` when `x` tends to `x₀` while staying within `s`.

decls.name: ContinuousOn
decls.sig: def ContinuousOn (f : X → Y) (s : Set X) : Prop
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is continuous on a subset `s` when it's continuous at every point of `s` within `s`.

decls.name: Specializes
decls.sig: def Specializes (x y : X) : Prop
decls.doc: `x` specializes to `y` (notation: `x ⤳ y`) if either of the following equivalent properties hold: * `𝓝 x ≤ 𝓝 y`; this property is used as the definition; * `pure x ≤ 𝓝 y`; in other words, any neighbourhood of `y` contains `x`; * `y ∈ closure {x}`; * `closure {y} ⊆ closure {x}`; * for any closed set

decls.name: Inseparable
decls.sig: def Inseparable (x y : X) : Prop
decls.doc: Two points `x` and `y` in a topological space are `Inseparable`, or *topologically indistinguishable*, if any of the following equivalent properties hold: - `𝓝 x = 𝓝 y`; we use this property as the definition; - for any open set `s`, `x ∈ s ↔ y ∈ s`, see `inseparable_iff_forall_isOpen`; - for any cl

decls.name: specializationPreorder
decls.sig: def specializationPreorder : Preorder X
decls.doc: Specialization forms a preorder on the topological space.

decls.name: inseparableSetoid
decls.sig: def inseparableSetoid : Setoid X
decls.doc: A `setoid` version of `Inseparable`, used to define the `SeparationQuotient`.

decls.name: SeparationQuotient
decls.sig: def SeparationQuotient
decls.doc: The quotient of a topological space by its `inseparableSetoid`. Also called the Kolmogorov quotient. This quotient is guaranteed to be a T₀ space.

decls.name: IsLocallyClosedAt
decls.sig: def IsLocallyClosedAt (s : Set X) (x : X) : Prop
decls.doc: A set `s` is locally closed at a point `x` if there is a neighborhood `U` of `x` and a closed set `Z` such that `U ∩ s = U ∩ Z`. Also see `isLocallyClosedAt_tfae` and other lemmas in `Mathlib/Topology/LocallyClosed.lean`.

decls.name: Filter.lim
decls.sig: noncomputable def Filter.lim [Nonempty X] (f : Filter X) : X
decls.doc: If `f` is a filter, then `Filter.lim f` is a limit of the filter, if it exists.

decls.name: Filter.limUnder
decls.sig: noncomputable def Filter.limUnder {α : Type*} [Nonempty X] (f : Filter α) (g : α → X) : X
decls.doc: If `f` is a filter in `α` and `g : α → X` is a function, then `Filter.limUnder f g` is a limit of `g` at `f`, if it exists.

decls.name: ClusterPt
decls.sig: def ClusterPt (x : X) (F : Filter X) : Prop
decls.doc: A point `x` is a cluster point of a filter `F` if `𝓝 x ⊓ F ≠ ⊥`. Also known as an accumulation point or a limit point, but beware that terminology varies. This is *not* the same as asking `𝓝[≠] x ⊓ F ≠ ⊥`, which is called `AccPt` in Mathlib. See `mem_closure_iff_clusterPt` in particular.

decls.name: MapClusterPt
decls.sig: def MapClusterPt {ι : Type*} (x : X) (F : Filter ι) (u : ι → X) : Prop
decls.doc: A point `x` is a cluster point of a sequence `u` along a filter `F` if it is a cluster point of `map u F`.

decls.name: AccPt
decls.sig: def AccPt (x : X) (F : Filter X) : Prop
decls.doc: A point `x` is an accumulation point of a filter `F` if `𝓝[≠] x ⊓ F ≠ ⊥`. See also `ClusterPt`.

decls.name: IsCompact
decls.sig: def IsCompact (s : Set X)
decls.doc: A set `s` is compact if for every nontrivial filter `f` that contains `s`, there exists `a ∈ s` such that every set of `f` meets every neighborhood of `a`.

decls.name: CompactSpace
decls.sig: class CompactSpace : Prop where
decls.doc: Type class for compact spaces. Separation is sometimes included in the definition, especially in the French literature, but we do not include it here.

decls.name: NoncompactSpace
decls.sig: class NoncompactSpace : Prop where
decls.doc: `X` is a noncompact topological space if it is not a compact space.

decls.name: WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace
decls.sig: class WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
decls.doc: We say that a topological space is a *weakly locally compact space*, if each point of this space admits a compact neighborhood.

decls.name: LocallyCompactSpace
decls.sig: class LocallyCompactSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
decls.doc: There are various definitions of "locally compact space" in the literature, which agree for Hausdorff spaces but not in general. This one is the precise condition on X needed for the evaluation map `C(X, Y) × X → Y` to be continuous for all `Y` when `C(X, Y)` is given the compact-open topology. See

decls.name: LocallyCompactPair
decls.sig: class LocallyCompactPair (X Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] : Prop where
decls.doc: We say that `X` and `Y` are a locally compact pair of topological spaces, if for any continuous map `f : X → Y`, a point `x : X`, and a neighbourhood `s ∈ 𝓝 (f x)`, there exists a compact neighbourhood `K ∈ 𝓝 x` such that `f` maps `K` to `s`. This is a technical assumption that appears in several th

decls.name: Filter.cocompact
decls.sig: def Filter.cocompact : Filter X
decls.doc: `Filter.cocompact` is the filter generated by complements to compact sets.

decls.name: Filter.coclosedCompact
decls.sig: def Filter.coclosedCompact : Filter X
decls.doc: `Filter.coclosedCompact` is the filter generated by complements to closed compact sets. In a Hausdorff space, this is the same as `Filter.cocompact`.

decls.name: TopologicalSpace.induced
decls.sig: def induced (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace Y) : TopologicalSpace X where
decls.doc: Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `Y`, the induced topology on `X` is the collection of sets that are preimages of some open set in `Y`. This is the coarsest topology that makes `f` continuous.

decls.name: TopologicalSpace.coinduced
decls.sig: def coinduced (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : TopologicalSpace Y where
decls.doc: Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `X`, the coinduced topology on `Y` is defined such that `s : Set Y` is open if the preimage of `s` is open. This is the finest topology that makes `f` continuous.

decls.name: WithTopology.topology_eq_coinduced
decls.sig: lemma topology_eq_coinduced (X : Type*) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : instTopologicalSpace X t = .coinduced (.toTopology t) t

decls.name: WithTopology.equiv
decls.sig: protected def equiv (X : Type*) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : WithTopology X t ≃ X where
decls.doc: `WithTopology.ofTopology` and `WithTopology.toTopology` as an equivalence.

decls.name: Topology.IsCoherentWith
decls.sig: structure IsCoherentWith (S : Set (Set X)) : Prop where
decls.doc: We say that restrictions of the topology on `X` to sets from a family `S` generates the original topology, if either of the following equivalent conditions hold: - a set which is relatively open in each `s ∈ S` is open; - a set which is relatively closed in each `s ∈ S` is closed; - for any topologi

decls.name: Topology.IsInducing
decls.sig: structure IsInducing (f : X → Y) : Prop where
decls.doc: A function `f : X → Y` between topological spaces is inducing if the topology on `X` is induced by the topology on `Y` through `f`, meaning that a set `s : Set X` is open iff it is the preimage under `f` of some open set `t : Set Y`.

decls.name: Topology.IsCoinducing
decls.sig: structure IsCoinducing (f : X → Y) : Prop where
decls.doc: A function `f : X → Y` between topological spaces is coinducing if the topology on `Y` is coinduced by the topology on `X` through `f`, meaning that a set `s : Set Y` is open iff its preimage is open.

decls.name: Topology.IsEmbedding
decls.sig: structure IsEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsInducing f where
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is an embedding if it is injective, and for all `s : Set X`, `s` is open iff it is the preimage of an open set.

decls.name: Topology.IsOpenEmbedding
decls.sig: structure IsOpenEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsEmbedding f where
decls.doc: An open embedding is an embedding with open range.

decls.name: Topology.IsClosedEmbedding
decls.sig: structure IsClosedEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsEmbedding f where
decls.doc: A closed embedding is an embedding with closed image.

decls.name: Topology.IsQuotientMap
decls.sig: structure IsQuotientMap {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : X → Y) : Prop extends isCoinducing : IsCoinducing f where
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is a quotient map if it is surjective, and for all `s : Set Y`, `s` is open iff its preimage is an open set.

decls.name: seqClosure
decls.sig: def seqClosure (s : Set X) : Set X
decls.doc: The sequential closure of a set `s : Set X` in a topological space `X` is the set of all `a : X` which arise as limit of sequences in `s`. Note that the sequential closure of a set is not guaranteed to be sequentially closed.

decls.name: IsSeqClosed
decls.sig: def IsSeqClosed (s : Set X) : Prop
decls.doc: A set `s` is sequentially closed if for any converging sequence `x n` of elements of `s`, the limit belongs to `s` as well. Note that the sequential closure of a set is not guaranteed to be sequentially closed.

decls.name: SeqContinuous
decls.sig: def SeqContinuous (f : X → Y) : Prop
decls.doc: A function between topological spaces is sequentially continuous if it commutes with limit of convergent sequences.

decls.name: IsSeqCompact
decls.sig: def IsSeqCompact (s : Set X)
decls.doc: A set `s` is sequentially compact if every sequence taking values in `s` has a converging subsequence.

decls.name: SeqCompactSpace
decls.sig: class SeqCompactSpace : Prop where
decls.doc: A space `X` is sequentially compact if every sequence in `X` has a converging subsequence.

decls.name: FrechetUrysohnSpace
decls.sig: class FrechetUrysohnSpace : Prop where
decls.doc: A topological space is called a *Fréchet-Urysohn space*, if the sequential closure of any set is equal to its closure. Since one of the inclusions is trivial, we require only the non-trivial one in the definition.

decls.name: SequentialSpace
decls.sig: class SequentialSpace : Prop where
decls.doc: A topological space is said to be a *sequential space* if any sequentially closed set in this space is closed. This condition is weaker than being a Fréchet-Urysohn space.

decls.name: IsSeqClosed.isClosed
decls.sig: protected theorem IsSeqClosed.isClosed [SequentialSpace X] {s : Set X} (hs : IsSeqClosed s) : IsClosed s
decls.doc: In a sequential space, a sequentially closed set is closed.

decls.name: Ultrafilter.lim
decls.sig: noncomputable nonrec def Ultrafilter.lim (F : Ultrafilter X) : X
decls.doc: If `F` is an ultrafilter, then `Filter.Ultrafilter.lim F` is a limit of the filter, if it exists. Note that dot notation `F.lim` can be used for `F : Filter.Ultrafilter X`.

decls.name: nhds_bind_nhdsWithin
decls.sig: theorem nhds_bind_nhdsWithin {a : α} {s : Set α} : ((𝓝 a).bind fun x => 𝓝[s] x) = 𝓝[s] a

decls.name: eventually_nhds_nhdsWithin
decls.sig: theorem eventually_nhds_nhdsWithin {a : α} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 a, ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] y, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] a, p x

decls.name: eventually_nhdsWithin_iff
decls.sig: theorem eventually_nhdsWithin_iff {a : α} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] a, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 a, x ∈ s → p x

decls.name: frequently_nhdsWithin_iff
decls.sig: theorem frequently_nhdsWithin_iff {z : α} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∃ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] z, p x) ↔ ∃ᶠ x in 𝓝 z, p x ∧ x ∈ s

decls.name: mem_closure_ne_iff_frequently_within
decls.sig: theorem mem_closure_ne_iff_frequently_within {z : α} {s : Set α} : z ∈ closure (s \ {z}) ↔ ∃ᶠ x in 𝓝[≠] z, x ∈ s

decls.name: eventually_eventually_nhdsWithin
decls.sig: theorem eventually_eventually_nhdsWithin {a : α} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[s] a, ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] y, p x) ↔ ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝[s] a, p x

decls.name: eventually_mem_nhdsWithin_iff
decls.sig: theorem eventually_mem_nhdsWithin_iff {x : α} {s t : Set α} : (∀ᶠ x' in 𝓝[s] x, t ∈ 𝓝[s] x') ↔ t ∈ 𝓝[s] x

decls.name: nhdsWithin_eq
decls.sig: theorem nhdsWithin_eq (a : α) (s : Set α) : 𝓝[s] a = ⨅ t ∈ { t : Set α | a ∈ t ∧ IsOpen t }, 𝓟 (t ∩ s)

decls.name: nhdsWithin_univ
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma nhdsWithin_univ (a : α) : 𝓝[Set.univ] a = 𝓝 a

decls.name: nhdsWithin_hasBasis
decls.sig: theorem nhdsWithin_hasBasis {ι : Sort*} {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set α} {a : α} (h : (𝓝 a).HasBasis p s) (t : Set α) : (𝓝[t] a).HasBasis p fun i => s i ∩ t

decls.name: nhdsWithin_basis_open
decls.sig: theorem nhdsWithin_basis_open (a : α) (t : Set α) : (𝓝[t] a).HasBasis (fun u => a ∈ u ∧ IsOpen u) fun u => u ∩ t

decls.name: mem_nhdsWithin
decls.sig: theorem mem_nhdsWithin {t : Set α} {a : α} {s : Set α} : t ∈ 𝓝[s] a ↔ ∃ u, IsOpen u ∧ a ∈ u ∧ u ∩ s ⊆ t

decls.name: mem_nhdsWithin_iff_exists_mem_nhds_inter
decls.sig: theorem mem_nhdsWithin_iff_exists_mem_nhds_inter {t : Set α} {a : α} {s : Set α} : t ∈ 𝓝[s] a ↔ ∃ u ∈ 𝓝 a, u ∩ s ⊆ t

decls.name: sdiff_mem_nhdsWithin_compl
decls.sig: theorem sdiff_mem_nhdsWithin_compl {x : α} {s : Set α} (hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x) (t : Set α) : s \ t ∈ 𝓝[tᶜ] x

decls.name: sdiff_mem_nhdsWithin_sdiff
