decls.sig: lemma tendsto_integral_of_forall_integral_le_liminf_integral {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι} {μ : Measure X} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {μs : ι → Measure X} [∀ i, IsProbabilityMeasure (μs i)] (h : ∀ f : X →ᵇ ℝ, 0 ≤ f → ∫ x, f x ∂μ ≤ L.liminf (fun i ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂(μs i))) (f : X →ᵇ ℝ) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂(μs i)) L (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ))

decls.name: Real.circleAverage
decls.sig: noncomputable def circleAverage : E
decls.doc: Define `circleAverage f c R` as the average value of `f` on the circle with center `c` and radius `R`. This is a real notion, which should not be confused with the complex path integral notion defined in `circleIntegral` (integrating with respect to `dz`).

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_def
decls.sig: lemma circleAverage_def : circleAverage f c R = (2 * π)⁻¹ • ∫ θ in 0..2 * π, f (circleMap c R θ)

decls.name: Real.circleAverage.integral_undef
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage.integral_undef (hf : ¬CircleIntegrable f c R) : circleAverage f c R = 0
decls.doc: If 'f' is *not* circle integrable, then the circle average is zero by definition.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_eq_intervalAverage
decls.sig: lemma circleAverage_eq_intervalAverage : circleAverage f c R = ⨍ θ in 0..2 * π, f (circleMap c R θ)
decls.doc: Expression of `circleAverage` in terms of interval averages.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_zero
decls.sig: @[simp] lemma circleAverage_zero [CompleteSpace E] : circleAverage f c 0 = f c
decls.doc: Interval averages for zero radii equal values at the center point.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_map_add_const
decls.sig: lemma circleAverage_map_add_const : circleAverage (fun z ↦ f (z + c)) 0 R = circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: Expression of `circleAverage` with arbitrary center in terms of `circleAverage` with center zero.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_eq_circleIntegral
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_eq_circleIntegral {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] {f : ℂ → F} (h : R ≠ 0) : circleAverage f c R = (2 * π * I)⁻¹ • (∮ z in C(c, R), (z - c)⁻¹ • f z)
decls.doc: Expression of the `circleAverage` in terms of a `circleIntegral`.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_eq_integral_add
decls.sig: lemma circleAverage_eq_integral_add (η : ℝ) : circleAverage f c R = (2 * π)⁻¹ • ∫ θ in 0..2 * π, f (circleMap c R (θ + η))
decls.doc: Circle averages do not change when shifting the angle.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_neg_radius
decls.sig: @[simp] theorem circleAverage_neg_radius : circleAverage f c (-R) = circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: Circle averages do not change when replacing the radius by its negative.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_abs_radius
decls.sig: @[simp] theorem circleAverage_abs_radius : circleAverage f c |R| = circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: Circle averages do not change when replacing the radius by its absolute value.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_congr_codiscreteWithin
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_congr_codiscreteWithin (hf : f₁ =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin (sphere c |R|)] f₂) (hR : R ≠ 0) : circleAverage f₁ c R = circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: If two functions agree outside of a discrete set in the circle, then their averages agree.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_congr_sphere
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_congr_sphere {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → E} (hf : Set.EqOn f₁ f₂ (sphere c |R|)) : circleAverage f₁ c R = circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: If two functions agree on the circle, then their circle averages agree.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_eq_circleAverage_zero_one
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_eq_circleAverage_zero_one : circleAverage f c R = (circleAverage (fun z ↦ f (R * z + c)) 0 1)
decls.doc: Express the circle average over an arbitrary circle as a circle average over the unit circle.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_zero_one_congr_inv
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_zero_one_congr_inv {f : ℂ → E} : circleAverage (f ·⁻¹) 0 1 = circleAverage f 0 1
decls.doc: The circle average of a function `f` on the unit sphere equals the circle average of the function `z ↦ f z⁻¹`.

decls.name: Real.circleMap.continuous
decls.sig: @[fun_prop] lemma circleMap.continuous {c : ℂ} : Continuous (fun (x : ℝ × ℝ) ↦ circleMap c x.1 x.2)
decls.doc: The circleMap for a fixed center is continuous as a function on `ℝ × ℝ`.

decls.name: Real.ContinuousOn.circleAverage
decls.sig: theorem ContinuousOn.circleAverage {f : ℂ → E} {s : Set ℝ} {c : ℂ} (hf : ContinuousOn f {z : ℂ | ‖z - c‖ ∈ s}) (hs : ∀ r ∈ s, 0 ≤ r) : ContinuousOn (circleAverage f c) s
decls.doc: The circle average of a continuous function is itself continuous, as a function of the radius.

decls.name: Real.Continuous.circleAverage
decls.sig: @[fun_prop] theorem Continuous.circleAverage {f : ℂ → E} (hf : Continuous f) : Continuous (Real.circleAverage f c)
decls.doc: The circle average of a continuous function is itself continuous, as a function of the radius.

decls.name: Real.ContinuousOn.eq_of_eqOn_Ioo
decls.sig: lemma ContinuousOn.eq_of_eqOn_Ioo {f : ℝ → ℝ} {c r R : ℝ} (h₁f : ContinuousOn f (Ioc r R)) (hR : r < R) (h₂f : EqOn f (fun _ ↦ c) (Ioo r R)) : f R = c
decls.doc: Companion lemma to `ContinuousOn.circleAverage`: a function continuous on `Ioc r R` and constant on `Ioo r R` is constant.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_const
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_const [CompleteSpace E] (a : E) (c : ℂ) (R : ℝ) : circleAverage (fun _ ↦ a) c R = a
decls.doc: The circle average of a constant function equals the constant.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_const_on_circle
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_const_on_circle [CompleteSpace E] {a : E} (hf : ∀ x ∈ Metric.sphere c |R|, f x = a) : circleAverage f c R = a
decls.doc: If `f x` equals `a` on for every point of the circle, then the circle average of `f` equals `a`.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_mono
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_mono {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → ℝ} (hf₁ : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R) (hf₂ : CircleIntegrable f₂ c R) (h : ∀ x ∈ Metric.sphere c |R|, f₁ x ≤ f₂ x) : circleAverage f₁ c R ≤ circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle averages respect the `≤` relation.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_mono_on_of_le_circle
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_mono_on_of_le_circle {f : ℂ → ℝ} {a : ℝ} (hf : CircleIntegrable f c R) (h₂f : ∀ x ∈ Metric.sphere c |R|, f x ≤ a) : circleAverage f c R ≤ a
decls.doc: If `f x` is smaller than `a` on for every point of the circle, then the circle average of `f` is smaller than `a`.

decls.name: Real.norm_circleAverage_le_circleAverage_norm
decls.sig: theorem norm_circleAverage_le_circleAverage_norm : ‖circleAverage f c R‖ ≤ circleAverage (fun z ↦ ‖f z‖) c R

decls.name: Real.abs_circleAverage_le_circleAverage_abs
decls.sig: theorem abs_circleAverage_le_circleAverage_abs {f : ℂ → ℝ} : |circleAverage f c R| ≤ circleAverage |f| c R
decls.doc: Analogue of `intervalIntegral.abs_integral_le_integral_abs`: The absolute value of a circle average is less than or equal to the circle average of the absolute value of the function.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_nonneg_of_nonneg
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_nonneg_of_nonneg {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℝ} (h₂f : ∀ x ∈ Metric.sphere c |R|, 0 ≤ f x) : 0 ≤ circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: The circle average of a nonnegative function is nonnegative.

decls.name: ContinuousLinearMap.circleAverage_comp_comm
decls.sig: theorem _root_.ContinuousLinearMap.circleAverage_comp_comm [CompleteSpace E] (L : E →L[ℝ] F) {f : ℂ → E} (hf : CircleIntegrable f c R) : circleAverage (L ∘ f) c R = L (circleAverage f c R)
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with continuous linear maps.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_smul
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_smul : circleAverage (a • f) c R = a • circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with scalar multiplication.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_fun_smul
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_fun_smul : circleAverage (fun z ↦ a • f z) c R = a • circleAverage f c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with scalar multiplication.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_add
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_add (hf₁ : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R) (hf₂ : CircleIntegrable f₂ c R) : circleAverage (f₁ + f₂) c R = circleAverage f₁ c R + circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with addition.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_fun_add
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_fun_add {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → E} (hf₁ : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R) (hf₂ : CircleIntegrable f₂ c R) : circleAverage (fun z ↦ f₁ z + f₂ z) c R = circleAverage f₁ c R + circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with addition.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_sum
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_sum {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℂ → E} (h : ∀ i ∈ s, CircleIntegrable (f i) c R) : circleAverage (∑ i ∈ s, f i) c R = ∑ i ∈ s, circleAverage (f i) c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with sums.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_fun_sum
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_fun_sum {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℂ → E} (h : ∀ i ∈ s, CircleIntegrable (f i) c R) : circleAverage (fun z ↦ ∑ i ∈ s, f i z) c R = ∑ i ∈ s, circleAverage (f i) c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with sums.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_sub
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_sub (hf₁ : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R) (hf₂ : CircleIntegrable f₂ c R) : circleAverage (f₁ - f₂) c R = circleAverage f₁ c R - circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with subtraction.

decls.name: Real.circleAverage_fun_sub
decls.sig: theorem circleAverage_fun_sub (hf₁ : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R) (hf₂ : CircleIntegrable f₂ c R) : circleAverage (fun z ↦ f₁ z - f₂ z) c R = circleAverage f₁ c R - circleAverage f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle averages commute with subtraction.

decls.name: range_circleMap

decls.name: circleMap_neg_radius
decls.sig: theorem circleMap_neg_radius {r x : ℝ} {c : ℂ} : circleMap c (-r) x = circleMap c r (x + π)

Note that the actual function used in the definition of `circleIntegral` is `(deriv (circleMap c R) θ) • f (circleMap c R θ)`. Integrability o

decls.name: CircleIntegrable.smul_continuousOn

decls.name: CircleIntegrable.continuousOn_mul

decls.name: circleIntegrable_zero_radius

decls.name: circleIntegrable_congr

decls.name: circleIntegrable_neg_radius

decls.name: CircleIntegrable.congr_codiscreteWithin

decls.name: circleIntegrable_congr_codiscreteWithin
decls.sig: theorem circleIntegrable_congr_codiscreteWithin {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → E} (hf : f₁ =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin (sphere c |R|)] f₂) : CircleIntegrable f₁ c R ↔ CircleIntegrable f₂ c R
decls.doc: Circle integrability is invariant when functions change along discrete sets.

decls.name: circleIntegrable_iff

decls.name: ContinuousOn.circleIntegrable'

decls.name: circleIntegrable_sub_zpow_iff

decls.sig: lemma tendsto_measure_of_ae_tendsto_indicator {μ : Measure α} (A_mble : MeasurableSet A) (As_mble : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (As i)) {B : Set α} (B_mble : MeasurableSet B) (B_finmeas : μ B ≠ ∞) (As_le_B : ∀ᶠ i in L, As i ⊆ B) (h_lim : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ᶠ i in L, x ∈ As i ↔ x ∈ A) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ μ (As i)) L (𝓝 (μ A))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lmarginal

decls.doc: Integrate `f(x₁,…,xₙ)` over all variables `xᵢ` where `i ∈ s`. Return a function in the remaining variables (it will be constant in the `xᵢ` for `i ∈ s`). This is the marginal distribution of all variables not in `s` when the considered measure is the product measure.

decls.doc: A binary function is integrable if the function `x ↦ f (x, y)` is integrable for almost every `y` and the function `y ↦ ∫ ‖f (x, y)‖ dx` is integrable.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_fn_integral_add
decls.sig: theorem integral_fn_integral_add ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (F : E → E') (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, F (∫ y, f (x, y) + g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ) = ∫ x, F ((∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν) + ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ
decls.doc: Integrals commute with addition inside another integral. `F` can be any function.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_fn_integral_sub
decls.sig: theorem integral_fn_integral_sub ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (F : E → E') (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, F (∫ y, f (x, y) - g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ) = ∫ x, F ((∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν) - ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ
decls.doc: Integrals commute with subtraction inside another integral. `F` can be any measurable function.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_fn_integral_sub
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_fn_integral_sub ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (F : E → ℝ≥0∞) (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫⁻ x, F (∫ y, f (x, y) - g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ) = ∫⁻ x, F ((∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν) - ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν) ∂μ
decls.doc: Integrals commute with subtraction inside a lower Lebesgue integral. `F` can be any function.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_add
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_add ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) + g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) = (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) + ∫ x, ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ
decls.doc: Double integrals commute with addition.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_add'
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_add' ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, ∫ y, (f + g) (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) = (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) + ∫ x, ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ
decls.doc: Double integrals commute with addition. This is the version with `(f + g) (x, y)` (instead of `f (x, y) + g (x, y)`) in the LHS.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_sub
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_sub ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) - g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) = (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) - ∫ x, ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ
decls.doc: Double integrals commute with subtraction.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_sub'
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_sub' ⦃f g : α × β → E⦄ (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) (hg : Integrable g (μ.prod ν)) : (∫ x, ∫ y, (f - g) (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) = (∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ) - ∫ x, ∫ y, g (x, y) ∂ν ∂μ
decls.doc: Double integrals commute with subtraction. This is the version with `(f - g) (x, y)` (instead of `f (x, y) - g (x, y)`) in the LHS.

decls.doc: **Fubini's Theorem**: For integrable functions on `α × β`, the Bochner integral of `f` is equal to the iterated Bochner integral. `integrable_prod_iff` can be useful to show that the function in question in integrable. `MeasureTheory.Integrable.integral_prod_right` is useful to show that the inner i

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_prod_symm
decls.sig: theorem integral_prod_symm (f : α × β → E) (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) : ∫ z, f z ∂μ.prod ν = ∫ y, ∫ x, f (x, y) ∂μ ∂ν
decls.doc: Symmetric version of **Fubini's Theorem**: For integrable functions on `α × β`, the Bochner integral of `f` is equal to the iterated Bochner integral. This version has the integrals on the right-hand side in the other order.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral {f : α → β → E} (hf : Integrable (uncurry f) (μ.prod ν)) : ∫ x, ∫ y, f x y ∂ν ∂μ = ∫ z, f z.1 z.2 ∂μ.prod ν

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_symm
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_symm {f : α → β → E} (hf : Integrable (uncurry f) (μ.prod ν)) : ∫ x, ∫ y, f x y ∂ν ∂μ = ∫ z, f z.2 z.1 ∂ν.prod μ
decls.doc: Reversed version of **Fubini's Theorem** (symmetric version).

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap
decls.sig: theorem integral_integral_swap ⦃f : α → β → E⦄ (hf : Integrable (uncurry f) (μ.prod ν)) : ∫ x, ∫ y, f x y ∂ν ∂μ = ∫ y, ∫ x, f x y ∂μ ∂ν

decls.name: MeasureTheory.intervalIntegral_intervalIntegral_swap

decls.doc: Change the order of integration for interval integrals.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport
decls.sig: lemma integral_integral_swap_of_hasCompactSupport {f : X → Y → E} (hf : Continuous f.uncurry) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f.uncurry) {μ : Measure X} {ν : Measure Y} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν] : ∫ x, (∫ y, f x y ∂ν) ∂μ = ∫ y, (∫ x, f x y ∂μ) ∂ν
decls.doc: A version of *Fubini theorem* for continuous functions with compact support: one may swap the order of integration with respect to locally finite measures. One does not assume that the measures are σ-finite, contrary to the usual Fubini theorem.

decls.name: IsCompact.measure_eq_biInf_integral_hasCompactSupport
decls.sig: lemma IsCompact.measure_eq_biInf_integral_hasCompactSupport {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] {k : Set X} (hk : IsCompact k) (μ : Measure X) [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ] [InnerRegularCompactLTTop μ] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [RegularSpace X] : μ k = ⨅ (f : X → ℝ) (_ : Continuous f) (_ : HasCompactSupport f) (_ : EqOn f 1 k) (_ : 0 ≤ f), ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, f x ∂μ)
decls.doc: In a locally compact regular space with an inner regular measure, the measure of a compact set `k` is the infimum of the integrals of compactly supported functions equal to `1` on `k`.

decls.name: IsOpen.measure_eq_biSup_integral_continuous
decls.sig: lemma IsOpen.measure_eq_biSup_integral_continuous {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [T2Space X] {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) (μ : Measure X) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [InnerRegularCompactLTTop μ] [NormalSpace X] : μ U = ⨆ (f : X → ℝ) (_ : Continuous f) (_ : EqOn f 0 Uᶜ) (_ : 0 ≤ f) (_ : f ≤ 1), ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x, f x ∂μ)
decls.doc: Given an inner regular finite measure, the measure of an open set is the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative continuous functions supported in this set and bounded by `1`.

decls.name: torusMap
decls.sig: def torusMap (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : ℝⁿ → ℂⁿ
decls.doc: The n-dimensional exponential map $θ_i ↦ c + R e^{θ_i*I}, θ ∈ ℝⁿ$ representing a torus in `ℂⁿ` with center `c ∈ ℂⁿ` and generalized radius `R ∈ ℝⁿ`, so we can adjust it to every n axis.

decls.name: torusMap_sub_center
decls.sig: theorem torusMap_sub_center (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) (θ : ℝⁿ) : torusMap c R θ - c = torusMap 0 R θ

decls.name: torusMap_eq_center_iff
decls.sig: theorem torusMap_eq_center_iff {c : ℂⁿ} {R : ℝⁿ} {θ : ℝⁿ} : torusMap c R θ = c ↔ R = 0

decls.name: torusMap_zero_radius
decls.sig: theorem torusMap_zero_radius (c : ℂⁿ) : torusMap c 0 = const ℝⁿ c

decls.name: TorusIntegrable
decls.sig: def TorusIntegrable (f : ℂⁿ → E) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f : ℂⁿ → E` is integrable on the generalized torus if the function `f ∘ torusMap c R θ` is integrable on `Icc (0 : ℝⁿ) (fun _ ↦ 2 * π)`.

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.torusIntegrable_const
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegrable_const (a : E) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : TorusIntegrable (fun _ => a) c R
decls.doc: Constant functions are torus integrable

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.neg
decls.sig: protected nonrec theorem neg (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) : TorusIntegrable (-f) c R
decls.doc: If `f` is torus integrable then `-f` is torus integrable.

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.add
decls.sig: protected nonrec theorem add (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) (hg : TorusIntegrable g c R) : TorusIntegrable (f + g) c R
decls.doc: If `f` and `g` are two torus integrable functions, then so is `f + g`.

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.sub
decls.sig: protected nonrec theorem sub (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) (hg : TorusIntegrable g c R) : TorusIntegrable (f - g) c R
decls.doc: If `f` and `g` are two torus integrable functions, then so is `f - g`.

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.torusIntegrable_zero_radius
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegrable_zero_radius {f : ℂⁿ → E} {c : ℂⁿ} : TorusIntegrable f c 0

decls.name: TorusIntegrable.function_integrable
decls.sig: theorem function_integrable [NormedSpace ℂ E] (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) : IntegrableOn (fun θ : ℝⁿ => (∏ i, R i * exp (θ i * I) * I : ℂ) • f (torusMap c R θ)) (Icc (0 : ℝⁿ) fun _ => 2 * π) volume
decls.doc: The function given in the definition of `torusIntegral` is integrable.

decls.name: torusIntegral
decls.sig: def torusIntegral (f : ℂⁿ → E) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ)
decls.doc: The integral over a generalized torus with center `c ∈ ℂⁿ` and radius `R ∈ ℝⁿ`, defined as the `•`-product of the derivative of `torusMap` and `f (torusMap c R θ)`

decls.name: torusIntegral_radius_zero
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_radius_zero (hn : n ≠ 0) (f : ℂⁿ → E) (c : ℂⁿ) : (∯ x in T(c, 0), f x) = 0

decls.name: torusIntegral_neg
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_neg (f : ℂⁿ → E) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : (∯ x in T(c, R), -f x) = -∯ x in T(c, R), f x

decls.name: torusIntegral_add
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_add (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) (hg : TorusIntegrable g c R) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x + g x) = (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) + ∯ x in T(c, R), g x

decls.name: torusIntegral_sub
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_sub (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) (hg : TorusIntegrable g c R) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x - g x) = (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) - ∯ x in T(c, R), g x

decls.name: torusIntegral_smul
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_smul {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 ℂ E] (a : 𝕜) (f : ℂⁿ → E) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : (∯ x in T(c, R), a • f x) = a • ∯ x in T(c, R), f x

decls.name: torusIntegral_const_mul
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_const_mul (a : ℂ) (f : ℂⁿ → ℂ) (c : ℂⁿ) (R : ℝⁿ) : (∯ x in T(c, R), a * f x) = a * ∯ x in T(c, R), f x

decls.name: norm_torusIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const
decls.sig: theorem norm_torusIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const {C : ℝ} (hf : ∀ θ, ‖f (torusMap c R θ)‖ ≤ C) : ‖∯ x in T(c, R), f x‖ ≤ ((2 * π) ^ (n : ℕ) * ∏ i, |R i|) * C
decls.doc: If for all `θ : ℝⁿ`, `‖f (torusMap c R θ)‖` is less than or equal to a constant `C : ℝ`, then `‖∯ x in T(c, R), f x‖` is less than or equal to `(2 * π)^n * (∏ i, |R i|) * C`

decls.name: torusIntegral_dim0
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_dim0 [CompleteSpace E] (f : ℂ⁰ → E) (c : ℂ⁰) (R : ℝ⁰) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) = f c

decls.name: torusIntegral_dim1
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_dim1 (f : ℂ¹ → E) (c : ℂ¹) (R : ℝ¹) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) = ∮ z in C(c 0, R 0), f fun _ => z
decls.doc: In dimension one, `torusIntegral` is the same as `circleIntegral` (up to the natural equivalence between `ℂ` and `Fin 1 → ℂ`).

decls.name: torusIntegral_succAbove
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_succAbove {f : ℂⁿ⁺¹ → E} {c : ℂⁿ⁺¹} {R : ℝⁿ⁺¹} (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) = ∮ x in C(c i, R i), ∯ y in T(c ∘ i.succAbove, R ∘ i.succAbove), f (i.insertNth x y)
decls.doc: Recurrent formula for `torusIntegral`, see also `torusIntegral_succ`.

decls.name: torusIntegral_succ
decls.sig: theorem torusIntegral_succ {f : ℂⁿ⁺¹ → E} {c : ℂⁿ⁺¹} {R : ℝⁿ⁺¹} (hf : TorusIntegrable f c R) : (∯ x in T(c, R), f x) = ∮ x in C(c 0, R 0), ∯ y in T(c ∘ Fin.succ, R ∘ Fin.succ), f (Fin.cons x y)
decls.doc: Recurrent formula for `torusIntegral`, see also `torusIntegral_succAbove`.

For an analogous statement for more general rings with an *a priori* integrability assumption on `f`, see `MeasureTheory.Integrable

decls.doc: Monotone convergence theorem for real-valued functions and Bochner integrals

decls.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_of_integral_tendsto_of_monotone
decls.sig: lemma tendsto_of_integral_tendsto_of_monotone {μ : Measure α} {f : ℕ → α → ℝ} {F : α → ℝ} (hf_int : ∀ n, Integrable (f n) μ) (hF_int : Integrable F μ) (hf_tendsto : Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫ a, f i a ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ a, F a ∂μ))) (hf_mono : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Monotone (fun i ↦ f i a)) (hf_bound : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ∀ i, f i a ≤ F a) : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun i ↦ f i a) atTop (𝓝 (F a))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq

decls.name: integral_conj

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul
decls.sig: def weightedSMul {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (s : Set α) : F →L[ℝ] F
decls.doc: Given a set `s`, return the continuous linear map `fun x => μ.real s • x`. The extension of that set function through `setToL1` gives the Bochner integral of L1 functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_apply
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_apply {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (s : Set α) (x : F) : weightedSMul μ s x = μ.real s • x

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_zero_measure
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_zero_measure {m : MeasurableSpace α} : weightedSMul (0 : Measure α) = (0 : Set α → F →L[ℝ] F)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_empty
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_empty {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) : weightedSMul μ ∅ = (0 : F →L[ℝ] F)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_add_measure
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_add_measure {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ ν : Measure α) {s : Set α} (hμs : μ s ≠ ∞) (hνs : ν s ≠ ∞) : (weightedSMul (μ + ν) s : F →L[ℝ] F) = weightedSMul μ s + weightedSMul ν s

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_smul_measure
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_smul_measure {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (c : ℝ≥0∞) {s : Set α} : (weightedSMul (c • μ) s : F →L[ℝ] F) = c.toReal • weightedSMul μ s

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_congr
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_congr (s t : Set α) (hst : μ s = μ t) : (weightedSMul μ s : F →L[ℝ] F) = weightedSMul μ t

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_null
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_null {s : Set α} (h_zero : μ s = 0) : (weightedSMul μ s : F →L[ℝ] F) = 0

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_union'
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_union' (s t : Set α) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hs_finite : μ s ≠ ∞) (ht_finite : μ t ≠ ∞) (hdisj : Disjoint s t) : (weightedSMul μ (s ∪ t) : F →L[ℝ] F) = weightedSMul μ s + weightedSMul μ t

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_union
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_union (s t : Set α) (_hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hs_finite : μ s ≠ ∞) (ht_finite : μ t ≠ ∞) (hdisj : Disjoint s t) : (weightedSMul μ (s ∪ t) : F →L[ℝ] F) = weightedSMul μ s + weightedSMul μ t

decls.name: MeasureTheory.weightedSMul_smul
decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_smul [SMul 𝕜 F] [SMulCommClass ℝ 𝕜 F] (c : 𝕜) (s : Set α) (x : F) : weightedSMul μ s (c • x) = c • weightedSMul μ s x

decls.name: MeasureTheory.norm_weightedSMul_le
decls.sig: theorem norm_weightedSMul_le (s : Set α) : ‖(weightedSMul μ s : F →L[ℝ] F)‖ ≤ μ.real s

decls.name: MeasureTheory.dominatedFinMeasAdditive_weightedSMul
decls.sig: theorem dominatedFinMeasAdditive_weightedSMul {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) : DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ (weightedSMul μ : Set α → F →L[ℝ] F) 1

decls.sig: theorem weightedSMul_nonneg [PartialOrder F] [IsOrderedModule ℝ F] (s : Set α) (x : F) (hx : 0 ≤ x) : 0 ≤ weightedSMul μ s x

decls.doc: Positive part of a simple function.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.negPart
decls.sig: def negPart [Neg E] (f : α →ₛ E) : α →ₛ E
decls.doc: Negative part of a simple function.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.posPart_map_norm
decls.sig: theorem posPart_map_norm (f : α →ₛ ℝ) : (posPart f).map norm = posPart f

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.negPart_map_norm
decls.sig: theorem negPart_map_norm (f : α →ₛ ℝ) : (negPart f).map norm = negPart f

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.posPart_sub_negPart
decls.sig: theorem posPart_sub_negPart (f : α →ₛ ℝ) : f.posPart - f.negPart = f

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral
decls.sig: def integral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α →ₛ F) : F
decls.doc: Bochner integral of simple functions whose codomain is a real `NormedSpace`. This is equal to `∑ x ∈ f.range, μ.real (f ⁻¹' {x}) • x` (see `integral_eq`).

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_def
decls.sig: theorem integral_def {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α →ₛ F) : f.integral μ = f.setToSimpleFunc (weightedSMul μ)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_eq
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α →ₛ F) : f.integral μ = ∑ x ∈ f.range, μ.real (f ⁻¹' {x}) • x

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_eq_sum_filter
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_sum_filter [DecidablePred fun x : F => x ≠ 0] {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α →ₛ F) (μ : Measure α) : f.integral μ = ∑ x ∈ {x ∈ f.range | x ≠ 0}, μ.real (f ⁻¹' {x}) • x

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_eq_sum_of_subset
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_sum_of_subset [DecidablePred fun x : F => x ≠ 0] {f : α →ₛ F} {s : Finset F} (hs : {x ∈ f.range | x ≠ 0} ⊆ s) : f.integral μ = ∑ x ∈ s, μ.real (f ⁻¹' {x}) • x
decls.doc: The Bochner integral is equal to a sum over any set that includes `f.range` (except `0`).

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_const
decls.sig: theorem integral_const {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (y : F) : (const α y).integral μ = μ.real univ • y

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_piecewise_zero
decls.sig: theorem integral_piecewise_zero {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α →ₛ F) (μ : Measure α) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (piecewise s hs f 0).integral μ = f.integral (μ.restrict s)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.map_integral
decls.sig: theorem map_integral (f : α →ₛ E) (g : E → F) (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg : g 0 = 0) : (f.map g).integral μ = ∑ x ∈ f.range, (μ.real (f ⁻¹' {x})) • g x
decls.doc: Calculate the integral of `g ∘ f : α →ₛ F`, where `f` is an integrable function from `α` to `E` and `g` is a function from `E` to `F`. We require `g 0 = 0` so that `g ∘ f` is integrable.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_eq_lintegral'
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_lintegral' {f : α →ₛ E} {g : E → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg0 : g 0 = 0) (ht : ∀ b, g b ≠ ∞) : (f.map (ENNReal.toReal ∘ g)).integral μ = ENNReal.toReal (∫⁻ a, g (f a) ∂μ)
decls.doc: `SimpleFunc.integral` and `SimpleFunc.lintegral` agree when the integrand has type `α →ₛ ℝ≥0∞`. But since `ℝ≥0∞` is not a `NormedSpace`, we need some form of coercion. See `integral_eq_lintegral` for a simpler version.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_congr
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr {f g : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) (h : f =ᵐ[μ] g) : f.integral μ = g.integral μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_eq_lintegral
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_lintegral {f : α →ₛ ℝ} (hf : Integrable f μ) (h_pos : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) : f.integral μ = ENNReal.toReal (∫⁻ a, ENNReal.ofReal (f a) ∂μ)
decls.doc: `SimpleFunc.integral` and `SimpleFunc.lintegral` agree when the integrand has type `α →ₛ ℝ≥0∞`. But since `ℝ≥0∞` is not a `NormedSpace`, we need some form of coercion.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_add
decls.sig: theorem integral_add {f g : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg : Integrable g μ) : integral μ (f + g) = integral μ f + integral μ g

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_neg
decls.sig: theorem integral_neg {f : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) : integral μ (-f) = -integral μ f

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_sub
decls.sig: theorem integral_sub {f g : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg : Integrable g μ) : integral μ (f - g) = integral μ f - integral μ g

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_smul
decls.sig: theorem integral_smul [DistribSMul 𝕜 E] [SMulCommClass ℝ 𝕜 E] (c : 𝕜) {f : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) : integral μ (c • f) = c • integral μ f

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.norm_setToSimpleFunc_le_integral_norm
decls.sig: theorem norm_setToSimpleFunc_le_integral_norm (T : Set α → E →L[ℝ] F) {C : ℝ} (hT_norm : ∀ s, MeasurableSet s → μ s < ∞ → ‖T s‖ ≤ C * μ.real s) {f : α →ₛ E} (hf : Integrable f μ) : ‖f.setToSimpleFunc T‖ ≤ C * (f.map norm).integral μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.norm_integral_le_integral_norm
decls.sig: theorem norm_integral_le_integral_norm (f : α →ₛ E) (hf : Integrable f μ) : ‖f.integral μ‖ ≤ (f.map norm).integral μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_add_measure
decls.sig: theorem integral_add_measure {ν} (f : α →ₛ E) (hf : Integrable f (μ + ν)) : f.integral (μ + ν) = f.integral μ + f.integral ν

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_nonneg
decls.sig: lemma integral_nonneg {f : α →ₛ F} (hf : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) : 0 ≤ f.integral μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.integral_mono

decls.name: MeasureTheory.hasSum_integral_measure

decls.doc: If `f` is integrable with respect to `Measure.sum μ`, then the sequence `fun i ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂μ i` is summable and its sum is `∫ x, f x ∂Measure.sum μ`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_sum_measure
decls.sig: theorem integral_sum_measure (hf : Integrable f (Measure.sum μ)) : ∫ x, f x ∂Measure.sum μ = ∑' i, ∫ x, f x ∂μ i

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_fintype

decls.name: MeasureTheory.integral_count

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_lt_lowerSemicontinuous_integral_lt
decls.sig: theorem exists_lt_lowerSemicontinuous_integral_lt [SigmaFinite μ] (f : α → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∃ g : α → EReal, (∀ x, (f x : EReal) < g x) ∧ LowerSemicontinuous g ∧ Integrable (fun x => EReal.toReal (g x)) μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x < ⊤) ∧ (∫ x, EReal.toReal (g x) ∂μ) < (∫ x, f x ∂μ) + ε

decls.doc: **Vitali-Carathéodory Theorem**: given an integrable real function `f`, there exists an integrable function `g < f` which is upper semicontinuous, with integral arbitrarily close to that of `f`. This function has to be `EReal`-valued in general.

decls.name: curveIntegralFun
decls.sig: noncomputable irreducible_def curveIntegralFun (lemma
decls.doc: The function `t ↦ ω (γ t) (γ' t)` which appears in the definition of a curve integral. This definition is used to factor out common parts of lemmas about `CurveIntegrable` and `curveIntegral`.

decls.name: CurveIntegrable
decls.sig: def CurveIntegrable (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : Prop
decls.doc: A 1-form `ω` is *curve integrable* along a path `γ`, if the function `curveIntegralFun ω γ t = ω (γ t) (γ' t)` is integrable on `[0, 1]`. The actual definition uses `Path.extend γ`, because both interval integrals and derivatives expect globally defined functions.

decls.name: curveIntegral
decls.sig: noncomputable irreducible_def curveIntegral (lemma
decls.doc: Integral of a 1-form `ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F` along a path `γ`, defined as $\int_0^1 \omega(\gamma(t))(\gamma'(t))$. The actual definition uses `curveIntegralFun` which uses `Path.extend γ` and `derivWithin (Path.extend γ) (Set.Icc 0 1) t`, because calculus-related definitions in Mathlib expect globally

decls.name: curveIntegral_of_not_completeSpace
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_of_not_completeSpace (h : ¬CompleteSpace F) (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : ∫ᶜ x in γ, ω x = 0
decls.doc: curve integral is defined using Bochner integral, thus it is defined as zero whenever the codomain is not a complete space.

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_def
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_def [NormedSpace ℝ E] (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) (t : ℝ) : curveIntegralFun ω γ t = ω (γ.extend t) (derivWithin γ.extend I t)

decls.name: curveIntegral_def
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_def [NormedSpace ℝ F] (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : curveIntegral ω γ = ∫ t in 0..1, curveIntegralFun ω γ t

decls.name: curveIntegral_eq_intervalIntegral_deriv
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_eq_intervalIntegral_deriv [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : ∫ᶜ x in γ, ω x = ∫ t in 0..1, ω (γ.extend t) (deriv γ.extend t)

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_refl
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_refl (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (a : E) : curveIntegralFun ω (.refl a) = 0

decls.name: curveIntegral_refl
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_refl (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (a : E) : ∫ᶜ x in .refl a, ω x = 0

decls.name: CurveIntegrable.refl
decls.sig: theorem CurveIntegrable.refl (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (a : E) : CurveIntegrable ω (.refl a)

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_cast
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_cast (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) (hc : c = a) (hd : d = b) : curveIntegralFun ω (γ.cast hc hd) = curveIntegralFun ω γ

decls.name: curveIntegral_cast
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_cast (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) (hc : c = a) (hd : d = b) : ∫ᶜ x in γ.cast hc hd, ω x = ∫ᶜ x in γ, ω x

decls.name: curveIntegrable_cast_iff
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegrable_cast_iff (hc : c = a) (hd : d = b) : CurveIntegrable ω (γ.cast hc hd) ↔ CurveIntegrable ω γ

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_symm_apply
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_symm_apply (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) (t : ℝ) : curveIntegralFun ω γ.symm t = -curveIntegralFun ω γ (1 - t)

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_symm
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_symm (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : curveIntegralFun ω γ.symm = (-curveIntegralFun ω γ <| 1 - ·)

decls.name: CurveIntegrable.symm
decls.sig: protected theorem CurveIntegrable.symm (h : CurveIntegrable ω γ) : CurveIntegrable ω γ.symm

decls.name: curveIntegrable_symm
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegrable_symm : CurveIntegrable ω γ.symm ↔ CurveIntegrable ω γ

decls.name: curveIntegral_symm
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_symm (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γ : Path a b) : ∫ᶜ x in γ.symm, ω x = -∫ᶜ x in γ, ω x

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_trans_of_lt_half
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_trans_of_lt_half (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γab : Path a b) (γbc : Path b c) (ht : t < 1 / 2) : curveIntegralFun ω (γab.trans γbc) t = (2 : ℕ) • curveIntegralFun ω γab (2 * t)

decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_trans_of_half_lt (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γab : Path a b) (γbc : Path b c) (ht₀ : 1 / 2 < t) : curveIntegralFun ω (γab.trans γbc) t = (2 : ℕ) • curveIntegralFun ω γbc (2 * t - 1)

decls.name: curveIntegralFun_trans_aeeq_right
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegralFun_trans_aeeq_right (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (γab : Path a b) (γbc : Path b c) : curveIntegralFun ω (γab.trans γbc) =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Ι (1 / 2 : ℝ) 1)] fun t ↦ (2 : ℕ) • curveIntegralFun ω γbc (2 * t - 1)

decls.name: CurveIntegrable.intervalIntegrable_curveIntegralFun_trans_right

decls.name: curveIntegrable_segment

decls.name: curveIntegral_segment
decls.sig: theorem curveIntegral_segment [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (ω : E → E →L[𝕜] F) (a b : E) : ∫ᶜ x in .segment a b, ω x = ∫ t in 0..1, ω (lineMap a b t) (b - a)

decls.name: curveIntegral_segment_const

decls.name: exists_dist_slope_lt_pairwiseDisjoint_hasSum
decls.sig: lemma exists_dist_slope_lt_pairwiseDisjoint_hasSum {f f' : ℝ → F} {d b η : ℝ} (hdb : d ≤ b) (hf : ∀ᵐ x, x ∈ Ioo d b → HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (hη : 0 < η) : ∃ u : Set (ℝ × ℝ), (∀ z ∈ u, (d < z.1 ∧ z.1 < z.2 ∧ z.2 < b) ∧ dist (slope f z.1 z.2) (f' z.1) < η) ∧ u.PairwiseDisjoint (fun z ↦ Icc z.1 z.2) ∧ HasSum (fun (z : u) ↦ z.val.2 - z.val.1) (b - d)
decls.doc: If `f` has derivative `f'` a.e. on `[d, b]` and `η` is positive, then there is a collection of pairwise disjoint closed subintervals of `[a, b]` of total length `b - a` where the slope of `f` on each subinterval `[x, y]` differs from `f' x` by at most `η`.

decls.name: AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.dist_le_of_pairwiseDisjoint_hasSum

decls.doc: If `f` is absolutely continuous on `[d, b]` and there is a collection of pairwise disjoint closed subintervals of `(d, b)` of total length `b - d` such that the sum of `dist (f x) (f y)` for `[x, y]` in the collection is equal to `y`, then `dist (f b) (f d) ≤ y`.

decls.name: IntervalIntegrable
decls.sig: def IntervalIntegrable (f : ℝ → ε) (μ : Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f` is called *interval integrable* with respect to a measure `μ` on an unordered interval `a..b` if it is integrable on both intervals `(a, b]` and `(b, a]`. One of these intervals is always empty, so this property is equivalent to `f` being integrable on `(min a b, max a b]`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral
decls.sig: def intervalIntegral (f : ℝ → E) (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : E
decls.doc: The interval integral `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ` is defined as `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`. If `a ≤ b`, then it equals `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ`, otherwise it equals `-∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`.

decls.sig: theorem integral_mul_const {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] (r : 𝕜) (f : ℝ → 𝕜) : ∫ x in a..b, f x * r ∂μ = (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) * r

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_div
decls.sig: theorem integral_div {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] (r : 𝕜) (f : ℝ → 𝕜) : ∫ x in a..b, f x / r ∂μ = (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) / r

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_const'
decls.sig: theorem integral_const' [CompleteSpace E] (c : E) : ∫ _ in a..b, c ∂μ = (μ.real (Ioc a b) - μ.real (Ioc b a)) • c

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_const
decls.sig: theorem integral_const [CompleteSpace E] (c : E) : ∫ _ in a..b, c = (b - a) • c

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_smul_measure
decls.sig: nonrec theorem integral_smul_measure (c : ℝ≥0∞) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂c • μ = c.toReal • ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: RCLike.intervalIntegral_ofReal
decls.sig: nonrec theorem _root_.RCLike.intervalIntegral_ofReal {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {a b : ℝ} {μ : Measure ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} : (∫ x in a..b, (f x : 𝕜) ∂μ) = ↑(∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_ofReal
decls.sig: nonrec theorem integral_ofReal {a b : ℝ} {μ : Measure ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} : (∫ x in a..b, (f x : ℂ) ∂μ) = ↑(∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_apply
decls.sig: theorem _root_.ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_apply {a b : ℝ} {φ : ℝ → F →L[𝕜] E} (hφ : IntervalIntegrable φ μ a b) (v : F) : (∫ x in a..b, φ x ∂μ) v = ∫ x in a..b, φ x v ∂μ

decls.name: ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm
decls.sig: theorem _root_.ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm [CompleteSpace E] (L : E →L[𝕜] F) (hf : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : (∫ x in a..b, L (f x) ∂μ) = L (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: LinearIsometry.intervalIntegral_comp_comm
decls.sig: theorem _root_.LinearIsometry.intervalIntegral_comp_comm (L : E →ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) (f : ℝ → E) : ∫ x in a..b, L (f x) ∂μ = L (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_re
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_re (hf : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : ∫ x in a..b, RCLike.re (f x) ∂μ = RCLike.re (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_im
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_im (hf : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : ∫ x in a..b, RCLike.im (f x) ∂μ = RCLike.im (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_conj
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_conj : ∫ x in a..b, conj (f x) ∂μ = conj (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_right
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_mul_right (hc : c ≠ 0) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x * c)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a * c..b * c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_right
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_mul_right (c) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (x * c)) = ∫ x in a * c..b * c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_left
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_mul_left (hc : c ≠ 0) : (∫ x in a..b, f (c * x)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in c * a..c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_left
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_mul_left (c) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x)) = ∫ x in c * a..c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_div
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_div (hc : c ≠ 0) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x / c)) = c • ∫ x in a / c..b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_smul_integral_comp_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_smul_integral_comp_div (c) : (c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c)) = ∫ x in a / c..b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_right
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_add_right (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x + d)) = ∫ x in a + d..b + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_left
decls.sig: nonrec theorem integral_comp_add_left (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d + x)) = ∫ x in d + a..d + b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_add
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_mul_add (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (c * x + d)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in c * a + d..c * b + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_add
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_mul_add (c d) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x + d)) = ∫ x in c * a + d..c * b + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_mul
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_add_mul (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d + c * x)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in d + c * a..d + c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_add_mul
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_add_mul (c d) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (d + c * x)) = ∫ x in d + c * a..d + c * b, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_div_add
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_div_add (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x / c + d)) = c • ∫ x in a / c + d..b / c + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_smul_integral_comp_div_add
decls.sig: theorem inv_smul_integral_comp_div_add (c d) : (c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c + d)) = ∫ x in a / c + d..b / c + d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_div
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_add_div (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d + x / c)) = c • ∫ x in d + a / c..d + b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_smul_integral_comp_add_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_smul_integral_comp_add_div (c d) : (c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, f (d + x / c)) = ∫ x in d + a / c..d + b / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_sub
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_mul_sub (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (c * x - d)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in c * a - d..c * b - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_sub
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_mul_sub (c d) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (c * x - d)) = ∫ x in c * a - d..c * b - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_mul
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_sub_mul (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d - c * x)) = c⁻¹ • ∫ x in d - c * b..d - c * a, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_sub_mul
decls.sig: theorem smul_integral_comp_sub_mul (c d) : (c • ∫ x in a..b, f (d - c * x)) = ∫ x in d - c * b..d - c * a, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_div_sub
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_div_sub (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x / c - d)) = c • ∫ x in a / c - d..b / c - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_smul_integral_comp_div_sub
decls.sig: theorem inv_smul_integral_comp_div_sub (c d) : (c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, f (x / c - d)) = ∫ x in a / c - d..b / c - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_div
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_sub_div (hc : c ≠ 0) (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d - x / c)) = c • ∫ x in d - b / c..d - a / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.inv_smul_integral_comp_sub_div
decls.sig: theorem inv_smul_integral_comp_sub_div (c d) : (c⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, f (d - x / c)) = ∫ x in d - b / c..d - a / c, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_right
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_sub_right (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (x - d)) = ∫ x in a - d..b - d, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_left
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_sub_left (d) : (∫ x in a..b, f (d - x)) = ∫ x in d - b..d - a, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_comp_neg
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_neg : (∫ x in a..b, f (-x)) = ∫ x in -b..-a, f x

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr {a b : ℝ} (h : EqOn f g [[a, b]]) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ
decls.doc: If two functions are equal in the relevant interval, their interval integrals are also equal.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals_cancel
decls.sig: theorem integral_add_adjacent_intervals_cancel (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hbc : IntervalIntegrable f μ b c) : (((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) + ∫ x in b..c, f x ∂μ) + ∫ x in c..a, f x ∂μ) = 0

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals
decls.sig: theorem integral_add_adjacent_intervals (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hbc : IntervalIntegrable f μ b c) : ((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) + ∫ x in b..c, f x ∂μ) = ∫ x in a..c, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico
decls.sig: theorem sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico {a : ℕ → ℝ} {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (hint : ∀ k ∈ Ico m n, IntervalIntegrable f μ (a k) (a <| k + 1)) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico m n, ∫ x in a k..a <| k + 1, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a m..a n, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.sum_integral_adjacent_intervals
decls.sig: theorem sum_integral_adjacent_intervals {a : ℕ → ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hint : ∀ k < n, IntervalIntegrable f μ (a k) (a <| k + 1)) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ∫ x in a k..a <| k + 1, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in (a 0)..(a n), f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_sub_left (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hac : IntervalIntegrable f μ a c) : ((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in a..c, f x ∂μ) = ∫ x in c..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_add_interval_comm
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_add_interval_comm (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hcd : IntervalIntegrable f μ c d) (hac : IntervalIntegrable f μ a c) : ((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) + ∫ x in c..d, f x ∂μ) = (∫ x in a..d, f x ∂μ) + ∫ x in c..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_interval_comm
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_sub_interval_comm (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hcd : IntervalIntegrable f μ c d) (hac : IntervalIntegrable f μ a c) : ((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in c..d, f x ∂μ) = (∫ x in a..c, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in b..d, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_interval_comm'
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_sub_interval_comm' (hab : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hcd : IntervalIntegrable f μ c d) (hac : IntervalIntegrable f μ a c) : ((∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in c..d, f x ∂μ) = (∫ x in d..b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in c..a, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Iic_sub_Iic
decls.sig: theorem integral_Iic_sub_Iic (ha : IntegrableOn f (Iic a) μ) (hb : IntegrableOn f (Iic b) μ) : ((∫ x in Iic b, f x ∂μ) - ∫ x in Iic a, f x ∂μ) = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_add_Ioi
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_add_Ioi (ha : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a) μ) (hb : IntegrableOn f (Ioi b) μ) : ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f x ∂μ + ∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi b, f x ∂μ = ∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi a, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_interval_add_Ioi'
decls.sig: theorem integral_interval_add_Ioi' (ha : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hb : IntegrableOn f (Ioi b) μ) : ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f x ∂μ + ∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi b, f x ∂μ = ∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi a, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi
decls.sig: theorem integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a) μ) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∫ x in Ioi a, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioi b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi'
decls.sig: theorem integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi' (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a) μ) (hg : IntegrableOn f (Ioi b) μ) : ∫ x in Ioi a, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioi b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Iio_sub_Iio
decls.sig: theorem integral_Iio_sub_Iio (hf : IntegrableOn f (Iio b) μ) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∫ x in Iio b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Iio a, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in Ico a b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Iio_sub_Iio'
decls.sig: theorem integral_Iio_sub_Iio' [NullSingletonClass μ] (hf : IntegrableOn f (Iio b) μ) (hg : IntegrableOn f (Iio a) μ) : ∫ x in Iio b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Iio a, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Ici_sub_Ici
decls.sig: theorem integral_Ici_sub_Ici (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ici a) μ) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∫ x in Ici a, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ici b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in Ico a b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Ici_sub_Ici'
decls.sig: theorem integral_Ici_sub_Ici' [NullSingletonClass μ] (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ici a) μ) (hg : IntegrableOn f (Ici b) μ) : ∫ x in Ici a, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ici b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Iic_add_Ioi
decls.sig: theorem integral_Iic_add_Ioi (h_left : IntegrableOn f (Iic b) μ) (h_right : IntegrableOn f (Ioi b) μ) : (∫ x in Iic b, f x ∂μ) + (∫ x in Ioi b, f x ∂μ) = ∫ (x : ℝ), f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_Iio_add_Ici
decls.sig: theorem integral_Iio_add_Ici (h_left : IntegrableOn f (Iio b) μ) (h_right : IntegrableOn f (Ici b) μ) : (∫ x in Iio b, f x ∂μ) + (∫ x in Ici b, f x ∂μ) = ∫ (x : ℝ), f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_const_of_cdf
decls.sig: theorem integral_const_of_cdf [CompleteSpace E] [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (c : E) : ∫ _ in a..b, c ∂μ = (μ.real (Iic b) - μ.real (Iic a)) • c
decls.doc: If `μ` is a finite measure then `∫ x in a..b, c ∂μ = (μ (Iic b) - μ (Iic a)) • c`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_integral_of_support_subset
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_integral_of_support_subset {a b} (h : support f ⊆ Ioc a b) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae'
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_ae' (h : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ioc a b → f x = g x) (h' : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ioc b a → f x = g x) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_ae (h : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ι a b → f x = g x) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_uIoo
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_uIoo [NullSingletonClass μ] (h : (uIoo a b).EqOn f g) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_Ioo_of_le
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_Ioo_of_le [NullSingletonClass μ] (hab : a ≤ b) (h : (Ioo a b).EqOn f g) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae_restrict
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_ae_restrict {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → E} {μ : Measure ℝ} (h : f =ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ι a b)] g) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ
decls.doc: Integrals are equal for functions that agree almost everywhere for the restricted measure.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_congr_codiscreteWithin
decls.sig: theorem integral_congr_codiscreteWithin {a b : ℝ} {f₁ f₂ : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : f₁ =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin (Ι a b)] f₂) : ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f₁ x = ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f₂ x
decls.doc: Integrals are invariant when functions change along discrete sets.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_zero_ae
decls.sig: theorem integral_zero_ae (h : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ι a b → f x = 0) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = 0

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_indicator
decls.sig: nonrec theorem integral_indicator {a₁ a₂ a₃ : ℝ} (h : a₂ ∈ Icc a₁ a₃) : ∫ x in a₁..a₃, indicator {x | x ≤ a₂} f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a₁..a₂, f x ∂μ

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_zero_iff_of_le_of_nonneg_ae
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_zero_iff_of_le_of_nonneg_ae (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ioc a b)] f) (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ioc a b)] 0

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae
decls.sig: theorem integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae (hf : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ioc a b ∪ Ioc b a)] f) (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ioc a b ∪ Ioc b a)] 0

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae'
decls.sig: theorem integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae' (hf : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ι a b)] f) (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : (0 < ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) ↔ a < b ∧ 0 < μ (support f ∩ Ioc a b)
decls.doc: If `f` is nonnegative and integrable on the unordered interval `Set.uIoc a b`, then its integral over `a..b` is positive if and only if `a < b` and the measure of `Function.support f ∩ Set.Ioc a b` is positive.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae
decls.sig: theorem integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae (hf : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] f) (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : (0 < ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) ↔ a < b ∧ 0 < μ (support f ∩ Ioc a b)
decls.doc: If `f` is nonnegative a.e.-everywhere and it is integrable on the unordered interval `Set.uIoc a b`, then its integral over `a..b` is positive if and only if `a < b` and the measure of `Function.support f ∩ Set.Ioc a b` is positive.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b) (hpos : ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ Ioo a b → 0 < f x) (hab : a < b) : 0 < ∫ x : ℝ in a..b, f x
decls.doc: If `f : ℝ → ℝ` is integrable on `(a, b]` for real numbers `a < b`, and positive on the interior of the interval, then its integral over `a..b` is strictly positive.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureSpace.volume a b) (hpos : ∀ x, 0 < f x) (hab : a < b) : 0 < ∫ x in a..b, f x
decls.doc: If `f : ℝ → ℝ` is strictly positive everywhere, and integrable on `(a, b]` for real numbers `a < b`, then its integral over `a..b` is strictly positive. (See `intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on` for a version only assuming positivity of `f` on `(a, b)` rather than everywhere.)

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_lt_integral_of_ae_le_of_measure_setOfPred_lt_ne_zero
decls.sig: theorem integral_lt_integral_of_ae_le_of_measure_setOfPred_lt_ne_zero (hab : a ≤ b) (hfi : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (hgi : IntervalIntegrable g μ a b) (hle : f ≤ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ioc a b)] g) (hlt : μ.restrict (Ioc a b) {x | f x < g x} ≠ 0) : (∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) < ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ
decls.doc: If `f` and `g` are two functions that are interval integrable on `a..b`, `a ≤ b`, `f x ≤ g x` for a.e. `x ∈ Set.Ioc a b`, and `f x < g x` on a subset of `Set.Ioc a b` of nonzero measure, then `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ < ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ`.

decls.name: intervalIntegral.integral_lt_integral_of_continuousOn_of_le_of_exists_lt
decls.sig: theorem integral_lt_integral_of_continuousOn_of_le_of_exists_lt {f g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hgc : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b)) (hle : ∀ x ∈ Ioc a b, f x ≤ g x) (hlt : ∃ c ∈ Icc a b, f c < g c) : (∫ x in a..b, f x) < ∫ x in a..b, g x

decls.name: Function.Periodic.intervalIntegrable_iff
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable_iff {t₁ t₂ : ℝ} (hf : Periodic f T) : IntervalIntegrable f volume t₁ (t₁ + T) ↔ IntervalIntegrable f volume t₂ (t₂ + T)
decls.doc: A periodic function is interval integrable over one full period if and only if it is interval integrable over any other full period. Special case of `Function.Periodic.intervalIntegrable`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.intervalIntegrable₀
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegrable₀ (h₁f : Function.Periodic f T) (hT : T ≠ 0) (h₂f : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume 0 T) (a₁ a₂ : ℝ) : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a₁ a₂
decls.doc: Special case of `Function.Periodic.intervalIntegrable`: A periodic function is interval integrable over every interval if it is interval integrable over the period starting from zero.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_add_eq (hf : Periodic f T) (t s : ℝ) : ∫ x in t..t + T, f x = ∫ x in s..s + T, f x
decls.doc: If `f` is a periodic function with period `T`, then its integral over `[t, t + T]` does not depend on `t`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq_add
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_add_eq_add (hf : Periodic f T) (t s : ℝ) (h_int : ∀ t₁ t₂, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureSpace.volume t₁ t₂) : ∫ x in t..s + T, f x = (∫ x in t..s, f x) + ∫ x in t..t + T, f x
decls.doc: If `f` is an integrable periodic function with period `T`, then its integral over `[t, s + T]` is the sum of its integrals over the intervals `[t, s]` and `[t, t + T]`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_zsmul_eq
decls.sig: theorem intervalIntegral_add_zsmul_eq (hf : Periodic f T) (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) (h_int : ∀ t₁ t₂, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureSpace.volume t₁ t₂) : ∫ x in t..t + n • T, f x = n • ∫ x in t..t + T, f x
decls.doc: If `f` is an integrable periodic function with period `T`, and `n` is an integer, then its integral over `[t, t + n • T]` is `n` times its integral over `[t, t + T]`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.sInf_add_zsmul_le_integral_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem sInf_add_zsmul_le_integral_of_pos (h_int : IntervalIntegrable g MeasureSpace.volume 0 T) (hT : 0 < T) (t : ℝ) : (sInf ((fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) '' Icc 0 T) + ⌊t / T⌋ • ∫ x in 0..T, g x) ≤ ∫ x in 0..t, g x
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0`, then for any `t : ℝ`, the function `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` is bounded below by `t ↦ X + ⌊t/T⌋ • Y` for appropriate constants `X` and `Y`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.integral_le_sSup_add_zsmul_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem integral_le_sSup_add_zsmul_of_pos (h_int : IntervalIntegrable g MeasureSpace.volume 0 T) (hT : 0 < T) (t : ℝ) : (∫ x in 0..t, g x) ≤ sSup ((fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) '' Icc 0 T) + ⌊t / T⌋ • ∫ x in 0..T, g x
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0`, then for any `t : ℝ`, the function `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` is bounded above by `t ↦ X + ⌊t/T⌋ • Y` for appropriate constants `X` and `Y`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.tendsto_atTop_intervalIntegral_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_atTop_intervalIntegral_of_pos (h₀ : 0 < ∫ x in 0..T, g x) (hT : 0 < T) : Tendsto (fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) atTop atTop
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0` and `0 < ∫ x in 0..T, g x`, then `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` tends to `∞` as `t` tends to `∞`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.tendsto_atBot_intervalIntegral_of_pos
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_atBot_intervalIntegral_of_pos (h₀ : 0 < ∫ x in 0..T, g x) (hT : 0 < T) : Tendsto (fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) atBot atBot
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0` and `0 < ∫ x in 0..T, g x`, then `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` tends to `-∞` as `t` tends to `-∞`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.tendsto_atTop_intervalIntegral_of_pos'
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_atTop_intervalIntegral_of_pos' (h_int : IntervalIntegrable g MeasureSpace.volume 0 T) (h₀ : ∀ x, 0 < g x) (hT : 0 < T) : Tendsto (fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) atTop atTop
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0` and `∀ x, 0 < g x`, then `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` tends to `∞` as `t` tends to `∞`.

decls.name: Function.Periodic.tendsto_atBot_intervalIntegral_of_pos'
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_atBot_intervalIntegral_of_pos' (h_int : IntervalIntegrable g MeasureSpace.volume 0 T) (h₀ : ∀ x, 0 < g x) (hT : 0 < T) : Tendsto (fun t => ∫ x in 0..t, g x) atBot atBot
decls.doc: If `g : ℝ → ℝ` is periodic with period `T > 0` and `∀ x, 0 < g x`, then `t ↦ ∫ x in 0..t, g x` tends to `-∞` as `t` tends to `-∞`.

decls.name: IntervalIntegrable.intervalIntegrable_slope
decls.sig: theorem IntervalIntegrable.intervalIntegrable_slope {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b c : ℝ} (hf : IntervalIntegrable f volume a (b + c)) (hab : a ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c)) volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is interval integrable on `a..(b + c)` where `a ≤ b` and `0 ≤ c`, then `fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c)` is interval integrable on `a..b`.

decls.name: MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_slope
decls.sig: theorem MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_slope {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b c : ℝ} (hf : MonotoneOn f (Icc a (b + c))) (hab : a ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : IntervalIntegrable (fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c)) volume a b
decls.doc: If `f` is monotone on `a..(b + c)` where `a ≤ b` and `0 ≤ c`, then `fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c)` is interval integrable on `a..b`.

decls.name: MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_slope_le
decls.sig: theorem MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_slope_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b c : ℝ} (hf : MonotoneOn f (Icc a (b + c))) (hab : a ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : ∫ x in a..b, slope f x (x + c) ≤ f (b + c) - f a
decls.doc: If `f` is monotone on `a..(b + c)` where `a ≤ b` and `0 ≤ c`, then the interval integral of `fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c)` on `a..b` is at most `f (b + c) - f a`.

decls.name: trapezoidal_integral
decls.sig: noncomputable def trapezoidal_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: Integration of `f` from `a` to `b` using the trapezoidal rule with `N+1` total evaluations of `f`. (Note the off-by-one problem here: `N` counts the number of trapezoids, not the number of evaluations.)

decls.name: trapezoidal_error
decls.sig: noncomputable def trapezoidal_error (f : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The absolute error of trapezoidal integration.

decls.name: trapezoidal_integral_symm
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_integral_symm (f : ℝ → ℝ) {N : ℕ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) (a b : ℝ) : trapezoidal_integral f N a b = -(trapezoidal_integral f N b a)
decls.doc: Just like exact integration, the trapezoidal approximation retains the same magnitude but changes sign when the endpoints are swapped.

decls.name: trapezoidal_error_symm
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_error_symm (f : ℝ → ℝ) {N : ℕ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) (a b : ℝ) : trapezoidal_error f N a b = -trapezoidal_error f N b a
decls.doc: The absolute error of the trapezoidal rule does not change when the endpoints are swapped.

decls.name: trapezoidal_integral_eq
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_integral_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (a : ℝ) : trapezoidal_integral f N a a = 0
decls.doc: Just like exact integration, the trapezoidal integration from `a` to `a` is zero.

decls.name: trapezoidal_error_eq
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_error_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (a : ℝ) : trapezoidal_error f N a a = 0
decls.doc: The error of the trapezoidal integration from `a` to `a` is zero.

decls.name: trapezoidal_integral_one
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_integral_one (f : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : trapezoidal_integral f 1 a b = (b - a) / 2 * (f a + f b)
decls.doc: An exact formula for integration with a single trapezoid (the "midpoint rule").

decls.name: sum_trapezoidal_integral_adjacent_intervals
decls.sig: theorem sum_trapezoidal_integral_adjacent_intervals {f : ℝ → ℝ} {N : ℕ} {a h : ℝ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) : ∑ i ∈ range N, trapezoidal_integral f 1 (a + i * h) (a + (i + 1) * h) = trapezoidal_integral f N a (a + N * h)
decls.doc: A basic trapezoidal equivalent to `IntervalIntegral.sum_integral_adjacent_intervals`. More general theorems are certainly possible, but many of them can be derived from repeated applications of this one.

decls.name: trapezoidal_integral_ext
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_integral_ext {f : ℝ → ℝ} {N : ℕ} {a h : ℝ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) : trapezoidal_integral f N a (a + N * h) + trapezoidal_integral f 1 (a + N * h) (a + (N + 1) * h) = trapezoidal_integral f (N + 1) a (a + (N + 1) * h)
decls.doc: A simplified version of the previous theorem, for use in proofs by induction and the like.

decls.name: sum_trapezoidal_error_adjacent_intervals
decls.sig: theorem sum_trapezoidal_error_adjacent_intervals {f : ℝ → ℝ} {N : ℕ} {a h : ℝ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) (h_f_int : IntervalIntegrable f volume a (a + N * h)) : ∑ i ∈ range N, trapezoidal_error f 1 (a + i * h) (a + (i + 1) * h) = trapezoidal_error f N a (a + N * h)
decls.doc: Since we have `sum_[]_adjacent_intervals` theorems for both exact and trapezoidal integration, it's natural to combine them into a similar formula for the error. This theorem is in particular used in the proof of the general error bound.

decls.name: trapezoidal_error_le
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_error_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (h_df : DifferentiableOn ℝ f [[a, b]]) (h_ddf : DifferentiableOn ℝ (derivWithin f [[a, b]]) [[a, b]]) {ζ : ℝ} (fpp_bound : ∀ x, |iteratedDerivWithin 2 f [[a, b]] x| ≤ ζ) {N : ℕ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) : |trapezoidal_error f N a b| ≤ |b - a| ^ 3 * ζ / (12 * N ^ 2)
decls.doc: The standard error bound for trapezoidal integration on the general interval `[[a, b]]`.

decls.name: trapezoidal_error_le_of_c2
decls.sig: theorem trapezoidal_error_le_of_c2 {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (h_f_c2 : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 f [[a, b]]) {ζ : ℝ} (fpp_bound : ∀ x, |iteratedDerivWithin 2 f [[a, b]] x| ≤ ζ) {N : ℕ} (N_nonzero : 0 < N) : |trapezoidal_error f N a b| ≤ |b - a| ^ 3 * ζ / (12 * N ^ 2)
decls.doc: The error bound for trapezoidal integration in the slightly weaker, but very common, case where `f` is `C^2`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_iSup
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_iSup {f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ n, Measurable (f n)) (h_mono : Monotone f) : ∫⁻ a, ⨆ n, f n a ∂μ = ⨆ n, ∫⁻ a, f n a ∂μ
decls.doc: **Monotone convergence theorem**, version with `Measurable` functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_iSup'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_iSup' {f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (f n) μ) (h_mono : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Monotone fun n => f n x) : ∫⁻ a, ⨆ n, f n a ∂μ = ⨆ n, ∫⁻ a, f n a ∂μ
decls.doc: **Monotone convergence theorem**, version with `AEMeasurable` functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_monotone
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_monotone {f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} {F : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (f n) μ) (h_mono : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Monotone fun n => f n x) (h_tendsto : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 <| F x)) : Tendsto (fun n => ∫⁻ x, f n x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 <| ∫⁻ x, F x ∂μ)
decls.doc: **Monotone convergence theorem** expressed with limits.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_iSup_ae
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_iSup_ae {f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ n, Measurable (f n)) (h_mono : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, f n a ≤ f n.succ a) : ∫⁻ a, ⨆ n, f n a ∂μ = ⨆ n, ∫⁻ a, f n a ∂μ
decls.doc: Weaker version of the **monotone convergence theorem**.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_iSup_directed_of_measurable
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_iSup_directed_of_measurable [Countable β] {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ b, Measurable (f b)) (h_directed : Directed (· ≤ ·) f) : ∫⁻ a, ⨆ b, f b a ∂μ = ⨆ b, ∫⁻ a, f b a ∂μ
decls.doc: **Monotone convergence theorem** for a supremum over a directed family and indexed by a countable type.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_iSup_directed
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_iSup_directed [Countable β] {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ b, AEMeasurable (f b) μ) (h_directed : Directed (· ≤ ·) f) : ∫⁻ a, ⨆ b, f b a ∂μ = ⨆ b, ∫⁻ a, f b a ∂μ
decls.doc: **Monotone convergence theorem** for a supremum over a directed family and indexed by a countable type.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_liminf_le'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_liminf_le' {ι : Type*} {f : ι → α → ℝ≥0∞} {u : Filter ι} [IsCountablyGenerated u] (h_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (f i) μ) : ∫⁻ a, liminf (fun i => f i a) u ∂μ ≤ liminf (fun i => ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ) u
decls.doc: **Fatou's lemma**, version with `AEMeasurable` functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_liminf_le
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_liminf_le {ι : Type*} {f : ι → α → ℝ≥0∞} {u : Filter ι} [IsCountablyGenerated u] (h_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (f i)) : ∫⁻ a, liminf (fun i => f i a) u ∂μ ≤ liminf (fun i => ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ) u
decls.doc: **Fatou's lemma**, version with `Measurable` functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_iSup_eapprox_lintegral
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_eq_iSup_eapprox_lintegral {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ⨆ n, (eapprox f n).lintegral μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_iSup_eapprox_lintegral'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_eq_iSup_eapprox_lintegral' {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ⨆ n, (eapprox (hf.mk f) n).lintegral μ
decls.doc: Generalization of `lintegral_eq_iSup_eapprox_lintegral` to ae-measurable functions.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eapprox_le_lintegral
decls.sig: lemma lintegral_eapprox_le_lintegral {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (n : ℕ) : (eapprox f n).lintegral μ ≤ ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.measure_support_eapprox_lt_top
decls.sig: lemma measure_support_eapprox_lt_top {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf_meas : Measurable f) (hf : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞) (n : ℕ) : μ (Function.support (eapprox f n)) < ∞

decls.name: MeasureTheory.le_lintegral_add
decls.sig: theorem le_lintegral_add (f g : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ
decls.doc: The sum of the lower Lebesgue integrals of two functions is less than or equal to the integral of their sum. The other inequality needs one of these functions to be (a.e.-)measurable.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_aux
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_add_aux {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g) : ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_left
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_add_left {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ
decls.doc: If `f g : α → ℝ≥0∞` are two functions and one of them is (a.e.) measurable, then the Lebesgue integral of `f + g` equals the sum of integrals. This lemma assumes that `f` is integrable, see also `MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_right` and primed versions of these lemmas.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_left'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_add_left' {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_right'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_add_right' (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) : ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_right
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_add_right (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : Measurable g) : ∫⁻ a, f a + g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ
decls.doc: If `f g : α → ℝ≥0∞` are two functions and one of them is (a.e.) measurable, then the Lebesgue integral of `f + g` equals the sum of integrals. This lemma assumes that `g` is integrable, see also `MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_left` and primed versions of these lemmas.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_finsetSum'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_finsetSum' (s : Finset β) {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ b ∈ s, AEMeasurable (f b) μ) : ∫⁻ a, ∑ b ∈ s, f b a ∂μ = ∑ b ∈ s, ∫⁻ a, f b a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_finsetSum
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_finsetSum (s : Finset β) {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ b ∈ s, Measurable (f b)) : ∫⁻ a, ∑ b ∈ s, f b a ∂μ = ∑ b ∈ s, ∫⁻ a, f b a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_tsum [Countable β] {f : β → α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (f i) μ) : ∫⁻ a, ∑' i, f i a ∂μ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_const_mul
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_const_mul (r : ℝ≥0∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ a, r * f a ∂μ = r * ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_const_mul''
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_const_mul'' (r : ℝ≥0∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) : ∫⁻ a, r * f a ∂μ = r * ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_const_mul_le
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_const_mul_le (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : r * ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, r * f a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_const_mul'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_const_mul' (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : r ≠ ∞) : ∫⁻ a, r * f a ∂μ = r * ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_const
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_mul_const (r : ℝ≥0∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ a, f a * r ∂μ = (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) * r

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_const''
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_mul_const'' (r : ℝ≥0∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) : ∫⁻ a, f a * r ∂μ = (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) * r

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_const_le
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_mul_const_le (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) * r ≤ ∫⁻ a, f a * r ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_const'
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_mul_const' (r : ℝ≥0∞) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hr : r ≠ ∞) : ∫⁻ a, f a * r ∂μ = (∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) * r

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_lintegral_mul
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_lintegral_mul {β} [MeasurableSpace β] {ν : Measure β} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} {g : β → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (hg : AEMeasurable g ν) : ∫⁻ x, ∫⁻ y, f x * g y ∂ν ∂μ = (∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ) * ∫⁻ y, g y ∂ν
decls.doc: A double integral of a product where each factor contains only one variable is a product of integrals

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_lintegral_mul_le

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_trim

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_measurable_le_lintegral_eq

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_nnreal
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_eq_nnreal {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ⨆ (φ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0) (_ : ∀ x, ↑(φ x) ≤ f x), (φ.map ((↑) : ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0∞)).lintegral μ
decls.doc: `∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ` is defined as the supremum of integrals of simple functions `φ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0∞` such that `φ ≤ f`. This lemma says that it suffices to take functions `φ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_simpleFunc_forall_lintegral_sub_lt_of_pos

decls.doc: Lebesgue integral over a set is monotone in function. This version assumes that the upper estimate is an a.e. measurable function and the estimate holds a.e. on the set. See also `setLIntegral_mono_ae'` for a version that assumes measurability of the set but assumes no regularity of either function.

decls.sig: theorem lintegral_eq_zero_iff' {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] 0
decls.doc: The Lebesgue integral is zero iff the function is a.e. zero. The measurability assumption is necessary, otherwise there are counterexamples: for instance, the conclusion fails if `f` is the characteristic function of a Vitali set.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_zero_iff

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_pos_setLIntegral_lt_of_measure_lt
decls.sig: theorem exists_pos_setLIntegral_lt_of_measure_lt {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≠ 0) : ∃ δ > 0, ∀ s, μ s < δ → ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ < ε
decls.doc: If `f` has finite integral, then `∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ` is absolutely continuous in `s`: it tends to zero as `μ s` tends to zero. This lemma states this fact in terms of `ε` and `δ`.

decls.doc: If `f` has finite integral, then `∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ` is absolutely continuous in `s`: it tends to zero as `μ s` tends to zero.

decls.sig: theorem lintegral_max {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) : ∫⁻ x, max (f x) (g x) ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in { x | f x ≤ g x }, g x ∂μ + ∫⁻ x in { x | g x < f x }, f x ∂μ

decls.sig: theorem rieszContentAux_le {K : Compacts X} {f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)} (h : ∀ x ∈ K, (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ f x) : rieszContentAux Λ K ≤ Λ f
decls.doc: Any compactly supported continuous nonnegative `f` such that `f ≥ 1` on `K` gives an upper bound on the content of `K`; namely `λ(K) ≤ Λ f`.

decls.name: exists_lt_rieszContentAux_add_pos
decls.sig: theorem exists_lt_rieszContentAux_add_pos (K : Compacts X) {ε : ℝ≥0} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∃ f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0), (∀ x ∈ K, (1 : ℝ≥0) ≤ f x) ∧ Λ f < rieszContentAux Λ K + ε
decls.doc: The Riesz content can be approximated arbitrarily well by evaluating the positive linear functional on test functions: for any `ε > 0`, there exists a compactly supported continuous nonnegative function `f` on `X` such that `f ≥ 1` on `K` and such that `λ(K) ≤ Λ f < λ(K) + ε`.

decls.name: rieszContentAux_sup_le
decls.sig: theorem rieszContentAux_sup_le (K1 K2 : Compacts X) : rieszContentAux Λ (K1 ⊔ K2) ≤ rieszContentAux Λ K1 + rieszContentAux Λ K2
decls.doc: The Riesz content `λ` associated to a given positive linear functional `Λ` is finitely subadditive: `λ(K₁ ∪ K₂) ≤ λ(K₁) + λ(K₂)` for any compact subsets `K₁, K₂ ⊆ X`.

decls.name: exists_continuous_add_one_of_isCompact_nnreal
decls.sig: lemma exists_continuous_add_one_of_isCompact_nnreal {s₀ s₁ : Set X} {t : Set X} (s₀_compact : IsCompact s₀) (s₁_compact : IsCompact s₁) (t_compact : IsCompact t) (disj : Disjoint s₀ s₁) (hst : s₀ ∪ s₁ ⊆ t) : ∃ (f₀ f₁ : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)), EqOn f₀ 1 s₀ ∧ EqOn f₁ 1 s₁ ∧ EqOn (f₀ + f₁) 1 t

decls.name: rieszContentAux_union
decls.sig: lemma rieszContentAux_union {K₁ K₂ : TopologicalSpace.Compacts X} (disj : Disjoint (K₁ : Set X) K₂) : rieszContentAux Λ (K₁ ⊔ K₂) = rieszContentAux Λ K₁ + rieszContentAux Λ K₂

decls.doc: The content induced by the linear functional `Λ`.

decls.name: NNRealRMK.rieszMeasure
decls.sig: def rieszMeasure
decls.doc: `rieszContent` gives a `Content` from `Λ : C_c(X, ℝ≥0) →ₗ[ℝ≥0] ℝ≥0`. Here `rieszContent Λ` is promoted to a measure. It will be later shown that `∫ (x : X), f x ∂(rieszMeasure Λ hΛ) = Λ f` for all `f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)`.
