decls.name: NNRealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure
decls.sig: theorem integral_rieszMeasure (f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)) : ∫ (x : X), (f x : ℝ) ∂(rieszMeasure Λ) = Λ f
decls.doc: The **Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem**: given a positive linear functional `Λ`, the (Bochner) integral of `f` (as a `ℝ`-valued function) with respect to the `rieszMeasure` associated to `Λ` is equal to `Λ f`.

decls.name: NNRealRMK.lintegral_rieszMeasure
decls.sig: theorem lintegral_rieszMeasure (f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)) : ∫⁻ (x : X), f x ∂(rieszMeasure Λ) = Λ f
decls.doc: The **Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem**: given a positive linear functional `Λ`, the (lower) Lebesgue integral of `f` with respect to the `rieszMeasure` associated to `Λ` is equal to `Λ f`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported_nnreal
decls.sig: theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported_nnreal {μ ν : Measure X} [μ.Regular] [ν.Regular] (hμν : ∀ (f : C_c(X, ℝ≥0)), ∫ (x : X), (f x : ℝ) ∂μ = ∫ (x : X), (f x : ℝ) ∂ν) : μ = ν
decls.doc: If two regular measures give the same integral for every function in `C_c(X, ℝ≥0)`, then they are equal.

decls.name: NNRealRMK.integralLinearMap_inj
decls.sig: theorem integralLinearMap_inj {μ ν : Measure X} [μ.Regular] [ν.Regular] : integralLinearMap μ = integralLinearMap ν ↔ μ = ν
decls.doc: If two regular measures induce the same linear functional on `C_c(X, ℝ≥0)`, then they are equal.

decls.doc: Every regular measure is induced by a positive linear functional on `C_c(X, ℝ≥0)`. That is, `NNRealRMK.rieszMeasure` is a surjective function onto regular measures.

decls.name: RealRMK.range_cut_partition
decls.sig: lemma range_cut_partition (f : C_c(X, ℝ)) (a : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (N : ℕ) (hf : range f ⊆ Ioo a (a + N * ε)) : ∃ (E : Fin N → Set X), tsupport f = ⋃ j, E j ∧ univ.PairwiseDisjoint E ∧ (∀ n : Fin N, ∀ x ∈ E n, a + ε * n < f x ∧ f x ≤ a + ε * (n + 1)) ∧ ∀ n : Fin N, MeasurableSet (E n)
decls.doc: Given `f : C_c(X, ℝ)` such that `range f ⊆ [a, b]` we obtain a partition of the support of `f` determined by partitioning `[a, b]` into `N` pieces.

decls.doc: Given a set `E`, a function `f : C_c(X, ℝ)`, `0 < ε` and `∀ x ∈ E, f x < c`, there exists an open set `V` such that `E ⊆ V` and the sets are similar in measure and `∀ x ∈ V, f x < c`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero_aux1
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero_aux1 (s : Set E) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) (t : Set E) (u : Set E) (h'u : μ u ≠ 0) (t_bound : t ⊆ closedBall 0 1) : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)) / μ ({x} + r • u)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero_aux2
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero_aux2 (s : Set E) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) (t : Set E) (u : Set E) (h'u : μ u ≠ 0) (R : ℝ) (Rpos : 0 < R) (t_bound : t ⊆ closedBall 0 R) : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)) / μ ({x} + r • u)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_zero_of_density_zero (s : Set E) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) (t : Set E) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (h''t : μ t ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)) / μ ({x} + r • t)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: Consider a point `x` at which a set `s` has density zero, with respect to closed balls. Then it also has density zero with respect to any measurable set `t`: the proportion of points in `s` belonging to a rescaled copy `{x} + r • t` of `t` tends to zero as `r` tends to zero.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_one_of_density_one_aux
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_one_of_density_one_aux (s : Set E) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)) (t : Set E) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (h't : μ t ≠ 0) (h''t : μ t ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)) / μ ({x} + r • t)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_one_of_density_one
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_addHaar_inter_smul_one_of_density_one (s : Set E) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)) (t : Set E) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (h't : μ t ≠ 0) (h''t : μ t ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)) / μ ({x} + r • t)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
decls.doc: Consider a point `x` at which a set `s` has density one, with respect to closed balls (i.e., a Lebesgue density point of `s`). Then `s` has also density one at `x` with respect to any measurable set `t`: the proportion of points in `s` belonging to a rescaled copy `{x} + r • t` of `t` tends to one a

decls.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.eventually_nonempty_inter_smul_of_density_one
decls.sig: theorem eventually_nonempty_inter_smul_of_density_one (s : Set E) (x : E) (h : Tendsto (fun r => μ (s ∩ closedBall x r) / μ (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)) (t : Set E) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (h't : μ t ≠ 0) : ∀ᶠ r in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), (s ∩ ({x} + r • t)).Nonempty
decls.doc: Consider a point `x` at which a set `s` has density one, with respect to closed balls (i.e., a Lebesgue density point of `s`). Then `s` intersects the rescaled copies `{x} + r • t` of a given set `t` with positive measure, for any small enough `r`.

decls.name: volume_regionBetween_eq_integral'
decls.sig: theorem volume_regionBetween_eq_integral' [SigmaFinite μ] (f_int : IntegrableOn f s μ) (g_int : IntegrableOn g s μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hfg : f ≤ᵐ[μ.restrict s] g) : μ.prod volume (regionBetween f g s) = ENNReal.ofReal (∫ y in s, (g - f) y ∂μ)

decls.name: volume_regionBetween_eq_integral
decls.sig: theorem volume_regionBetween_eq_integral [SigmaFinite μ] (f_int : IntegrableOn f s μ) (g_int : IntegrableOn g s μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hfg : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ g x) : μ.prod volume (regionBetween f g s) = ENNReal.ofReal (∫ y in s, (g - f) y ∂μ)
decls.doc: If two functions are integrable on a measurable set, and one function is less than or equal to the other on that set, then the volume of the region between the two functions can be represented as an integral.

decls.name: Real.integrable_of_summable_norm_Icc
decls.sig: theorem Real.integrable_of_summable_norm_Icc {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {f : C(ℝ, E)} (hf : Summable fun n : ℤ => ‖(f.comp <| ContinuousMap.addRight n).restrict (Icc 0 1)‖) : Integrable f
decls.doc: If the sequence with `n`-th term the sup norm of `fun x ↦ f (x + n)` on the interval `Icc 0 1`, for `n ∈ ℤ`, is summable, then `f` is integrable on `ℝ`.

decls.name: integral_comp_neg_Iic
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_neg_Iic {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (c : ℝ) (f : ℝ → E) : (∫ x in Iic c, f (-x)) = ∫ x in Ioi (-c), f x

decls.name: integral_comp_neg_Ioi
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_neg_Ioi {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (c : ℝ) (f : ℝ → E) : (∫ x in Ioi c, f (-x)) = ∫ x in Iic (-c), f x

decls.name: integral_comp_abs
decls.sig: theorem integral_comp_abs {f : ℝ → ℝ} : ∫ x, f |x| = 2 * ∫ x in Ioi (0 : ℝ), f x

decls.name: MeasureTheory.measure_unitBall_eq_integral_div_gamma
decls.sig: theorem MeasureTheory.measure_unitBall_eq_integral_div_gamma {E : Type*} {p : ℝ} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (μ : Measure E) [IsAddHaarMeasure μ] (hp : 0 < p) : μ (Metric.ball 0 1) = .ofReal ((∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-‖x‖ ^ p) ∂μ) / Real.Gamma (finrank ℝ E / p + 1))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.measure_lt_one_eq_integral_div_gamma
decls.sig: theorem MeasureTheory.measure_lt_one_eq_integral_div_gamma {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) : μ {x : E | g x < 1} = .ofReal ((∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-(g x) ^ p) ∂μ) / Real.Gamma (finrank ℝ E / p + 1))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.measure_le_eq_lt
decls.sig: theorem MeasureTheory.measure_le_eq_lt [Nontrivial E] (r : ℝ) : μ {x : E | g x ≤ r} = μ {x : E | g x < r}

decls.name: MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_lt_one

decls.name: MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_lt
decls.sig: theorem MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_lt [Nonempty ι] {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (r : ℝ) : volume {x : ι → ℝ | (∑ i, |x i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) < r} = (.ofReal r) ^ card ι * .ofReal ((2 * Gamma (1 / p + 1)) ^ card ι / Gamma (card ι / p + 1))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_le
decls.sig: theorem MeasureTheory.volume_sum_rpow_le [Nonempty ι] {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (r : ℝ) : volume {x : ι → ℝ | (∑ i, |x i| ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ r} = (.ofReal r) ^ card ι * .ofReal ((2 * Gamma (1 / p + 1)) ^ card ι / Gamma (card ι / p + 1))

decls.name: Complex.volume_sum_rpow_lt_one
decls.sig: theorem Complex.volume_sum_rpow_lt_one {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : volume {x : ι → ℂ | ∑ i, ‖x i‖ ^ p < 1} = .ofReal ((π * Real.Gamma (2 / p + 1)) ^ card ι / Real.Gamma (2 * card ι / p + 1))

decls.name: Complex.volume_sum_rpow_lt
decls.sig: theorem Complex.volume_sum_rpow_lt [Nonempty ι] {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (r : ℝ) : volume {x : ι → ℂ | (∑ i, ‖x i‖ ^ p) ^ (1 / p) < r} = (.ofReal r) ^ (2 * card ι) * .ofReal ((π * Real.Gamma (2 / p + 1)) ^ card ι / Real.Gamma (2 * card ι / p + 1))

decls.name: Complex.volume_sum_rpow_le
decls.sig: theorem Complex.volume_sum_rpow_le [Nonempty ι] {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (r : ℝ) : volume {x : ι → ℂ | (∑ i, ‖x i‖ ^ p) ^ (1 / p) ≤ r} = (.ofReal r) ^ (2 * card ι) * .ofReal ((π * Real.Gamma (2 / p + 1)) ^ card ι / Real.Gamma (2 * card ι / p + 1))

decls.name: InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall

decls.name: InnerProductSpace.volume_ball_of_dim_odd

decls.name: InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall_of_dim_odd

decls.name: Filter
decls.sig: structure Filter (α : Type*) where
decls.doc: A filter `F` on a type `α` is a collection of sets of `α` which contains the whole `α`, is upwards-closed, and is stable under intersection. We do not forbid this collection to be all sets of `α`.

decls.doc: Construct a filter from a property that is stable under finite unions. A set `s` belongs to `Filter.comk p _ _ _` iff its complement satisfies the predicate `p`. This constructor is useful to define filters like `Filter.cofinite`.

decls.doc: The *kernel* of a filter is the intersection of all its sets.

decls.doc: The join of a filter of filters is defined by the relation `s ∈ join f ↔ {t | s ∈ t} ∈ f`.

decls.sig: class NeBot (f : Filter α) : Prop where
decls.doc: A filter is `NeBot` if it is not equal to `⊥`, or equivalently the empty set does not belong to the filter. Bourbaki include this assumption in the definition of a filter but we prefer to have a `CompleteLattice` structure on `Filter _`, so we use a typeclass argument in lemmas instead.

decls.name: Filter.Eventually
decls.sig: protected def Eventually (p : α → Prop) (f : Filter α) : Prop
decls.doc: `f.Eventually p` or `∀ᶠ x in f, p x` mean that `{x | p x} ∈ f`. E.g., `∀ᶠ x in atTop, p x` means that `p` holds true for sufficiently large `x`.

decls.name: Filter.Frequently
decls.sig: protected def Frequently (p : α → Prop) (f : Filter α) : Prop
decls.doc: `f.Frequently p` or `∃ᶠ x in f, p x` mean that `{x | ¬p x} ∉ f`. E.g., `∃ᶠ x in atTop, p x` means that there exist arbitrarily large `x` for which `p` holds true.

decls.name: Filter.EventuallyEq
decls.sig: def EventuallyEq (l : Filter α) (f g : α → β) : Prop
decls.doc: Two functions `f` and `g` are *eventually equal* along a filter `l` if the set of `x` such that `f x = g x` belongs to `l`.

decls.name: Filter.EventuallyLE
decls.sig: def EventuallyLE [LE β] (l : Filter α) (f g : α → β) : Prop
decls.doc: A function `f` is eventually less than or equal to a function `g` at a filter `l`.

decls.name: Filter.EventuallyEqSet
decls.sig: def EventuallyEqSet (l : Filter α) (s t : Set α) : Prop
decls.doc: Two sets `s` and `t` are *eventually equal* along a filter `l` if the set of `x` such that `x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t` belongs to `l`. This is definitionally `(· ∈ s) =ᶠ[l] (· ∈ t)`, but it is a separate definition (rather than an abbreviation) to avoid simp unfolding membership of concrete sets.

decls.name: Filter.EventuallySubset
decls.sig: def EventuallySubset (l : Filter α) (s t : Set α) : Prop
decls.doc: A set `s` is *eventually contained* in a set `t` along a filter `l` if the set of `x` such that `x ∈ s → x ∈ t` belongs to `l`. This is definitionally `(· ∈ s) ≤ᶠ[l] (· ∈ t)`, but it is a separate definition (rather than an abbreviation) to avoid simp unfolding membership of concrete sets.

decls.name: IsMinFilter
decls.sig: def IsMinFilter : Prop
decls.doc: `IsMinFilter f l a` means that `f a ≤ f x` for all `x` in some `l`-neighborhood of `a`

decls.name: IsMaxFilter
decls.sig: def IsMaxFilter : Prop
decls.doc: `is_maxFilter f l a` means that `f x ≤ f a` for all `x` in some `l`-neighborhood of `a`

decls.name: IsExtrFilter
decls.sig: def IsExtrFilter : Prop
decls.doc: `IsExtrFilter f l a` means `IsMinFilter f l a` or `IsMaxFilter f l a`

decls.name: IsMinOn
decls.sig: def IsMinOn
decls.doc: `IsMinOn f s a` means that `f a ≤ f x` for all `x ∈ s`. Note that we do not assume `a ∈ s`.

decls.name: IsMaxOn
decls.sig: def IsMaxOn
decls.doc: `IsMaxOn f s a` means that `f x ≤ f a` for all `x ∈ s`. Note that we do not assume `a ∈ s`.

decls.name: IsExtrOn

decls.doc: `IsExtrOn f s a` means `IsMinOn f s a` or `IsMaxOn f s a`

In all instances `Ixx` is one of `Set.Icc`, `Set.Ico`, `Set.Ioc`, or `Set.Ioo`. The instances provide the best `l₂` for a given `l₁`. In many cases `l₁ = l₂` but sometim

decls.sig: def map₂ (m : α → β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : Filter γ
decls.doc: The image of a binary function `m : α → β → γ` as a function `Filter α → Filter β → Filter γ`. Mathematically this should be thought of as the image of the corresponding function `α × β → γ`.

decls.name: Filter.mem_map₂_iff
decls.sig: theorem mem_map₂_iff : u ∈ map₂ m f g ↔ ∃ s ∈ f, ∃ t ∈ g, image2 m s t ⊆ u

decls.name: Filter.image2_mem_map₂
decls.sig: theorem image2_mem_map₂ (hs : s ∈ f) (ht : t ∈ g) : image2 m s t ∈ map₂ m f g

decls.name: Filter.map_prod_eq_map₂
decls.sig: theorem map_prod_eq_map₂ (m : α → β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : Filter.map (fun p : α × β => m p.1 p.2) (f ×ˢ g) = map₂ m f g

decls.name: Filter.map_prod_eq_map₂'
decls.sig: theorem map_prod_eq_map₂' (m : α × β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : Filter.map m (f ×ˢ g) = map₂ (fun a b => m (a, b)) f g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_mk_eq_prod
decls.sig: theorem map₂_mk_eq_prod (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : map₂ Prod.mk f g = f ×ˢ g

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.map₂
decls.sig: protected lemma HasBasis.map₂ {ι ι' : Type*} {p : ι → Prop} {q : ι' → Prop} {s t} (m : α → β → γ) (hf : f.HasBasis p s) (hg : g.HasBasis q t) : (map₂ m f g).HasBasis (fun i : ι × ι' ↦ p i.1 ∧ q i.2) fun i ↦ image2 m (s i.1) (t i.2)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_mono
decls.sig: theorem map₂_mono (hf : f₁ ≤ f₂) (hg : g₁ ≤ g₂) : map₂ m f₁ g₁ ≤ map₂ m f₂ g₂

decls.name: Filter.map₂_mono_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_mono_left (h : g₁ ≤ g₂) : map₂ m f g₁ ≤ map₂ m f g₂

decls.name: Filter.map₂_mono_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_mono_right (h : f₁ ≤ f₂) : map₂ m f₁ g ≤ map₂ m f₂ g

decls.name: Filter.le_map₂_iff
decls.sig: theorem le_map₂_iff {h : Filter γ} : h ≤ map₂ m f g ↔ ∀ ⦃s⦄, s ∈ f → ∀ ⦃t⦄, t ∈ g → image2 m s t ∈ h

decls.name: Filter.map₂_eq_bot_iff
decls.sig: theorem map₂_eq_bot_iff : map₂ m f g = ⊥ ↔ f = ⊥ ∨ g = ⊥

decls.name: Filter.map₂_bot_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_bot_left : map₂ m ⊥ g = ⊥

decls.name: Filter.map₂_bot_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_bot_right : map₂ m f ⊥ = ⊥

decls.name: Filter.map₂_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem map₂_neBot_iff : (map₂ m f g).NeBot ↔ f.NeBot ∧ g.NeBot

decls.name: Filter.NeBot.map₂
decls.sig: protected theorem NeBot.map₂ (hf : f.NeBot) (hg : g.NeBot) : (map₂ m f g).NeBot

decls.name: Filter.NeBot.of_map₂_left
decls.sig: theorem NeBot.of_map₂_left (h : (map₂ m f g).NeBot) : f.NeBot

decls.name: Filter.NeBot.of_map₂_right
decls.sig: theorem NeBot.of_map₂_right (h : (map₂ m f g).NeBot) : g.NeBot

decls.name: Filter.map₂_sup_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_sup_left : map₂ m (f₁ ⊔ f₂) g = map₂ m f₁ g ⊔ map₂ m f₂ g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_sup_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_sup_right : map₂ m f (g₁ ⊔ g₂) = map₂ m f g₁ ⊔ map₂ m f g₂

decls.name: Filter.map₂_inf_subset_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_inf_subset_left : map₂ m (f₁ ⊓ f₂) g ≤ map₂ m f₁ g ⊓ map₂ m f₂ g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_inf_subset_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_inf_subset_right : map₂ m f (g₁ ⊓ g₂) ≤ map₂ m f g₁ ⊓ map₂ m f g₂

decls.name: Filter.map₂_pure_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_pure_left : map₂ m (pure a) g = g.map (m a)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_pure_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_pure_right : map₂ m f (pure b) = f.map (m · b)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_pure
decls.sig: theorem map₂_pure : map₂ m (pure a) (pure b) = pure (m a b)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_swap
decls.sig: theorem map₂_swap (m : α → β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : map₂ m f g = map₂ (fun a b => m b a) g f

decls.name: Filter.map₂_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_left [NeBot g] : map₂ (fun x _ => x) f g = f

decls.name: Filter.map₂_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_right [NeBot f] : map₂ (fun _ y => y) f g = g

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂ (m : α → β → γ) (n : γ → δ) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ (fun a b => n (m a b)) f g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_map_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_map_left (m : γ → β → δ) (n : α → γ) : map₂ m (f.map n) g = map₂ (fun a b => m (n a) b) f g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_map_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_map_right (m : α → γ → δ) (n : β → γ) : map₂ m f (g.map n) = map₂ (fun a b => m a (n b)) f g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_curry
decls.sig: theorem map₂_curry (m : α × β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : map₂ m.curry f g = (f ×ˢ g).map m

decls.name: Filter.map_uncurry_prod
decls.sig: theorem map_uncurry_prod (m : α → β → γ) (f : Filter α) (g : Filter β) : (f ×ˢ g).map (uncurry m) = map₂ m f g

decls.name: Filter.map₂_assoc
decls.sig: theorem map₂_assoc {m : δ → γ → ε} {n : α → β → δ} {m' : α → ε' → ε} {n' : β → γ → ε'} {h : Filter γ} (h_assoc : ∀ a b c, m (n a b) c = m' a (n' b c)) : map₂ m (map₂ n f g) h = map₂ m' f (map₂ n' g h)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_comm
decls.sig: theorem map₂_comm {n : β → α → γ} (h_comm : ∀ a b, m a b = n b a) : map₂ m f g = map₂ n g f

decls.name: Filter.map₂_left_comm
decls.sig: theorem map₂_left_comm {m : α → δ → ε} {n : β → γ → δ} {m' : α → γ → δ'} {n' : β → δ' → ε} (h_left_comm : ∀ a b c, m a (n b c) = n' b (m' a c)) : map₂ m f (map₂ n g h) = map₂ n' g (map₂ m' f h)

decls.name: Filter.map₂_right_comm
decls.sig: theorem map₂_right_comm {m : δ → γ → ε} {n : α → β → δ} {m' : α → γ → δ'} {n' : δ' → β → ε} (h_right_comm : ∀ a b c, m (n a b) c = n' (m' a c) b) : map₂ m (map₂ n f g) h = map₂ n' (map₂ m' f h) g

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_distrib
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_distrib {n : γ → δ} {m' : α' → β' → δ} {n₁ : α → α'} {n₂ : β → β'} (h_distrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' (n₁ a) (n₂ b)) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' (f.map n₁) (g.map n₂)

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_distrib_left
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_distrib_left {n : γ → δ} {m' : α' → β → δ} {n' : α → α'} (h_distrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' (n' a) b) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' (f.map n') g
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map₂_map_left_comm`.

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_distrib_right
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_distrib_right {n : γ → δ} {m' : α → β' → δ} {n' : β → β'} (h_distrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' a (n' b)) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' f (g.map n')
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_right_comm`.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_map_left_comm
decls.sig: theorem map₂_map_left_comm {m : α' → β → γ} {n : α → α'} {m' : α → β → δ} {n' : δ → γ} (h_left_comm : ∀ a b, m (n a) b = n' (m' a b)) : map₂ m (f.map n) g = (map₂ m' f g).map n'
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_distrib_left`.

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_right_comm
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_right_comm {m : α → β' → γ} {n : β → β'} {m' : α → β → δ} {n' : δ → γ} (h_right_comm : ∀ a b, m a (n b) = n' (m' a b)) : map₂ m f (g.map n) = (map₂ m' f g).map n'
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_distrib_right`.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_distrib_le_left
decls.sig: theorem map₂_distrib_le_left {m : α → δ → ε} {n : β → γ → δ} {m₁ : α → β → β'} {m₂ : α → γ → γ'} {n' : β' → γ' → ε} (h_distrib : ∀ a b c, m a (n b c) = n' (m₁ a b) (m₂ a c)) : map₂ m f (map₂ n g h) ≤ map₂ n' (map₂ m₁ f g) (map₂ m₂ f h)
decls.doc: The other direction does not hold because of the `f-f` cross terms on the RHS.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_distrib_le_right
decls.sig: theorem map₂_distrib_le_right {m : δ → γ → ε} {n : α → β → δ} {m₁ : α → γ → α'} {m₂ : β → γ → β'} {n' : α' → β' → ε} (h_distrib : ∀ a b c, m (n a b) c = n' (m₁ a c) (m₂ b c)) : map₂ m (map₂ n f g) h ≤ map₂ n' (map₂ m₁ f h) (map₂ m₂ g h)
decls.doc: The other direction does not hold because of the `h`-`h` cross terms on the RHS.

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_antidistrib
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_antidistrib {n : γ → δ} {m' : β' → α' → δ} {n₁ : β → β'} {n₂ : α → α'} (h_antidistrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' (n₁ b) (n₂ a)) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' (g.map n₁) (f.map n₂)

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_antidistrib_left
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_antidistrib_left {n : γ → δ} {m' : β' → α → δ} {n' : β → β'} (h_antidistrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' (n' b) a) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' (g.map n') f
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map₂_map_left_anticomm`.

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_antidistrib_right
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_antidistrib_right {n : γ → δ} {m' : β → α' → δ} {n' : α → α'} (h_antidistrib : ∀ a b, n (m a b) = m' b (n' a)) : (map₂ m f g).map n = map₂ m' g (f.map n')
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_right_anticomm`.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_map_left_anticomm
decls.sig: theorem map₂_map_left_anticomm {m : α' → β → γ} {n : α → α'} {m' : β → α → δ} {n' : δ → γ} (h_left_anticomm : ∀ a b, m (n a) b = n' (m' b a)) : map₂ m (f.map n) g = (map₂ m' g f).map n'
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_antidistrib_left`.

decls.name: Filter.map_map₂_right_anticomm
decls.sig: theorem map_map₂_right_anticomm {m : α → β' → γ} {n : β → β'} {m' : β → α → δ} {n' : δ → γ} (h_right_anticomm : ∀ a b, m a (n b) = n' (m' b a)) : map₂ m f (g.map n) = (map₂ m' g f).map n'
decls.doc: Symmetric statement to `Filter.map_map₂_antidistrib_right`.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_left_identity
decls.sig: theorem map₂_left_identity {f : α → β → β} {a : α} (h : ∀ b, f a b = b) (l : Filter β) : map₂ f (pure a) l = l
decls.doc: If `a` is a left identity for `f : α → β → β`, then `pure a` is a left identity for `Filter.map₂ f`.

decls.name: Filter.map₂_right_identity
decls.sig: theorem map₂_right_identity {f : α → β → α} {b : β} (h : ∀ a, f a b = a) (l : Filter α) : map₂ f l (pure b) = l
decls.doc: If `b` is a right identity for `f : α → β → α`, then `pure b` is a right identity for `Filter.map₂ f`.

decls.name: Filter.rmap
decls.sig: def rmap (r : SetRel α β) (l : Filter α) : Filter β where
decls.doc: The forward map of a filter under a relation. Generalization of `Filter.map` to relations. Note that `Rel.core` generalizes `Set.preimage`.

decls.name: Filter.rmap_sets
decls.sig: theorem rmap_sets (r : SetRel α β) (l : Filter α) : (l.rmap r).sets = r.core ⁻¹' l.sets

decls.name: Filter.mem_rmap
decls.sig: theorem mem_rmap (r : SetRel α β) (l : Filter α) (s : Set β) : s ∈ l.rmap r ↔ r.core s ∈ l

decls.name: Filter.rmap_rmap
decls.sig: theorem rmap_rmap (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) (l : Filter α) : rmap s (rmap r l) = rmap (r.comp s) l

decls.name: Filter.rmap_compose
decls.sig: theorem rmap_compose (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) : rmap s ∘ rmap r = rmap (r.comp s)

decls.name: Filter.RTendsto
decls.sig: def RTendsto (r : SetRel α β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β)
decls.doc: Generic "limit of a relation" predicate. `RTendsto r l₁ l₂` asserts that for every `l₂`-neighborhood `a`, the `r`-core of `a` is an `l₁`-neighborhood. One generalization of `Filter.Tendsto` to relations.

decls.name: Filter.rtendsto_def
decls.sig: theorem rtendsto_def (r : SetRel α β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) : RTendsto r l₁ l₂ ↔ ∀ s ∈ l₂, r.core s ∈ l₁

decls.name: Filter.rcomap
decls.sig: def rcomap (r : SetRel α β) (f : Filter β) : Filter α where
decls.doc: One way of taking the inverse map of a filter under a relation. One generalization of `Filter.comap` to relations. Note that `Rel.core` generalizes `Set.preimage`.

decls.name: Filter.rcomap_sets
decls.sig: theorem rcomap_sets (r : SetRel α β) (f : Filter β) : (rcomap r f).sets = SetRel.image {(s, t) : _ × _ | r.core s ⊆ t} f.sets

decls.name: Filter.rcomap_rcomap
decls.sig: theorem rcomap_rcomap (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) (l : Filter γ) : rcomap r (rcomap s l) = rcomap (r.comp s) l

decls.name: Filter.rcomap_compose
decls.sig: theorem rcomap_compose (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) : rcomap r ∘ rcomap s = rcomap (r.comp s)

decls.name: Filter.rtendsto_iff_le_rcomap
decls.sig: theorem rtendsto_iff_le_rcomap (r : SetRel α β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) : RTendsto r l₁ l₂ ↔ l₁ ≤ l₂.rcomap r

decls.name: Filter.rcomap'
decls.sig: def rcomap' (r : SetRel α β) (f : Filter β) : Filter α where
decls.doc: One way of taking the inverse map of a filter under a relation. Generalization of `Filter.comap` to relations.

decls.name: Filter.mem_rcomap'
decls.sig: theorem mem_rcomap' (r : SetRel α β) (l : Filter β) (s : Set α) : s ∈ l.rcomap' r ↔ ∃ t ∈ l, r.preimage t ⊆ s

decls.name: Filter.rcomap'_sets
decls.sig: theorem rcomap'_sets (r : SetRel α β) (f : Filter β) : (rcomap' r f).sets = SetRel.image {(s, t) | r.preimage s ⊆ t} f.sets

decls.name: Filter.rcomap'_rcomap'
decls.sig: theorem rcomap'_rcomap' (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) (l : Filter γ) : rcomap' r (rcomap' s l) = rcomap' (r.comp s) l

decls.name: Filter.rcomap'_compose
decls.sig: theorem rcomap'_compose (r : SetRel α β) (s : SetRel β γ) : rcomap' r ∘ rcomap' s = rcomap' (r.comp s)

decls.name: Filter.RTendsto'
decls.sig: def RTendsto' (r : SetRel α β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β)
decls.doc: Generic "limit of a relation" predicate. `RTendsto' r l₁ l₂` asserts that for every `l₂`-neighborhood `a`, the `r`-preimage of `a` is an `l₁`-neighborhood. One generalization of `Filter.Tendsto` to relations.

decls.name: Filter.rtendsto'_def
decls.sig: theorem rtendsto'_def (r : SetRel α β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) : RTendsto' r l₁ l₂ ↔ ∀ s ∈ l₂, r.preimage s ∈ l₁

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_iff_rtendsto
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_iff_rtendsto (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) (f : α → β) : Tendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ RTendsto (Function.graph f) l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_iff_rtendsto'
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_iff_rtendsto' (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) (f : α → β) : Tendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ RTendsto' (Function.graph f) l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.pmap
decls.sig: def pmap (f : α →. β) (l : Filter α) : Filter β
decls.doc: The forward map of a filter under a partial function. Generalization of `Filter.map` to partial functions.

decls.name: Filter.mem_pmap
decls.sig: theorem mem_pmap (f : α →. β) (l : Filter α) (s : Set β) : s ∈ l.pmap f ↔ f.core s ∈ l

decls.name: Filter.PTendsto
decls.sig: def PTendsto (f : α →. β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β)
decls.doc: Generic "limit of a partial function" predicate. `PTendsto r l₁ l₂` asserts that for every `l₂`-neighborhood `a`, the `p`-core of `a` is an `l₁`-neighborhood. One generalization of `Filter.Tendsto` to partial function.

decls.name: Filter.ptendsto_def
decls.sig: theorem ptendsto_def (f : α →. β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) : PTendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ ∀ s ∈ l₂, f.core s ∈ l₁

decls.name: Filter.ptendsto_iff_rtendsto
decls.sig: theorem ptendsto_iff_rtendsto (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) (f : α →. β) : PTendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ RTendsto f.graph' l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.pmap_res
decls.sig: theorem pmap_res (l : Filter α) (s : Set α) (f : α → β) : pmap (PFun.res f s) l = map f (l ⊓ 𝓟 s)

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_iff_ptendsto
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_iff_ptendsto (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) (s : Set α) (f : α → β) : Tendsto f (l₁ ⊓ 𝓟 s) l₂ ↔ PTendsto (PFun.res f s) l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_iff_ptendsto_univ
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_iff_ptendsto_univ (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) (f : α → β) : Tendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ PTendsto (PFun.res f Set.univ) l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.pcomap'
decls.sig: def pcomap' (f : α →. β) (l : Filter β) : Filter α
decls.doc: Inverse map of a filter under a partial function. One generalization of `Filter.comap` to partial functions.

decls.name: Filter.PTendsto'
decls.sig: def PTendsto' (f : α →. β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β)
decls.doc: Generic "limit of a partial function" predicate. `PTendsto' r l₁ l₂` asserts that for every `l₂`-neighborhood `a`, the `p`-preimage of `a` is an `l₁`-neighborhood. One generalization of `Filter.Tendsto` to partial functions.

decls.name: Filter.ptendsto'_def
decls.sig: theorem ptendsto'_def (f : α →. β) (l₁ : Filter α) (l₂ : Filter β) : PTendsto' f l₁ l₂ ↔ ∀ s ∈ l₂, f.preimage s ∈ l₁

decls.name: Filter.ptendsto_of_ptendsto'
decls.sig: theorem ptendsto_of_ptendsto' {f : α →. β} {l₁ : Filter α} {l₂ : Filter β} : PTendsto' f l₁ l₂ → PTendsto f l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.ptendsto'_of_ptendsto
decls.sig: theorem ptendsto'_of_ptendsto {f : α →. β} {l₁ : Filter α} {l₂ : Filter β} (h : f.Dom ∈ l₁) : PTendsto f l₁ l₂ → PTendsto' f l₁ l₂

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_eval_pi
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_eval_pi (f : ∀ i, Filter (α i)) (i : ι) : Tendsto (eval i) (pi f) (f i)

decls.name: Filter.tendsto_pi
decls.sig: theorem tendsto_pi {β : Type*} {m : β → ∀ i, α i} {l : Filter β} : Tendsto m l (pi f) ↔ ∀ i, Tendsto (fun x => m x i) l (f i)

decls.name: Filter.le_pi
decls.sig: theorem le_pi {g : Filter (∀ i, α i)} : g ≤ pi f ↔ ∀ i, Tendsto (eval i) g (f i)

decls.name: Filter.pi_mono
decls.sig: theorem pi_mono (h : ∀ i, f₁ i ≤ f₂ i) : pi f₁ ≤ pi f₂

decls.name: Filter.mem_pi_of_mem
decls.sig: theorem mem_pi_of_mem (i : ι) {s : Set (α i)} (hs : s ∈ f i) : eval i ⁻¹' s ∈ pi f

decls.name: Filter.pi_mem_pi
decls.sig: theorem pi_mem_pi {I : Set ι} (hI : I.Finite) (h : ∀ i ∈ I, s i ∈ f i) : I.pi s ∈ pi f

decls.name: Filter.mem_pi
decls.sig: theorem mem_pi {s : Set (∀ i, α i)} : s ∈ pi f ↔ ∃ I : Set ι, I.Finite ∧ ∃ t : ∀ i, Set (α i), (∀ i, t i ∈ f i) ∧ I.pi t ⊆ s

decls.name: Filter.mem_pi'

decls.sig: theorem hasBasis_iSup {ι : Sort*} {ι' : ι → Type*} {l : ι → Filter α} {p : ∀ i, ι' i → Prop} {s : ∀ i, ι' i → Set α} (hl : ∀ i, (l i).HasBasis (p i) (s i)) : (⨆ i, l i).HasBasis (fun f : ∀ i, ι' i => ∀ i, p i (f i)) fun f : ∀ i, ι' i => ⋃ i, s i (f i)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.sup_principal
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.sup_principal (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (t : Set α) : (l ⊔ 𝓟 t).HasBasis p fun i => s i ∪ t

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.sup_pure
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.sup_pure (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (x : α) : (l ⊔ pure x).HasBasis p fun i => s i ∪ {x}

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.inf_principal
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.inf_principal (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (s' : Set α) : (l ⊓ 𝓟 s').HasBasis p fun i => s i ∩ s'

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.principal_inf
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.principal_inf (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (s' : Set α) : (𝓟 s' ⊓ l).HasBasis p fun i => s' ∩ s i

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.inf_basis_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.inf_basis_neBot_iff (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (hl' : l'.HasBasis p' s') : NeBot (l ⊓ l') ↔ ∀ ⦃i⦄, p i → ∀ ⦃i'⦄, p' i' → (s i ∩ s' i').Nonempty

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.inf_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.inf_neBot_iff (hl : l.HasBasis p s) : NeBot (l ⊓ l') ↔ ∀ ⦃i⦄, p i → ∀ ⦃s'⦄, s' ∈ l' → (s i ∩ s').Nonempty

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.inf_principal_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.inf_principal_neBot_iff (hl : l.HasBasis p s) {t : Set α} : NeBot (l ⊓ 𝓟 t) ↔ ∀ ⦃i⦄, p i → (s i ∩ t).Nonempty

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.disjoint_iff
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.disjoint_iff (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (hl' : l'.HasBasis p' s') : Disjoint l l' ↔ ∃ i, p i ∧ ∃ i', p' i' ∧ Disjoint (s i) (s' i')

decls.name: Disjoint.exists_mem_filter_basis
decls.sig: theorem _root_.Disjoint.exists_mem_filter_basis (h : Disjoint l l') (hl : l.HasBasis p s) (hl' : l'.HasBasis p' s') : ∃ i, p i ∧ ∃ i', p' i' ∧ Disjoint (s i) (s' i')

decls.name: Filter.inf_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem inf_neBot_iff : NeBot (l ⊓ l') ↔ ∀ ⦃s : Set α⦄, s ∈ l → ∀ ⦃s'⦄, s' ∈ l' → (s ∩ s').Nonempty

decls.name: Filter.inf_principal_neBot_iff
decls.sig: theorem inf_principal_neBot_iff {s : Set α} : NeBot (l ⊓ 𝓟 s) ↔ ∀ U ∈ l, (U ∩ s).Nonempty

decls.name: Filter.mem_iff_inf_principal_compl
decls.sig: theorem mem_iff_inf_principal_compl {f : Filter α} {s : Set α} : s ∈ f ↔ f ⊓ 𝓟 sᶜ = ⊥

decls.name: Filter.notMem_iff_inf_principal_compl
decls.sig: theorem notMem_iff_inf_principal_compl {f : Filter α} {s : Set α} : s ∉ f ↔ NeBot (f ⊓ 𝓟 sᶜ)

decls.name: Filter.disjoint_principal_right
decls.sig: theorem disjoint_principal_right {f : Filter α} {s : Set α} : Disjoint f (𝓟 s) ↔ sᶜ ∈ f

decls.name: Filter.disjoint_principal_left
decls.sig: theorem disjoint_principal_left {f : Filter α} {s : Set α} : Disjoint (𝓟 s) f ↔ sᶜ ∈ f

decls.name: Filter.disjoint_principal_principal
decls.sig: theorem disjoint_principal_principal {s t : Set α} : Disjoint (𝓟 s) (𝓟 t) ↔ Disjoint s t

decls.name: Filter.disjoint_pure_pure
decls.sig: theorem disjoint_pure_pure {x y : α} : Disjoint (pure x : Filter α) (pure y) ↔ x ≠ y

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.disjoint_iff_left
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.disjoint_iff_left (h : l.HasBasis p s) : Disjoint l l' ↔ ∃ i, p i ∧ (s i)ᶜ ∈ l'

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.disjoint_iff_right
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.disjoint_iff_right (h : l.HasBasis p s) : Disjoint l' l ↔ ∃ i, p i ∧ (s i)ᶜ ∈ l'

decls.name: Filter.le_iff_forall_inf_principal_compl
decls.sig: theorem le_iff_forall_inf_principal_compl {f g : Filter α} : f ≤ g ↔ ∀ V ∈ g, f ⊓ 𝓟 Vᶜ = ⊥

decls.name: Filter.inf_neBot_iff_frequently_left
decls.sig: theorem inf_neBot_iff_frequently_left {f g : Filter α} : NeBot (f ⊓ g) ↔ ∀ {p : α → Prop}, (∀ᶠ x in f, p x) → ∃ᶠ x in g, p x

decls.name: Filter.inf_neBot_iff_frequently_right
decls.sig: theorem inf_neBot_iff_frequently_right {f g : Filter α} : NeBot (f ⊓ g) ↔ ∀ {p : α → Prop}, (∀ᶠ x in g, p x) → ∃ᶠ x in f, p x

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.eq_biInf
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.eq_biInf (h : l.HasBasis p s) : l = ⨅ (i) (_ : p i), 𝓟 (s i)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.eq_iInf
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.eq_iInf (h : l.HasBasis (fun _ => True) s) : l = ⨅ i, 𝓟 (s i)

decls.name: Filter.hasBasis_iInf_principal
decls.sig: theorem hasBasis_iInf_principal {s : ι → Set α} (h : Directed (· ≥ ·) s) [Nonempty ι] : (⨅ i, 𝓟 (s i)).HasBasis (fun _ => True) s

decls.name: Filter.hasBasis_biInf_principal
decls.sig: theorem hasBasis_biInf_principal {s : β → Set α} {S : Set β} (h : DirectedOn (s ⁻¹'o (· ≥ ·)) S) (ne : S.Nonempty) : (⨅ i ∈ S, 𝓟 (s i)).HasBasis (fun i => i ∈ S) s

decls.name: Filter.hasBasis_biInf_principal'
decls.sig: theorem hasBasis_biInf_principal' {ι : Type*} {p : ι → Prop} {s : ι → Set α} (h : ∀ i, p i → ∀ j, p j → ∃ k, p k ∧ s k ⊆ s i ∧ s k ⊆ s j) (ne : ∃ i, p i) : (⨅ (i) (_ : p i), 𝓟 (s i)).HasBasis p s

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.map
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.map (f : α → β) (hl : l.HasBasis p s) : (l.map f).HasBasis p fun i => f '' s i

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.comap
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.comap (f : β → α) (hl : l.HasBasis p s) : (l.comap f).HasBasis p fun i => f ⁻¹' s i

decls.name: Filter.comap_hasBasis
decls.sig: theorem comap_hasBasis (f : α → β) (l : Filter β) : HasBasis (comap f l) (fun s : Set β => s ∈ l) fun s => f ⁻¹' s

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.forall_mem_mem
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.forall_mem_mem (h : HasBasis l p s) {x : α} : (∀ t ∈ l, x ∈ t) ↔ ∀ i, p i → x ∈ s i

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.biInf_mem
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.biInf_mem [CompleteLattice β] {f : Set α → β} (h : HasBasis l p s) (hf : Monotone f) : ⨅ t ∈ l, f t = ⨅ (i) (_ : p i), f (s i)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.biInter_mem
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.biInter_mem {f : Set α → Set β} (h : HasBasis l p s) (hf : Monotone f) : ⋂ t ∈ l, f t = ⋂ (i) (_ : p i), f (s i)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.ker
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.ker (h : HasBasis l p s) : l.ker = ⋂ (i) (_ : p i), s i

decls.name: Filter.IsAntitoneBasis
decls.sig: structure IsAntitoneBasis : Prop extends IsBasis (fun _ => True) s'' where
decls.doc: `IsAntitoneBasis s` means the image of `s` is a filter basis such that `s` is decreasing.

decls.name: Filter.HasAntitoneBasis
decls.sig: structure HasAntitoneBasis (l : Filter α) (s : ι'' → Set α) : Prop extends HasBasis l (fun _ => True) s where
decls.doc: We say that a filter `l` has an antitone basis `s : ι → Set α`, if `t ∈ l` if and only if `t` includes `s i` for some `i`, and `s` is decreasing.

decls.name: Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.map
decls.sig: protected theorem HasAntitoneBasis.map {l : Filter α} {s : ι'' → Set α} (hf : HasAntitoneBasis l s) (m : α → β) : HasAntitoneBasis (map m l) (m '' s ·)

decls.name: Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.comap
decls.sig: protected theorem HasAntitoneBasis.comap {l : Filter α} {s : ι'' → Set α} (hf : HasAntitoneBasis l s) (m : β → α) : HasAntitoneBasis (comap m l) (m ⁻¹' s ·)

decls.name: Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.iInf_principal
decls.sig: lemma HasAntitoneBasis.iInf_principal {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] {s : ι → Set α} (hs : Antitone s) : (⨅ i, 𝓟 (s i)).HasAntitoneBasis s

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.tendsto_left_iff

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.tendsto_right_iff

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.tendsto_iff
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.tendsto_iff (hla : la.HasBasis pa sa) (hlb : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : Tendsto f la lb ↔ ∀ ib, pb ib → ∃ ia, pa ia ∧ ∀ x ∈ sa ia, f x ∈ sb ib

decls.name: Filter.Tendsto.basis_left
decls.sig: theorem Tendsto.basis_left (H : Tendsto f la lb) (hla : la.HasBasis pa sa) : ∀ t ∈ lb, ∃ i, pa i ∧ MapsTo f (sa i) t

decls.name: Filter.Tendsto.basis_right
decls.sig: theorem Tendsto.basis_right (H : Tendsto f la lb) (hlb : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : ∀ i, pb i → ∀ᶠ x in la, f x ∈ sb i

decls.name: Filter.Tendsto.basis_both
decls.sig: theorem Tendsto.basis_both (H : Tendsto f la lb) (hla : la.HasBasis pa sa) (hlb : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : ∀ ib, pb ib → ∃ ia, pa ia ∧ MapsTo f (sa ia) (sb ib)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod_pprod

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.prod {ι ι' : Type*} {pa : ι → Prop} {sa : ι → Set α} {pb : ι' → Prop} {sb : ι' → Set β} (hla : la.HasBasis pa sa) (hlb : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : (la ×ˢ lb).HasBasis (fun i : ι × ι' => pa i.1 ∧ pb i.2) fun i => sa i.1 ×ˢ sb i.2

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.principal_prod
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.principal_prod (sa : Set α) (h : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : (𝓟 sa ×ˢ lb).HasBasis pb (sa ×ˢ sb ·)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod_principal
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.prod_principal (h : la.HasBasis pa sa) (sb : Set β) : (la ×ˢ 𝓟 sb).HasBasis pa (sa · ×ˢ sb)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.top_prod
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.top_prod (h : lb.HasBasis pb sb) : (⊤ ×ˢ lb : Filter (α × β)).HasBasis pb (univ ×ˢ sb ·)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod_top
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.prod_top (h : la.HasBasis pa sa) : (la ×ˢ ⊤ : Filter (α × β)).HasBasis pa (sa · ×ˢ univ)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod_same_index

decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.prod_same_index_anti {ι : Type*} [LinearOrder ι] {p : ι → Prop} {sa : ι → Set α} {sb : ι → Set β} (hla : la.HasBasis p sa) (hlb : lb.HasBasis p sb) (hsa : AntitoneOn sa { i | p i }) (hsb : AntitoneOn sb { i | p i }) : (la ×ˢ lb).HasBasis p fun i => sa i ×ˢ sb i

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.prod_self
decls.sig: theorem HasBasis.prod_self (hl : la.HasBasis pa sa) : (la ×ˢ la).HasBasis pa fun i => sa i ×ˢ sa i

decls.name: Filter.eventually_prod_self_iff'

decls.doc: A version of `eventually_prod_self_iff` that is more suitable for forward rewriting.

decls.name: Filter.HasAntitoneBasis.prod
decls.sig: theorem HasAntitoneBasis.prod {ι : Type*} [LinearOrder ι] {f : Filter α} {g : Filter β} {s : ι → Set α} {t : ι → Set β} (hf : HasAntitoneBasis f s) (hg : HasAntitoneBasis g t) : HasAntitoneBasis (f ×ˢ g) fun n => s n ×ˢ t n

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.and_isClosed

decls.doc: A filter `l` which has a basis of sets contained in the filter which satisfy some predicate `p` that is preserved under a `ClosureOperator` `c` has a basis which consists of sets contained in `l` which satisfy predicate `p` and are _closed_ under `c`.

decls.name: Filter.map_sigma_mk_comap

decls.name: Filter.ofSets_filter_eq_generate
decls.sig: theorem ofSets_filter_eq_generate (s : Set (Set α)) : (FilterBasis.ofSets s).filter = generate s

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.iInf
decls.sig: protected theorem HasBasis.iInf {ι : Type*} {ι' : ι → Type*} {l : ι → Filter α} {p : ∀ i, ι' i → Prop} {s : ∀ i, ι' i → Set α} (hl : ∀ i, (l i).HasBasis (p i) (s i)) : (⨅ i, l i).HasBasis (fun If : Σ I : Set ι, ∀ i : I, ι' i => If.1.Finite ∧ ∀ i : If.1, p i (If.2 i)) fun If => ⋂ i : If.1, s i (If.2 i)

decls.name: Filter.HasBasis.biInf_finset

decls.name: Set.PairwiseDisjoint.exists_mem_filter_basis
decls.sig: theorem _root_.Set.PairwiseDisjoint.exists_mem_filter_basis {I : Type*} {l : I → Filter α} {ι : I → Sort*} {p : ∀ i, ι i → Prop} {s : ∀ i, ι i → Set α} {S : Set I} (hd : S.PairwiseDisjoint l) (hS : S.Finite) (h : ∀ i, (l i).HasBasis (p i) (s i)) : ∃ ind : ∀ i, ι i, (∀ i, p i (ind i)) ∧ S.PairwiseDisjoint fun i => s i (ind i)

decls.name: Filter.hasBasis_iInf_principal_finite
decls.sig: theorem hasBasis_iInf_principal_finite {ι : Type*} (s : ι → Set α) : (⨅ i, 𝓟 (s i)).HasBasis (fun t : Set ι => t.Finite) fun t => ⋂ i ∈ t, s i

decls.name: Matrix.cramerMap_is_linear
decls.sig: theorem cramerMap_is_linear (i : n) : IsLinearMap α fun b => cramerMap A b i

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_is_linear
decls.sig: theorem cramer_is_linear : IsLinearMap α (cramerMap A)

decls.name: Matrix.cramer
decls.sig: def cramer (A : Matrix n n α) : (n → α) →ₗ[α] (n → α)
decls.doc: `cramer A b i` is the determinant of the matrix `A` with column `i` replaced with `b`, and thus `cramer A b` is the vector output by Cramer's rule on `A` and `b`. If `A * x = b` has a unique solution in `x`, `cramer A` sends the vector `b` to `A.det • x`. Otherwise, the outcome of `cramer` is well-d

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_apply
decls.sig: theorem cramer_apply (i : n) : cramer A b i = (A.updateCol i b).det

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_transpose_apply
decls.sig: theorem cramer_transpose_apply (i : n) : cramer Aᵀ b i = (A.updateRow i b).det

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_transpose_row_self
decls.sig: theorem cramer_transpose_row_self (i : n) : Aᵀ.cramer (A i) = Pi.single i A.det

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_row_self
decls.sig: theorem cramer_row_self (i : n) (h : ∀ j, b j = A j i) : A.cramer b = Pi.single i A.det

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_one
decls.sig: theorem cramer_one : cramer (1 : Matrix n n α) = 1

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_smul
decls.sig: theorem cramer_smul (r : α) (A : Matrix n n α) : cramer (r • A) = r ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • cramer A

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_subsingleton_apply
decls.sig: theorem cramer_subsingleton_apply [Subsingleton n] (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) (i : n) : cramer A b i = b i

decls.doc: Use linearity of `cramer` to take it out of a summation.

decls.doc: Use linearity of `cramer` and vector evaluation to take `cramer A _ i` out of a summation.

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_submatrix_equiv
decls.sig: theorem cramer_submatrix_equiv (A : Matrix m m α) (e : n ≃ m) (b : n → α) : cramer (A.submatrix e e) b = cramer A (b ∘ e.symm) ∘ e

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_reindex
decls.sig: theorem cramer_reindex (e : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m α) (b : n → α) : cramer (reindex e e A) b = cramer A (b ∘ e) ∘ e.symm

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate
decls.sig: def adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : Matrix n n α
decls.doc: The adjugate matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix. Typically, the cofactor matrix is defined by taking minors, i.e. the determinant of the matrix with a row and column removed. However, the proof of `mul_adjugate` becomes a lot easier if we use the matrix replacing a column with a basis ve

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_def
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_def (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate A = of fun i => cramer Aᵀ (Pi.single i 1)

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_apply
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_apply (A : Matrix n n α) (i j : n) : adjugate A i j = (A.updateRow j (Pi.single i 1)).det

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_transpose
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_transpose (A : Matrix n n α) : (adjugate A)ᵀ = adjugate Aᵀ

decls.name: Matrix.IsSymm.adjugate
decls.sig: theorem IsSymm.adjugate {A : Matrix n n α} (hA : A.IsSymm) : A.adjugate.IsSymm

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_submatrix_equiv_self
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_submatrix_equiv_self (e : n ≃ m) (A : Matrix m m α) : adjugate (A.submatrix e e) = (adjugate A).submatrix e e

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_reindex
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_reindex (e : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m α) : adjugate (reindex e e A) = reindex e e (adjugate A)

decls.name: Matrix.cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec
decls.sig: theorem cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) : cramer A b = A.adjugate *ᵥ b
decls.doc: Since the map `b ↦ cramer A b` is linear in `b`, it must be multiplication by some matrix. This matrix is `A.adjugate`.

decls.name: Matrix.mul_adjugate_apply
decls.sig: theorem mul_adjugate_apply (A : Matrix n n α) (i j k) : A i k * adjugate A k j = cramer Aᵀ (Pi.single k (A i k)) j

decls.name: Matrix.mul_adjugate
decls.sig: theorem mul_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : A * adjugate A = A.det • (1 : Matrix n n α)

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_mul
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_mul (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate A * A = A.det • (1 : Matrix n n α)

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_smul
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_smul (r : α) (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate (r • A) = r ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • adjugate A

decls.name: Matrix.mulVec_cramer
decls.sig: theorem mulVec_cramer (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) : A *ᵥ cramer A b = A.det • b
decls.doc: A stronger form of **Cramer's rule** that allows us to solve some instances of `A * x = b` even if the determinant is not a unit. A sufficient (but still not necessary) condition is that `A.det` divides `b`.

decls.sig: theorem adjugate_eq_one_of_card_eq_one {A : Matrix n n α} (h : Fintype.card n = 1) : adjugate A = 1

decls.sig: theorem adjugate_zero [Nontrivial n] : adjugate (0 : Matrix n n α) = 0

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_one
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_one : adjugate (1 : Matrix n n α) = 1

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_diagonal
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_diagonal (v : n → α) : adjugate (diagonal v) = diagonal fun i => ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, v j

decls.name: Matrix.det_adjugate
decls.sig: theorem det_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : (adjugate A).det = A.det ^ (Fintype.card n - 1)

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_zero
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_zero (A : Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) α) : adjugate A = 0

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_one
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_one (A : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) α) : adjugate A = 1

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_succ_eq_det_submatrix
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_succ_eq_det_submatrix {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) α) (i j) : adjugate A i j = (-1) ^ (j + i : ℕ) * det (A.submatrix j.succAbove i.succAbove)

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_two
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_two (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) α) : adjugate A = !![A 1 1, -A 0 1; -A 1 0, A 0 0]

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_two_of
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_two_of (a b c d : α) : adjugate !![a, b; c, d] = !![d, -b; -c, a]

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_three
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_three (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) α) : adjugate A = !![A 1 1 * A 2 2 - A 1 2 * A 2 1, -(A 0 1 * A 2 2) + A 0 2 * A 2 1, A 0 1 * A 1 2 - A 0 2 * A 1 1; -(A 1 0 * A 2 2) + A 1 2 * A 2 0, A 0 0 * A 2 2 - A 0 2 * A 2 0, -(A 0 0 * A 1 2) + A 0 2 * A 1 0;

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_fin_three_of
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_fin_three_of (a b c d e f g h i : α) : adjugate !![a, b, c; d, e, f; g, h, i] = !![  e * i  - f * h, -(b * i) + c * h,   b * f  - c * e; -(d * i) + f * g,   a * i  - c * g, -(a * f) + c * d; d * h  - e * g, -(a * h) + b * g,   a * e  - b * d]

decls.name: Matrix.det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_row
decls.sig: theorem det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_row (A : Matrix n n α) (i : n) : det A = ∑ j : n, A i j * adjugate A j i

decls.name: Matrix.det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_col
decls.sig: theorem det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_col (A : Matrix n n α) (j : n) : det A = ∑ i : n, A i j * adjugate A j i

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_conjTranspose

decls.name: Matrix.isRegular_of_isLeftRegular_det

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_mul_distrib_aux

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_mul_distrib
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_mul_distrib (A B : Matrix n n α) : adjugate (A * B) = adjugate B * adjugate A
decls.doc: Proof follows from "The trace Cayley-Hamilton theorem" by Darij Grinberg, Section 5.3

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_pow
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_pow (A : Matrix n n α) (k : ℕ) : adjugate (A ^ k) = adjugate A ^ k

decls.name: Matrix.det_smul_adjugate_adjugate
decls.sig: theorem det_smul_adjugate_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : det A • adjugate (adjugate A) = det A ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • A

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_adjugate
decls.sig: theorem adjugate_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) (h : Fintype.card n ≠ 1) : adjugate (adjugate A) = det A ^ (Fintype.card n - 2) • A
decls.doc: Note that this is not true for `Fintype.card n = 1` since `1 - 2 = 0` and not `-1`.

decls.name: Matrix.adjugate_adjugate'

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix
decls.sig: def toMatrix (e : Basis ι R M) (v : ι' → M) : Matrix ι ι' R
decls.doc: From a basis `e : ι → M` and a family of vectors `v : ι' → M`, make the matrix whose columns are the vectors `v i` written in the basis `e`.

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_apply : e.toMatrix v i j = e.repr (v j) i

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_transpose_apply
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_transpose_apply : (e.toMatrix v)ᵀ j = e.repr (v j)

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_eq_toMatrix_constr
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_eq_toMatrix_constr [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (v : ι → M) : e.toMatrix v = LinearMap.toMatrix e e (e.constr ℕ v)

decls.name: Module.Basis.coePiBasisFun.toMatrix_eq_transpose
decls.sig: theorem coePiBasisFun.toMatrix_eq_transpose [Finite ι] : ((Pi.basisFun R ι).toMatrix : Matrix ι ι R → Matrix ι ι R) = Matrix.transpose

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_self
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_self [DecidableEq ι] : e.toMatrix e = 1

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_update
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_update [DecidableEq ι'] (x : M) : e.toMatrix (Function.update v j x) = Matrix.updateCol (e.toMatrix v) j (e.repr x)

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_unitsSMul
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_unitsSMul [DecidableEq ι] (e : Basis ι R₂ M₂) (w : ι → R₂ˣ) : e.toMatrix (e.unitsSMul w) = diagonal ((↑) ∘ w)
decls.doc: The basis constructed by `unitsSMul` has vectors given by a diagonal matrix.

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_isUnitSMul
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_isUnitSMul [DecidableEq ι] (e : Basis ι R₂ M₂) {w : ι → R₂} (hw : ∀ i, IsUnit (w i)) : e.toMatrix (e.isUnitSMul hw) = diagonal w
decls.doc: The basis constructed by `isUnitSMul` has vectors given by a diagonal matrix.

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_smul_left
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_smul_left {G} [Group G] [DistribMulAction G M] [SMulCommClass G R M] (g : G) : (g • e).toMatrix v = e.toMatrix (g⁻¹ • v)

decls.name: Module.Basis.sum_toMatrix_smul_self

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_smul
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_smul {R₁ S : Type*} [CommSemiring R₁] [Semiring S] [Algebra R₁ S] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (x : S) (b : Basis ι R₁ S) (w : ι → S) : (b.toMatrix (x • w)) = (Algebra.leftMulMatrix b x) * (b.toMatrix w)

decls.name: Module.Basis.toMatrix_map_vecMul
decls.sig: theorem toMatrix_map_vecMul {S : Type*} [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R S) (v : ι' → S) : b ᵥ* ((b.toMatrix v).map <| algebraMap R S) = v

decls.name: Module.Basis.toLin_toMatrix
decls.sig: theorem toLin_toMatrix [Finite ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (v : Basis ι' R M) : Matrix.toLin v e (e.toMatrix v) = LinearMap.id

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular
decls.sig: def BlockTriangular (M : Matrix m m R) (b : m → α) : Prop
decls.doc: Let `b` map rows and columns of a square matrix `M` to blocks indexed by `α`s. Then `BlockTriangular M n b` says the matrix is block triangular.

decls.name: Matrix.IsUpperTriangular
decls.sig: abbrev IsUpperTriangular [LT m] (M : Matrix m m R) : Prop
decls.doc: `M` is upper triangular: entries below the diagonal vanish.

decls.name: Matrix.IsLowerTriangular
decls.sig: abbrev IsLowerTriangular [LT m] (M : Matrix m m R) : Prop
decls.doc: `M` is lower triangular: entries above the diagonal vanish.

decls.name: Matrix.IsIndecomposable
decls.sig: def IsIndecomposable (M : Matrix m m R) : Prop
decls.doc: A matrix is indecomposable if it cannot be reindexed to block-triangular form.

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.submatrix
decls.sig: protected theorem BlockTriangular.submatrix {f : n → m} (h : M.BlockTriangular b) : (M.submatrix f f).BlockTriangular (b ∘ f)

decls.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_reindex_iff
decls.sig: theorem blockTriangular_reindex_iff {b : n → α} {e : m ≃ n} : (reindex e e M).BlockTriangular b ↔ M.BlockTriangular (b ∘ e)

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.transpose
decls.sig: protected theorem BlockTriangular.transpose : M.BlockTriangular b → Mᵀ.BlockTriangular (toDual ∘ b)

decls.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_transpose_iff
decls.sig: protected theorem blockTriangular_transpose_iff {b : m → αᵒᵈ} : Mᵀ.BlockTriangular b ↔ M.BlockTriangular (ofDual ∘ b)

decls.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_zero
decls.sig: theorem blockTriangular_zero : BlockTriangular (0 : Matrix m m R) b

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.neg

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.add
decls.sig: theorem BlockTriangular.add [AddZeroClass R] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (hN : BlockTriangular N b) : BlockTriangular (M + N) b

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.sub
decls.sig: theorem BlockTriangular.sub [SubNegZeroMonoid R] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (hN : BlockTriangular N b) : BlockTriangular (M - N) b

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.add_iff_right
decls.sig: lemma BlockTriangular.add_iff_right [AddGroup R] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) : BlockTriangular (M + N) b ↔ BlockTriangular N b

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.add_iff_left
decls.sig: lemma BlockTriangular.add_iff_left [AddGroup R] (hN : BlockTriangular N b) : BlockTriangular (M + N) b ↔ BlockTriangular M b

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.sub_iff_right
decls.sig: lemma BlockTriangular.sub_iff_right [AddGroup R] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) : BlockTriangular (M - N) b ↔ BlockTriangular N b

decls.sig: lemma BlockTriangular.sub_iff_left [AddGroup R] (hN : BlockTriangular N b) : BlockTriangular (M - N) b ↔ BlockTriangular M b

decls.sig: lemma BlockTriangular.comp [Zero R] {M : Matrix m m (Matrix n n R)} (h : BlockTriangular M b) : BlockTriangular (M.comp m m n n R) fun i ↦ b i.1

decls.sig: theorem blockTriangular_one [One R] : BlockTriangular (1 : Matrix m m R) b

decls.sig: theorem blockTriangular_algebraMap [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] (r : R) : (algebraMap R (Matrix m m A) r).BlockTriangular b

decls.doc: `BlockTriangular` matrices form a subalgebra.

decls.sig: theorem mem_blockTriangularSubalgebra [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] {M : Matrix m m A} : M ∈ blockTriangularSubalgebra R A b ↔ BlockTriangular M b

decls.name: Matrix.isIndecomposable_iff_blockTriangular_const
decls.sig: lemma isIndecomposable_iff_blockTriangular_const [Nontrivial α] [Finite m] [Zero R] (M : Matrix m m R) : M.IsIndecomposable ↔ ∀ b : m → α, M.BlockTriangular b → ∃ a, b = const m a

decls.name: Matrix.upper_two_blockTriangular
decls.sig: theorem upper_two_blockTriangular [Zero R] [Preorder α] (A : Matrix m m R) (B : Matrix m n R) (D : Matrix n n R) {a b : α} (hab : a < b) : BlockTriangular (fromBlocks A B 0 D) (Sum.elim (fun _ => a) fun _ => b)

decls.name: Matrix.equiv_block_det
decls.sig: theorem equiv_block_det (M : Matrix m m R) {p q : m → Prop} [DecidablePred p] [DecidablePred q] (e : ∀ x, q x ↔ p x) : (toSquareBlockProp M p).det = (toSquareBlockProp M q).det

decls.name: Matrix.det_toSquareBlock_id
decls.sig: theorem det_toSquareBlock_id (M : Matrix m m R) (i : m) : (M.toSquareBlock id i).det = M i i

decls.name: Matrix.det_toBlock
decls.sig: theorem det_toBlock (M : Matrix m m R) (p : m → Prop) [DecidablePred p] : M.det = (fromBlocks (toBlock M p p) (toBlock M p fun j => ¬p j) (toBlock M (fun j => ¬p j) p) <| toBlock M (fun j => ¬p j) fun j => ¬p j).det

decls.name: Matrix.twoBlockTriangular_det
decls.sig: theorem twoBlockTriangular_det (M : Matrix m m R) (p : m → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : ∀ i, ¬p i → ∀ j, p j → M i j = 0) : M.det = (toSquareBlockProp M p).det * (toSquareBlockProp M fun i => ¬p i).det

decls.name: Matrix.twoBlockTriangular_det'
decls.sig: theorem twoBlockTriangular_det' (M : Matrix m m R) (p : m → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : ∀ i, p i → ∀ j, ¬p j → M i j = 0) : M.det = (toSquareBlockProp M p).det * (toSquareBlockProp M fun i => ¬p i).det

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.det
decls.sig: protected theorem BlockTriangular.det [DecidableEq α] [LinearOrder α] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) : M.det = ∏ a ∈ univ.image b, (M.toSquareBlock b a).det

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.det_fintype
decls.sig: theorem BlockTriangular.det_fintype [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] [LinearOrder α] (h : BlockTriangular M b) : M.det = ∏ k : α, (M.toSquareBlock b k).det

decls.name: Matrix.det_of_isUpperTriangular
decls.sig: theorem det_of_isUpperTriangular [LinearOrder m] (h : M.IsUpperTriangular) : M.det = ∏ i : m, M i i

decls.name: Matrix.det_of_isLowerTriangular
decls.sig: theorem det_of_isLowerTriangular [LinearOrder m] (M : Matrix m m R) (h : M.IsLowerTriangular) : M.det = ∏ i : m, M i i

decls.name: Matrix.IsUpperTriangular.det_ne_zero_iff
decls.sig: theorem IsUpperTriangular.det_ne_zero_iff [LinearOrder m] [IsDomain R] (hM : M.IsUpperTriangular) : M.det ≠ 0 ↔ ∀ i, M.diag i ≠ 0

decls.name: Matrix.IsLowerTriangular.det_ne_zero_iff
decls.sig: theorem IsLowerTriangular.det_ne_zero_iff [LinearOrder m] [IsDomain R] (hM : M.IsLowerTriangular) : M.det ≠ 0 ↔ ∀ i, M.diag i ≠ 0

decls.sig: theorem matrixOfPolynomials_isUpperTriangular {R} [Semiring R] {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → R[X]) (h_deg : ∀ i, (p i).natDegree ≤ i) : (Matrix.of (fun (i j : Fin n) => (p j).coeff i)).IsUpperTriangular

decls.name: Matrix.det_matrixOfPolynomials
decls.sig: theorem det_matrixOfPolynomials {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → R[X]) (h_deg : ∀ i, (p i).natDegree = i) (h_monic : ∀ i, Monic <| p i) : (Matrix.of (fun (i j : Fin n) => (p j).coeff i)).det = 1

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.toBlock_inverse_mul_toBlock_eq_one
decls.sig: theorem BlockTriangular.toBlock_inverse_mul_toBlock_eq_one [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : ((M⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k) * M.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k) = 1

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.inv_toBlock
decls.sig: theorem BlockTriangular.inv_toBlock [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : (M.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k)⁻¹ = M⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k
decls.doc: The inverse of an upper-left subblock of a block-triangular matrix `M` is the upper-left subblock of `M⁻¹`.

decls.name: Matrix.BlockTriangular.invertibleToBlock
decls.sig: def BlockTriangular.invertibleToBlock [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : Invertible (M.toBlock (fun i => b i < k) fun i => b i < k)
decls.doc: An upper-left subblock of an invertible block-triangular matrix is invertible.

decls.name: Matrix.toBlock_inverse_eq_zero
decls.sig: theorem toBlock_inverse_eq_zero [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) (k : α) : (M⁻¹.toBlock (fun i => k ≤ b i) fun i => b i < k) = 0
decls.doc: A lower-left subblock of the inverse of a block-triangular matrix is zero. This is a first step towards `BlockTriangular.inv_toBlock` below.

decls.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_inv_of_blockTriangular
decls.sig: theorem blockTriangular_inv_of_blockTriangular [LinearOrder α] [Invertible M] (hM : BlockTriangular M b) : BlockTriangular M⁻¹ b
decls.doc: The inverse of a block-triangular matrix is block-triangular.

decls.name: Matrix.circulant
decls.sig: def circulant [Sub n] (v : n → α) : Matrix n n α
decls.doc: Given the condition `[Sub n]` and a vector `v : n → α`, we define `circulant v` to be the circulant matrix generated by `v` of type `Matrix n n α`. The `(i,j)`th entry is defined to be `v (i - j)`.

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_apply
decls.sig: theorem circulant_apply [Sub n] (v : n → α) (i j) : circulant v i j = v (i - j)

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_col_zero_eq
decls.sig: theorem circulant_col_zero_eq [SubtractionMonoid n] (v : n → α) (i : n) : circulant v i 0 = v i

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_injective
decls.sig: theorem circulant_injective [SubtractionMonoid n] : Injective (circulant : (n → α) → Matrix n n α)

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.circulant_injective
decls.sig: theorem Fin.circulant_injective : ∀ n, Injective fun v : Fin n → α => circulant v | 0 => by simp [Injective] | _ + 1 => Matrix.circulant_injective

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_inj
decls.sig: theorem circulant_inj [SubtractionMonoid n] {v w : n → α} : circulant v = circulant w ↔ v = w

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.circulant_inj
decls.sig: theorem Fin.circulant_inj {n} {v w : Fin n → α} : circulant v = circulant w ↔ v = w

decls.name: Matrix.transpose_circulant
decls.sig: theorem transpose_circulant [SubtractionMonoid n] (v : n → α) : (circulant v)ᵀ = circulant fun i => v (-i)

decls.name: Matrix.conjTranspose_circulant
decls.sig: theorem conjTranspose_circulant [Star α] [SubtractionMonoid n] (v : n → α) : (circulant v)ᴴ = circulant (star fun i => v (-i))

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.transpose_circulant
decls.sig: theorem Fin.transpose_circulant : ∀ {n} (v : Fin n → α), (circulant v)ᵀ = circulant fun i => v (-i) | 0 => by simp [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton] | _ + 1 => Matrix.transpose_circulant

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.conjTranspose_circulant
decls.sig: theorem Fin.conjTranspose_circulant [Star α] : ∀ {n} (v : Fin n → α), (circulant v)ᴴ = circulant (star fun i => v (-i)) | 0 => by simp [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton] | _ + 1 => Matrix.conjTranspose_circulant

decls.name: Matrix.map_circulant
decls.sig: theorem map_circulant [Sub n] (v : n → α) (f : α → β) : (circulant v).map f = circulant fun i => f (v i)

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_neg
decls.sig: theorem circulant_neg [Neg α] [Sub n] (v : n → α) : circulant (-v) = -circulant v

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_zero
decls.sig: theorem circulant_zero (α n) [Zero α] [Sub n] : circulant 0 = (0 : Matrix n n α)

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_add
decls.sig: theorem circulant_add [Add α] [Sub n] (v w : n → α) : circulant (v + w) = circulant v + circulant w

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_sub
decls.sig: theorem circulant_sub [Sub α] [Sub n] (v w : n → α) : circulant (v - w) = circulant v - circulant w

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_mul
decls.sig: theorem circulant_mul [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring α] [Fintype n] [AddGroup n] (v w : n → α) : circulant v * circulant w = circulant (circulant v *ᵥ w)
decls.doc: The product of two circulant matrices `circulant v` and `circulant w` is the circulant matrix generated by `circulant v *ᵥ w`.

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.circulant_mul
decls.sig: theorem Fin.circulant_mul [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring α] : ∀ {n} (v w : Fin n → α), circulant v * circulant w = circulant (circulant v *ᵥ w) | 0 => by simp [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton] | _ + 1 => Matrix.circulant_mul

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_mul_comm
decls.sig: theorem circulant_mul_comm [CommMagma α] [AddCommMonoid α] [Fintype n] [AddCommGroup n] (v w : n → α) : circulant v * circulant w = circulant w * circulant v
decls.doc: Multiplication of circulant matrices commutes when the elements do.

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.circulant_mul_comm
decls.sig: theorem Fin.circulant_mul_comm [CommMagma α] [AddCommMonoid α] : ∀ {n} (v w : Fin n → α), circulant v * circulant w = circulant w * circulant v | 0 => by simp | _ + 1 => Matrix.circulant_mul_comm

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_smul
decls.sig: theorem circulant_smul [Sub n] [SMul R α] (k : R) (v : n → α) : circulant (k • v) = k • circulant v
decls.doc: `k • circulant v` is another circulant matrix `circulant (k • v)`.

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_single_one
decls.sig: theorem circulant_single_one (α n) [Zero α] [One α] [DecidableEq n] [AddGroup n] : circulant (Pi.single 0 1 : n → α) = (1 : Matrix n n α)

decls.name: Matrix.circulant_single
decls.sig: theorem circulant_single (n) [Semiring α] [DecidableEq n] [AddGroup n] [Fintype n] (a : α) : circulant (Pi.single 0 a : n → α) = scalar n a

decls.name: Matrix.Fin.circulant_ite
decls.sig: theorem Fin.circulant_ite (α) [Zero α] [One α] : ∀ n, circulant (fun i => ite (i.1 = 0) 1 0 : Fin n → α) = 1 | 0 => by simp [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton] | n + 1 => by rw [← circulant_single_one] congr with j simp [Pi.single_apply]

decls.name: Matrix.permanent
decls.sig: def permanent (M : Matrix n n R) : R
decls.doc: The permanent of a square matrix defined as a sum over all permutations. This is analogous to the determinant but without alternating signs.

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_diagonal
decls.sig: theorem permanent_diagonal {d : n → R} : permanent (diagonal d) = ∏ i, d i

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_zero
decls.sig: theorem permanent_zero [Nonempty n] : permanent (0 : Matrix n n R) = 0

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_one
decls.sig: theorem permanent_one : permanent (1 : Matrix n n R) = 1

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_isEmpty
decls.sig: theorem permanent_isEmpty [IsEmpty n] {A : Matrix n n R} : permanent A = 1

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_eq_one_of_card_eq_zero
decls.sig: theorem permanent_eq_one_of_card_eq_zero {A : Matrix n n R} (h : card n = 0) : permanent A = 1

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_unique
decls.sig: theorem permanent_unique {n : Type*} [Unique n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n R) : permanent A = A default default
decls.doc: If `n` has only one element, the permanent of an `n` by `n` matrix is just that element. Although `Unique` implies `DecidableEq` and `Fintype`, the instances might not be syntactically equal. Thus, we need to fill in the args explicitly.

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_eq_elem_of_subsingleton
decls.sig: theorem permanent_eq_elem_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton n] (A : Matrix n n R) (k : n) : permanent A = A k k

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_eq_elem_of_card_eq_one
decls.sig: theorem permanent_eq_elem_of_card_eq_one {A : Matrix n n R} (h : card n = 1) (k : n) : permanent A = A k k

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_transpose
decls.sig: theorem permanent_transpose (M : Matrix n n R) : Mᵀ.permanent = M.permanent
decls.doc: Transposing a matrix preserves the permanent.

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_permute_cols
decls.sig: theorem permanent_permute_cols (σ : Perm n) (M : Matrix n n R) : (M.submatrix σ id).permanent = M.permanent
decls.doc: Permuting the columns does not change the permanent.

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_permute_rows
decls.sig: theorem permanent_permute_rows (σ : Perm n) (M : Matrix n n R) : (M.submatrix id σ).permanent = M.permanent
decls.doc: Permuting the rows does not change the permanent.

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_smul
decls.sig: theorem permanent_smul (M : Matrix n n R) (c : R) : permanent (c • M) = c ^ Fintype.card n * permanent M

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_updateCol_smul
decls.sig: theorem permanent_updateCol_smul (M : Matrix n n R) (j : n) (c : R) (u : n → R) : permanent (updateCol M j <| c • u) = c * permanent (updateCol M j u)

decls.name: Matrix.permanent_updateRow_smul
decls.sig: theorem permanent_updateRow_smul (M : Matrix n n R) (j : n) (c : R) (u : n → R) : permanent (updateRow M j <| c • u) = c * permanent (updateRow M j u)

decls.name: Equiv.Perm.permMatrix

decls.sig: theorem det_permutation [CommRing R] : det (σ.permMatrix R) = Perm.sign σ
decls.doc: The determinant of a permutation matrix equals its sign.

decls.sig: theorem trace_permutation [AddCommMonoidWithOne R] : trace (σ.permMatrix R) = (Function.fixedPoints σ).ncard
decls.doc: The trace of a permutation matrix equals the number of fixed points.

decls.name: Matrix.permMatrix_mulVec
decls.sig: lemma permMatrix_mulVec {v : n → R} [CommRing R] : σ.permMatrix R *ᵥ v = v ∘ σ

decls.sig: lemma vecMul_permMatrix {v : n → R} [CommRing R] : v ᵥ* σ.permMatrix R = v ∘ σ.symm

decls.name: Matrix.permMatrix_mul
decls.sig: lemma permMatrix_mul [NonAssocSemiring R] : (σ * τ).permMatrix R = τ.permMatrix R * σ.permMatrix R

decls.doc: The l2-operator norm of a permutation matrix is bounded above by 1. See `Matrix.permMatrix_l2_opNorm_eq` for the equality statement assuming the matrix is nonempty.

decls.name: Matrix.permMatrix_l2_opNorm_eq
decls.sig: theorem permMatrix_l2_opNorm_eq [Nonempty n] : ‖σ.permMatrix 𝕜‖ = 1
decls.doc: The l2-operator norm of a nonempty permutation matrix is equal to 1. Note that this is not true for the empty case, since the empty matrix has l2-operator norm 0. See `Matrix.permMatrix_l2_opNorm_le` for the inequality version of the empty case.
